In the POLO trial, maintenance olaparib, a drug that exploits faulty DNA repair, for inherited BRCA mutations doubled progression-free survival (7.4 against 3.8 months; hazard ratio 0.53), but overall survival was 19.0 against 19.2 months with a hazard ratio of 0.83 that was not significant, partly because placebo patients later received other active drugs [[TX-005]][[TX-L24]]. In the borderline-resectable trial of FOLFIRINOX (a four-drug chemotherapy regimen) before surgery, two-year survival was 72% among patients who were resected and 56% among everyone enrolled; the first number describes people selected by having done well enough to reach surgery [[TX-011]]. Against this background, the RASolute 302 trial is the kind of result that changes practice: 500 previously treated patients randomized to daraxonrasib (a RAS inhibitor) or chemotherapy, median overall survival 13.2 against 6.7 months with a hazard ratio of 0.40, progression-free survival 7.2 against 3.6 months, and response 30% against 11%, all moving together [[RAS-033]], which led to US approval on 26 August 2026 [[SEC-RAS-01]].

research_notes.what_findings_mean: The response-without-survival pattern recurs across unrelated mechanisms, which is the strongest argument that it is a property of the disease rather than of any one drug: survival in metastatic pancreatic cancer is governed by disease outside the measured lesions and by host factors such as nutrition and performance status [[TME-004]][[TME-027]]. The olaparib dissociation has a competing explanation, that the drug delays radiologic progression of indolent disease without changing the lethal clone, while a three-year survival difference of 34% against 18% hints at a long-tail effect in a trial underpowered for survival [[TX-L24]]. The daraxonrasib trial is available to this atlas only as an abstract, so trial conduct, subgroups and crossover handling cannot be assessed here, and its dual primary endpoints were defined in the RAS G12-mutant 92% of patients while the US indication carries no mutation requirement [[RAS-033]].
research_notes.how_studied: Endpoint behavior is studied inside the trials themselves. Response is scored against RECIST, which sums the diameters of chosen target lesions and calls a partial response at 30% shrinkage. Progression-free and overall survival are estimated by the Kaplan-Meier method, which handles patients still alive at analysis, and compared with a Cox model that yields the hazard ratio. Trials prespecify whether the primary analysis is intention-to-treat and whether review is by investigators or a blinded central panel, and discrepancies between those readings are themselves reported [[TX-006]]. Resected-cohort and intention-to-treat survival are both published so that readers can see the selection gap [[TX-011]][[TX-012]]. Crossover-adjusted survival methods exist for trials where control patients later received the study drug [[TX-L24]].

mechanism_notes.text: Hyaluronidase and hydroxychloroquine each raised the response rate without improving survival. The proposed reason is that both improve control of the index lesions, by delivering more drug or by making cells less able to survive stress, while survival in metastatic disease is governed by micrometastatic burden and by host factors, and the added toxicity reduced the chemotherapy dose actually delivered [[INF-TME-02]][[TME-004]][[TME-027]]. A simpler competing explanation is that both trials were powered for larger effects than exist.

The POLO investigators proposed that crossover to later active therapy and platinum re-sensitivity in the placebo arm, together with a trial underpowered for survival, masked a true overall-survival effect that shows only as a three-year tail among durable responders [[INF-TX-02]][[TX-L24]][[TX-005]]. The competing view is that olaparib delays radiologic progression of indolent disease without altering the kinetics of the lethal clone.

glossary.definition: The middle value of a group: the time by which half of the patients have reached the event and half have not.
The ratio of event rates between two groups over the whole follow-up; 0.70 means a 30% lower rate in the treated group.
The time from treatment start until the cancer grows on scans or the patient dies, whichever comes first.
The time from treatment start or randomization until death from any cause.
The proportion of patients whose measured tumors shrink by a set amount on scans.
Analyzing every patient in the group they were assigned to, whether or not they completed the planned treatment.

related.statement: Trial endpoints such as median survival and hazard ratios describe groups, and survival statistics explain why they do not forecast individuals.
The endpoints described here are what phase 2 and phase 3 clinical trials are built to measure.
Maintenance olaparib is the clearest pancreatic cancer example of progression-free survival improving without a significant overall survival gain.
Daraxonrasib's phase 3 trial improved response, progression-free survival and overall survival together, which is why it changed practice.
The hyaluronidase trial raised response rate without changing survival, a lesson about what response measures.
Reading endpoints correctly is the first step in judging whether a headline result counts as progress.

faq.q: The trial reported a hazard ratio of 0.7. Does that mean a 30% better chance of survival for me?
faq.a: No. A hazard ratio of 0.7 means the rate of death in the treated group was 30% lower, averaged over the trial's follow-up, in a group defined by the trial's eligibility rules. It is a comparison of groups, and in the erlotinib trial a hazard ratio of 0.82 corresponded to a median gain of about ten days [[RAS-037]].

faq.q: Why would a drug shrink tumors but not help people live longer?
faq.a: Because response measures the chosen index lesions, while survival in metastatic pancreatic cancer is set by disease elsewhere and by how well the body tolerates treatment. Hyaluronidase raised the response rate by 11 points with a hazard ratio for death of exactly 1.00, and hydroxychloroquine raised it by 17 points while survival was numerically worse [[TME-004]][[TME-027]].

topics.title: Clinical trials: phases, registries and what counts as progress
topics.orientation: Clinical trials are how a treatment moves from an idea to an approved drug. The phase tells you what question a trial was built to answer, a registry entry tells you a trial exists, and only a completed, published result tells you whether the treatment works.

section1.label: What this means
section1.preview: Phase 1 trials find a safe dose in a few dozen patients and measure side effects; any tumor shrinkage is a bonus. Phase 2 trials test whether the drug has activity, often in a single arm compared with a historical benchmark. Phase 3 trials randomize hundreds of patients between the new treatment and the standard, with survival as the usual endpoint. Trials are registered on ClinicalTrials.gov with an NCT number before they start.
section1.full: A registry record states a trial's design, enrollment, status and sometimes results; status words such as 'recruiting', 'active, not recruiting' or 'completed' describe where enrollment stands, not whether the treatment worked. Many peer-reviewed trials never post results to the registry at all [[SEC-TX-14]], and a pivotal trial can be approved by the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) while the registry still shows no results [[SEC-RAS-05]]. Regulatory approval comes in grades. Regular approval rests on a randomized trial showing a survival or progression benefit. Accelerated approval rests on a surrogate endpoint (a stand-in measure) such as response rate and duration from a single-arm study, with confirmation expected later; zenocutuzumab for pancreatic cancer carrying an NRG1 gene fusion (a rare gene rearrangement) was approved this way in December 2024 on a 42% response rate in 36 patients [[TX-020]][[SEC-TX-08]]. Tissue-agnostic approval covers any tumor with a given molecular feature, such as pembrolizumab, an immunotherapy, for mismatch-repair deficiency (a faulty DNA-repair system that leaves tumors heavily mutated), even though the pancreatic subset responded less often than other cancers (18% against 53% across tumor types) [[TX-007]][[TX-016]]. Off-label use means prescribing an approved drug outside its labeled indication, which is legal and common; the four-drug FOLFIRINOX chemotherapy regimen is guideline-recommended but not labeled as such [[SEC-TX-09]]. A trial's phase, its registry status and its approval status are three different facts.

section2.label: In pancreatic cancer
section2.preview: Pancreatic cancer has an unusually long record of promising early results that did not survive randomization, which makes phase and design the first things to check. Every immunotherapy that looked encouraging in a single-arm study and was then tested against a control arm failed to improve survival. The 2026 approval of daraxonrasib shows the opposite path: a phase 1/2 signal confirmed by a 500-patient randomized phase 3.
section2.full: The GVAX and CRS-207 cancer-vaccine program illustrates the pattern. A promising subgroup result in a phase 2a trial led to a randomized phase 2b in 303 patients, where the vaccine arm had a median survival of 3.7 months against 4.6 months with chemotherapy, a hazard ratio of 1.17 in the wrong direction [[IMM-005]]. The same shrinkage toward no effect is seen across checkpoint, chemokine and CD40 agents, other classes of immunotherapy [[IMM-010]][[IMM-012]]. Within single arms, patients who mount an immune response to a vaccine live longer than those who do not, but that correlation has never been converted into a survival benefit in a randomized trial, and in several studies the responder threshold was chosen from the same patients whose survival it then split [[IMM-001]][[IMM-003]]. The personalized mRNA vaccine that generated T cells in half of 16 patients is now in a randomized phase 2 with no results posted [[SEC-IMMUNE-01]]. By contrast, daraxonrasib moved from a phase 1/2 study with a 35% response rate in previously treated patients whose tumors carried a RAS G12 mutation [[RAS-032]] to the RASolute 302 phase 3, where median survival was 13.2 against 6.7 months with chemotherapy (hazard ratio 0.40) [[RAS-033]], and to US approval on 26 August 2026 [[SEC-RAS-01]]. Its first-line and adjuvant trials, RASolute 303 and 304, were recruiting with no results as of 8 October 2026 [[SEC-RAS-06]][[SEC-RAS-07]].

research_notes.what_findings_mean: The repeated collapse of early immunotherapy signals is best read as a property of small, selected or interim datasets rather than of any one mechanism: the CXCR4-plus-pembrolizumab cohort, for example, was published with an interim response rate that fell to 18.6% at full accrual [[IMM-010]]. A pre-treatment immune profile predicted survival just as strongly in control arms as in vaccine arms, so immune 'responders' may simply be patients who were already more robust [[IMM-022]]. The daraxonrasib approval is the first time a RAS-pathway drug has produced a large randomized survival benefit in this disease after decades of negative trials of farnesyltransferase, MEK and SOS1 inhibitors [[RAS-036]][[RAS-005]][[RAS-018]], but it is available to this atlas only as an abstract, and the US indication is broader than the trial's primary population [[RAS-033]].
research_notes.how_studied: Phase 1 trials escalate dose in small cohorts and define dose-limiting toxicities; phase 2 trials use a single arm with a prespecified activity threshold or a randomized 'pick-the-winner' design, neither of which can prove benefit [[TX-013]]. Phase 3 trials randomize against the current standard, prespecify primary endpoints and analysis populations, and are monitored by independent committees that can stop them for futility, as happened to the MEK-plus-AKT trial when its interim boundary was crossed [[RAS-005]]. A registry record on ClinicalTrials.gov gives a trial's status, enrollment and any posted results, and is a separate document from its publication [[SEC-RAS-05]]. A drug's regulatory status is defined by FDA approval documents and the current prescribing label, not by press reports [[SEC-RAS-01]][[SEC-RAS-02]].

mechanism_notes.text: Across four vaccine platforms over 14 years, patients who mounted an immune response lived markedly longer than those who did not, yet no randomized trial reproduced the effect at the arm level. The likeliest explanation is reverse causation: occult residual tumor burden both suppresses the immune response and causes early recurrence, so 'immune responder' marks how little disease a patient had rather than what the vaccine did [[INF-IMMUNE-02]][[IMM-022]][[IMM-013]]. The competing view, that the vaccines work only in patients able to respond, would require a randomized trial restricted to responders to test.

glossary.definition: An early trial that finds a safe dose and records side effects in a small number of patients.
A trial that tests whether a treatment shows activity, usually without a randomized comparison.
A large randomized trial comparing a new treatment with the current standard, usually with survival as the endpoint.
The identifier a trial receives when registered on ClinicalTrials.gov, such as NCT06625320.
US approval granted on a surrogate endpoint such as response rate, with a confirmatory trial expected afterwards.
An approval that applies to any cancer carrying a specified molecular feature, regardless of the organ it started in.
Prescribing an approved drug for a use not listed on its label, which is legal and often guideline-supported.

related.statement: Daraxonrasib is the clearest pancreatic cancer example of a phase 1/2 signal confirmed by a randomized phase 3 and converted into approval.
The RASolute 302, 303 and 304 trials show the phase 3 program that follows an approved drug into new settings.
The personalized mRNA vaccine is a phase 1 result awaiting its randomized phase 2 readout.
Immune combination trials in pancreatic cancer illustrate early signals that shrank toward no effect under randomization.
Judging a trial requires reading its endpoints as well as its phase.
What counts as progress depends on whether a result has survived a randomized comparison.
Pembrolizumab's tissue-agnostic approval shows how a drug can be labeled for pancreatic cancer on evidence mostly from other tumors.

faq.q: A trial is listed as 'recruiting'. Does that mean the drug works?
faq.a: No. Recruiting means the trial is enrolling patients; it says nothing about results. The adjuvant daraxonrasib trial RASolute 304, for example, was recruiting 500 patients with no results as of 8 October 2026, so whether the drug helps after surgery is unknown [[SEC-RAS-07]].

faq.q: What does accelerated approval mean for me?
faq.a: It means the drug was approved on a surrogate such as response rate from a single-arm study, with a confirmatory trial expected later. Zenocutuzumab for NRG1-fusion pancreatic cancer was approved this way on a 42% response rate in 36 patients, so its survival benefit has not yet been measured against a control group [[TX-020]][[SEC-TX-08]].

faq.q: Should I consider joining a trial?
faq.a: Trials are how patients gain access to drugs before approval and how the field learns; the daraxonrasib approval came from patients who enrolled in RASolute 302. Phase matters: a phase 3 trial offers a randomized comparison with standard care, while a phase 1 trial is primarily a safety study [[RAS-033]][[SEC-RAS-05]].

topics.title: Survival statistics and the individual
topics.orientation: Survival statistics describe groups. They are indispensable for comparing treatments and unreliable as a forecast for one person, because the groups they describe are defined by when, where and how the patients were treated and selected. This entry explains what the common figures mean and why they differ so much.

section1.label: What this means
section1.preview: A median survival is the time by which half of a group has died and half is still alive; it says nothing about the shape of the other half. A five-year rate is the proportion alive at that point. A hazard ratio compares two groups' rates of dying over the whole follow-up. All three are properties of a defined group, and the group's definition, by stage, treatment, fitness and era, matters more than the number.
section1.full: The median is used because survival data are unfinished: when a trial reports, many patients are still alive, and the median is the first summary point that can be calculated without waiting for everyone. It carries no information about spread. Two groups with the same median can differ greatly in how many people are alive at three or five years, which is why trials report both: in the POLO trial of maintenance olaparib for inherited BRCA mutations the medians were 19.0 and 19.2 months while three-year survival was 34% against 18% [[TX-L24]]. A five-year rate is a snapshot and depends on who was counted at the start; among resected patients it ranged from 39% for the smallest node-negative tumors (stage IA) to 11% for stage III, which in resected patients mostly means four or more positive nodes [[DIAG-017]]. A hazard ratio of 0.68 means the rate of death in the treated group was 32% lower at any given moment, averaged over follow-up; it is not a 32% chance of anything for an individual [[TX-003]]. Every one of these numbers is conditional on a population defined by eligibility, and most trials enroll fitter, younger patients than a clinic sees [[TX-003]].

section2.label: In pancreatic cancer
section2.preview: Pancreatic cancer figures vary more by population than by treatment. A number from patients who reached surgery after chemotherapy, from a trial of fit patients under 80, from a national registry including everyone, or from a decade-old series will differ by years, and each is correct for its own group. The right use of a statistic is to ask which group it describes and how closely that group resembles the person asking.
section2.full: Compare figures that all describe 'resected pancreatic cancer'. In a randomized adjuvant trial of patients under 80 with good recovery and CA 19-9 (carbohydrate antigen 19-9) below 180 U/mL, median survival was 53.5 months with modified FOLFIRINOX (a four-drug chemotherapy regimen) and 35.5 with gemcitabine [[TX-003]]. In a 1,525-patient international cohort of resected patients across all adjuvant eras, median survival was 24.4 months [[DIAG-017]]. In a Canadian population registry that included every resected case, median survival after pancreatectomy was 25.9 months, and 33.1 months among those who had a preoperative MRI (magnetic resonance imaging), a difference that reflects who was selected for surgery as much as the scan itself [[DIAG-021]]. Among patients resected after total neoadjuvant therapy at a single center, median survival was 58.8 months, because that group had already survived and responded to months of treatment [[TX-L25]]. None of these contradicts the others. Stage-specific numbers add another layer: five-year survival by nodal status ran from 35.6% to 10.9% within the same cohort [[DIAG-017]]. Treatment-specific numbers shift with each new regimen, and the figures a search engine returns are often from before those regimens existed. A care team can say which of these groups a person most resembles and which features, such as CA 19-9 trend or response to treatment, are moving them within it.

research_notes.what_findings_mean: Three selection effects explain most of the variation between quoted figures. Trial eligibility: the adjuvant FOLFIRINOX result is not generalizable to frail or elderly patients, and most participants received reduced dose intensity [[TX-003]]. Conditioning on reaching surgery: survival among resected patients after neoadjuvant therapy overstates what a newly diagnosed patient should expect, because early progressors and non-tolerators never reach the operating room [[TX-011]][[TX-012]][[TX-L25]]. Era and setting: registry and cohort medians blend decades of changing regimens and hospital volumes, and operative mortality alone varies several-fold by hospital volume [[SURG-003]]. Staging itself explains only a minority of survival variation, with a concordance statistic near 0.57 [[DIAG-017]]. The residual variation is individual, and it is what population statistics cannot see.
research_notes.how_studied: Survival is estimated with the Kaplan-Meier method, which uses every patient's follow-up up to the point they were last seen, so that people still alive contribute information without being counted as deaths. Medians and fixed-time rates are read off that curve with confidence intervals that widen as fewer patients remain. Hazard ratios come from Cox regression, which can adjust for stage, age and other factors and so compares like with like [[DIAG-021]]. Concordance statistics measure how well a staging system ranks patients by survival [[DIAG-017]]. Registry studies capture whole populations but lack treatment detail; trials capture treatment precisely but in selected people [[TX-003]]. Reading both together is how a group estimate is narrowed toward an individual.

glossary.definition: The time by which half of a defined group of patients has died and half is still alive.
The proportion of a defined group still alive five years after diagnosis or treatment.
The ratio of death rates between two groups over the whole follow-up; 0.68 means a 32% lower rate in the treated group.
A graph of the proportion of a group surviving over time that accounts for patients still alive at the time of analysis.
The way a group's definition, such as trial eligibility or reaching surgery, shapes its survival figures independently of treatment.

related.statement: The medians and hazard ratios in survival statistics are the same quantities that trial results report.
Stage-specific survival figures depend on nodal status, which is why stage and resectability must be read separately.
Survival figures from patients resected after neoadjuvant therapy describe a selected group and overstate what everyone who starts can expect.
Trial survival figures apply to the fit, selected patients who met the trial's eligibility rules.
A CA 19-9 trend is one of the individual features that moves a person within the group a survival statistic describes.

faq.q: What are my chances?
faq.a: No published figure answers that for one person. Survival statistics describe groups defined by stage, treatment, fitness and era, and the same label, 'resected pancreatic cancer', yields medians from about 24 months in a mixed cohort to 53.5 months in a trial of fit patients on modified FOLFIRINOX [[DIAG-017]][[TX-003]]. Your care team can say which group you most resemble and which of your own features are moving you within it.

faq.q: Why do the numbers I find online differ so much from what my oncologist says?
faq.a: Online figures are often all-stage registry averages from before current regimens existed, while an oncologist is describing a group matched to your stage, resectability, fitness and treatment. Among resected patients alone, five-year survival ranges from 39% to 11% depending on stage [[DIAG-017]].

topics.title: Jaundice and itching
topics.orientation: Jaundice is the yellowing of skin and eyes that happens when bile backs up into the blood. In pancreatic cancer it almost always means a tumor in the head of the pancreas is squeezing the bile duct that passes through it on its way to the intestine.

section1.label: What this experience involves
section1.preview: Jaundice shows as yellow eyes and skin, dark tea-colored urine, pale clay-colored stools and, in many people, a deep itch that is worst at night and on the palms and soles. All four signs share one cause: bile made by the liver can no longer reach the intestine, so bilirubin, its yellow pigment, and bile salts spill over into the bloodstream. Ordinary antihistamines usually do little for the itch, because histamine is not what drives it.
section1.full: The liver makes bile continuously and sends it down the common bile duct, which runs through the head of the pancreas before opening into the duodenum at the ampulla. When that duct is pinched shut, bilirubin that the liver has already processed into a water-soluble form builds up in blood and is filtered by the kidneys, which is why urine darkens first; stool turns pale because no pigment reaches it, and fat digestion falters because bile salts are missing. The itch has its own chemistry: in people with cholestatic itch (itch from blocked bile flow), the enzyme autotaxin and its product lysophosphatidic acid tracked itch intensity while histamine and bile salts did not, and both the itch and the enzyme fell once bile was drained [[ANAT-043]]. Among symptoms recorded in primary care, jaundice is the one that most specifically points to pancreatic cancer: it was noted in 30.5% of people later diagnosed versus 0.1% of controls, giving a positive predictive value of about 22% in people over 60, meaning roughly one in five people over 60 with recorded jaundice turned out to have the cancer [[ANAT-010]]. It also appears late, a median of about one month before diagnosis, whereas back pain had been present for a median of 16 months [[ANAT-022]]. A typical sequence is a week of darker urine and itching, then a partner noticing yellow in the whites of the eyes.

section2.label: Connection to pancreatic cancer
section2.preview: The bile duct runs through the head of the pancreas, so a head tumor of modest size can obstruct it, while tumors in the body or tail rarely cause jaundice and tend to be found later and larger. Relief comes from reopening the duct, usually with a stent placed through an endoscope, or from the operation that removes the head. Draining the duct also makes the tumor marker CA 19-9 interpretable, since obstruction inflates it.
section2.full: On imaging, a head tumor often dilates both the bile duct and the pancreatic duct at once, the so-called double-duct sign; that finding was malignant in about half of 103 patients overall, but in the 20 whose sign was incidental with normal bilirubin, liver enzymes and CA 19-9, no head cancer emerged over a median 7.3 years of follow-up [[ANAT-020]]. Head tumors are also less often metastatic at diagnosis than body or tail tumors (42% versus 69% and 84% in a national registry), partly because jaundice forces an earlier visit [[ANAT-003]]. Whether to drain before surgery was answered differently for different stents: with plastic stents, drainage raised serious complications to 74% versus 39% with early surgery [[SUPP-L07]], but in a 2026 trial using covered metal stents, serious adverse events within 120 days were 29.0% (40 of 138) with drainage versus 26.5% (36 of 136) with early surgery, with more events while waiting (15.2% versus 5.1%) but fewer after the operation [[SUPP-008]]. During months of preoperative chemotherapy about 72% of metal stents kept draining, covered stents failing by migration and uncovered ones by tumor ingrowth [[SUPP-012]]. After drainage, CA 19-9 fell by a mean 39% in malignant obstruction, so the marker is read once bilirubin has settled [[DIAG-016]].

action_note.heading: When to call the care team now
action_note.text: Fever or shaking chills together with new or returning jaundice, dark urine or pain under the right ribs are the warning signs of cholangitis, an infection in a blocked or stented bile duct that can progress to sepsis within hours and needs urgent drainage [[SEC-SUPP-14]]. A temperature of 100.4 °F (38 °C) or higher counts as a fever for anyone on cancer treatment [[SEC-SUPP-03]]. Jaundice that returns after a stent usually means the stent has blocked and should be reported the same day [[SUPP-012]].

research_notes.what_findings_mean: The symptom studies are primary-care case-control designs, which measure how much a recorded symptom raises the probability of a later cancer diagnosis rather than how often a person with cancer has the symptom; the 22% positive predictive value for jaundice applies to people over 60 presenting to a general practitioner [[ANAT-010]]. The drainage trials differ in stent type and era: the plastic-stent trial is available to this atlas only as an abstract [[SUPP-L07]], while the 2026 metal-stent trial was open-label and its composite endpoint mixes stent and surgical events [[SUPP-008]]. The itch mechanism comes from cholestasis of several causes, not specifically pancreatic cancer [[ANAT-043]].
research_notes.how_studied: Case-control studies in general-practice databases compare symptom codes recorded before diagnosis in people with pancreatic cancer against matched controls, giving odds ratios and positive predictive values that help clinicians decide whom to scan [[ANAT-010]][[ANAT-022]]. Randomized trials of preoperative drainage assign jaundiced patients to stent-first or surgery-first and count serious adverse events over 120 days, which captures both stent complications and operative ones [[SUPP-008]]. Stent-type trials follow patients through neoadjuvant chemotherapy and record whether drainage is sustained until surgery [[SUPP-012]]. Serum autotaxin activity was measured in itchy and non-itchy cholestatic patients and before and after biliary drainage [[ANAT-043]].

mechanism_notes.text: Cholestatic itch is best explained by circulating lysophosphatidic acid generated by the enzyme autotaxin, which activates sensory neurons directly; this fits the observations that histamine, bile salts and opioids did not track itch intensity while autotaxin did, and that both fell with drainage [[ANAT-043]]. It predicts that relieving the obstruction, not antihistamines, is the effective treatment, which matches the stent and surgical experience [[SUPP-008]].

glossary.definition: The yellow pigment produced when old red blood cells are broken down, normally removed from the body in bile.
Any condition in which bile cannot flow from the liver to the intestine.
The small opening in the wall of the duodenum where the bile duct and pancreatic duct empty.
Simultaneous widening of the bile duct and pancreatic duct on a scan, usually from a blockage in the head of the pancreas.
An endoscopic procedure that reaches the bile duct through the mouth and stomach to place a stent or clear a blockage.
Bacterial infection of a blocked bile duct, causing fever, chills and jaundice.
The medical word for itching.

related.statement: A tumor in the head of the pancreas is the usual cause of jaundice because the common bile duct passes through the head.
Jaundice signals that the common bile duct is blocked before it reaches the ampulla in the duodenum.
Jaundice from a blocked bile duct is usually relieved by a metal biliary stent placed during ERCP.
The Whipple operation removes the head of the pancreas and the lower bile duct, relieving jaundice permanently when the tumor can be resected.
Fever with returning jaundice signals cholangitis, an infection of the blocked bile duct that needs urgent drainage.
Bile-duct obstruction inflates CA 19-9, so the marker is interpreted after jaundice has been drained.

faq.q: Does jaundice mean the cancer is advanced?
faq.a: No. Jaundice reports where the tumor sits, not how far it has spread. Head tumors cause jaundice early and were metastatic at diagnosis in 42% of cases in a national registry, compared with 84% of tail tumors, which cause no jaundice [[ANAT-003]].

faq.q: Why do antihistamines not help the itching?
faq.a: Cholestatic itch is driven by lysophosphatidic acid made by the enzyme autotaxin rather than by histamine; autotaxin tracked itch intensity and fell when bile was drained [[ANAT-043]]. Relieving the blockage is the treatment that works.

topics.title: Pain, including back pain
topics.orientation: Pain in pancreatic cancer comes mainly from the nerves that run through and around the gland, which is why it is often felt high in the abdomen and bores through to the mid-back. It is treatable at several levels, from medicines to nerve blocks.

section1.label: What this experience involves
section1.preview: The typical pain is a dull, constant ache high in the abdomen that radiates straight through to the back, sometimes easier when leaning forward and worse after meals or lying flat. Back pain is a frequent early symptom yet a poor clue: it preceded diagnosis by a median of 16 months because it was attributed to the spine or muscles [[ANAT-022]]. By the time people reach palliative-care services, about 7 in 10 report distress from pain [[SUPP-032]].
section1.full: The pancreas lies against the back wall of the abdomen, directly in front of the aorta and spine, and its sensory fibers travel through the celiac plexus, a dense web of nerves around the celiac artery, before entering the spinal cord at the lower chest segments; the brain maps those signals onto the upper abdomen and back. In primary-care records, back pain raised the odds of pancreatic cancer only modestly (odds ratio about 1.4) whereas jaundice raised them roughly a thousandfold, which is why back pain alone rarely prompts a scan [[ANAT-010]]. Pain does not scale neatly with stage. In 95 people with resectable tumors, pain tracked tumor size, nerve invasion, capsule invasion and nodal spread, and those without pain lived longer on average than those with severe pain, an association from an older abstract that describes groups rather than any one person [[ANAT-037]]. Pain also rarely travels alone: among people with pain distress, 79% also reported sleep distress, 83% nausea and 80% bowel distress [[SUPP-032]]. A common story is a year of 'muscular' back pain treated with physiotherapy before upper-abdominal pain, weight loss or jaundice finally lead to imaging.

section2.label: Connection to pancreatic cancer
section2.preview: Pancreatic cancer is unusually entangled with nerves. Cancer cells grow along nerve sheaths in about 80% of resected tumors [[ANAT-013]], and the tumor thickens and multiplies the nerves around it. Pain tracks the immune and glial cells gathered around those nerves more than the amount of cancer inside them, which makes pancreatic pain a neuro-immune process rather than simple pressure. Treatment therefore ranges from opioid-based medicines to blocks that silence the celiac plexus.
section2.full: Nerve remodeling begins before cancer: in mice, nerve density was already 1.7 times normal at the precursor stage, with nerve growth factor raised 2.25-fold [[ANAT-011]]. In human tumors, painful cancers had 31% perineural mast cells versus 13% in painless ones, and this did not track the grade of nerve invasion [[ANAT-002]]. A 2026 study added the next link: tumor-derived GDF15, the stress-signaling protein also implicated in cachexia (cancer-related wasting), reprograms Schwann cells, the nerves' support cells, into a state that promotes growth of pain-sensing fibers; destroying those cells relieved pain in mice, and plasma GDF15 correlated with pain scores in 120 patients [[ANAT-029]]. Early lesions may do the opposite, recruiting Schwann cells that dampen pain in mice, which could explain the long painless window [[ANAT-012]]. Nerves also feed the tumor: removing pancreatic sensory neurons in mice before disease onset extended median survival from 4.5 to 7.8 months, an experimental finding rather than a treatment [[TME-030]]. What helps: a neurolytic (nerve-destroying) celiac plexus block gave greater pain relief than opioids alone in a 100-patient randomized trial, without a quality-of-life or survival advantage [[ANAT-034]]; endoscopic ultrasound-guided neurolysis cut pain scores by 60.7% at three months in one trial [[SUPP-L04]] but not significantly at four weeks in another [[SUPP-L06]]. One warning: extending neurolysis to the celiac ganglia (the nerve-cell clusters within the plexus) shortened median survival (5.59 versus 10.46 months) without better pain relief [[SUPP-L05]]. Enzyme replacement lowered pancreatic-pain scores from 47 to 26 over three weeks in metastatic disease, so part of the pain is maldigestion and distension [[SUPP-021]].

action_note.heading: When to call the care team now
action_note.text: Pain that changes character suddenly, especially with fever or chills, jaundice, repeated vomiting or a swollen abdomen, can mean cholangitis or a blockage rather than the tumor itself and needs same-day assessment [[SEC-SUPP-14]][[SEC-SUPP-11]]. Pain that is no longer controlled by the prescribed plan is a reason to call rather than to wait for the next visit.

research_notes.what_findings_mean: Nerve biology comes from mouse models and resected human tissue, so it explains why pain exists and why it arrives late rather than proving any drug target; the GDF15 to Schwann-cell pathway is preclinical, with a human correlation to pain scores [[ANAT-029]]. The neurolysis trials are small, several are available to this atlas only as an abstract [[ANAT-034]][[SUPP-L04]][[SUPP-L06]], and they disagree on whether a block adds to good opioid care; the survival harm seen with ganglia neurolysis [[SUPP-L05]] is one trial but is the reason that technique is not standard. Symptom-prevalence figures describe people referred to palliative services, not everyone at diagnosis [[SUPP-032]].
research_notes.how_studied: Pain mechanisms are studied by staining resected tumors for nerve fibers, Schwann cells and immune cells and comparing patients who reported pain with those who did not [[ANAT-002]][[ANAT-029]], and by mouse models in which specific cell types are ablated or signaling molecules knocked down while pain behaviors such as hunching and withdrawal from touch are scored [[ANAT-012]][[ANAT-029]]. Nerve blocks are tested in randomized trials that compare pain scores on a 0-10 scale and opioid consumption at fixed times, typically 4 and 12 weeks, against opioid treatment alone [[ANAT-034]][[SUPP-L04]][[SUPP-005]].

mechanism_notes.text: The painless early window and the painful late disease may be two states of the same Schwann-cell population: early lesions recruit CXCL12-responsive Schwann cells that dampen pain signaling in mice, while established tumors secrete GDF15 that switches Schwann cells into a CCN3-positive, neurotrophin-secreting state that sensitizes pain fibers [[INF-ANAT-02]][[ANAT-012]][[ANAT-029]]. If correct, plasma GDF15 could serve as a pain biomarker, though it does not by itself prescribe an analgesic strategy.

glossary.definition: A web of nerves around the celiac artery, in front of the aorta, through which most pain signals from the pancreas travel.
Cancer cells growing along the sheath of a nerve.
Deliberately destroying a nerve or nerve plexus with alcohol or another agent to stop it carrying pain.
The support cell that wraps peripheral nerve fibers and helps them grow or repair.
Growth differentiation factor 15, a stress signal released by tumors that affects appetite, activity and, in this setting, pain.
An immune cell that releases histamine and other inflammatory chemicals, found clustered around nerves in painful tumors.

related.statement: Pain from pancreatic cancer travels through the celiac plexus, the nerve web that can be blocked to relieve it.
Nerves remodeled inside the tumor, with their Schwann cells and surrounding mast cells, are a proposed cause of pancreatic cancer pain.
The same tumor signal, GDF15, is implicated in both pancreatic cancer pain and cachexia.
Part of pancreatic pain is relieved by enzyme replacement because undigested food distends the gut.
Pain in pancreatic cancer is managed by palliative-care teams alongside oncology treatment.
A sudden change in pain with fever or vomiting can mean cholangitis or a blockage rather than tumor pain.

faq.q: Is back pain a sign of pancreatic cancer?
faq.a: Rarely on its own: in primary care it raised the odds only about 1.4-fold, while jaundice raised them roughly a thousandfold [[ANAT-010]]. It matters when it comes with weight loss, new diabetes, upper-abdominal pain or jaundice.

faq.q: Will a nerve block let me stop opioids?
faq.a: Usually not entirely. Blocks added pain relief in the randomized trials, but the reduction in morphine use was not statistically significant and quality of life did not improve [[SUPP-L04]][[ANAT-034]]; most people continue a lower dose.

topics.title: Weight loss, muscle loss and cachexia
topics.orientation: Losing weight and muscle is one of the most common and least visible parts of pancreatic cancer. It has two engines, one in the gut and one in the bloodstream, and they need different responses.

section1.label: What this experience involves
section1.preview: Weight loss here is rarely just eating less: people lose fat and muscle even when they manage to eat, and appetite fades on its own. In 20 people with unresectable disease, every one had lost weight by diagnosis, a median 14% of their usual weight [[SUPP-L03]]. Muscle can disappear behind a steady scale: during first-line chemotherapy, muscle area fell in 61% of men and 41% of women while body-mass index fell in only 37% [[SUPP-003]].
section1.full: Cachexia is a metabolic state of ongoing muscle loss, with or without fat loss, that feeding alone does not reverse. In pancreatic cancer it begins long before diagnosis. In a population study, blood sugar drifted up from about 30 months before diagnosis; from 18 months, fat and weight began falling while muscle held; in the final six months fat, muscle and cholesterol fell together while glucose kept rising, and fat tissue showed a more than 20-fold rise in UCP1, a protein that burns calories as heat [[ANAT-031]]. In mice, fat wasting appeared before invasive cancer and was driven by loss of digestive-enzyme delivery; an enzyme-supplemented diet reduced it [[ANAT-027]]. Among 782 untreated patients, 65% were sarcopenic (had low muscle mass) at diagnosis whatever the stage [[ANAT-027]]. Why it matters clinically: muscle loss, not weight, carried the risk. Sarcopenia at diagnosis was associated with a hazard ratio for death of 1.72 (a 72% higher rate of death over follow-up), and muscle loss during chemotherapy with 1.39, even in people whose body-mass index stayed stable (hazard ratio 1.50) [[SUPP-003]]; among mostly resected patients, those who lost muscle over six months had a median survival of 24.6 months versus 50.8 months for those who gained [[SUPP-015]]. These are group associations rather than individual forecasts, but they explain why clinicians now look at muscle on the CT scan rather than at the bathroom scale.

section2.label: Connection to pancreatic cancer
section2.preview: Pancreatic cancer attacks weight from two directions at once. Locally, a tumor blocking the pancreatic duct or replacing enzyme-making tissue stops fat and protein from being digested, so calories pass through unused. Systemically, the tumor and the inflamed tissue around it release signaling proteins, of which growth differentiation factor 15 (GDF-15) is the best established in humans, that suppress appetite, lower activity and drive muscle breakdown. Enzyme capsules fix only the first problem; the second needs different tools.
section2.full: The gut arm is well documented: exocrine insufficiency (too little enzyme reaching the gut) was present in 66% of head-region tumors at diagnosis and 92% two months later [[ANAT-041]], and in advanced disease it came with weight loss in 84% [[ANAT-021]]. Enzyme replacement in unresectable cancer produced a weight change of +1.2% versus -3.7% on placebo over eight weeks [[SUPP-L01]]. The systemic arm was shown directly in people by blocking the signal: in 187 people with cancer cachexia (32% pancreatic) and high GDF-15, the antibody ponsegromab raised body weight by 2.81 kg (95% credible interval 1.55 to 4.08) relative to placebo at 12 weeks at the highest dose, improved appetite scores and increased physical activity, with adverse events no more frequent than on placebo [[SUPP-014]]. That is phase 2 evidence; ponsegromab is investigational in the US as of 8 Oct 2026, and a phase 3 trial in pancreatic cancer cachexia is recruiting [[SEC-SUPP-15]]. The appetite-hormone mimic anamorelin added 1.89 kg of lean mass over 12 weeks in an uncontrolled Japanese study but raised blood sugar in about 6% and is not approved in the US [[SUPP-022]]. Current US guidance is dietary counseling for everyone, short courses of a progestin (a hormone-type appetite stimulant) or corticosteroid for appetite, low-dose olanzapine (an antipsychotic that stimulates appetite) as an option, and no routine tube or intravenous feeding in advanced cancer [[SEC-SUPP-05]]. Six months of resistance training did not change CT-measured muscle, which shows how strongly the systemic drive uncouples muscle from exercise [[SUPP-015]].

research_notes.what_findings_mean: Body-composition studies measure muscle on routine CT scans and relate it to survival; they are observational, so muscle loss marks a more aggressive course as much as it causes one, and cut-offs derived from the same data flatter the effect [[SUPP-003]][[SUPP-015]]. The ponsegromab trial is the strongest causal evidence that a circulating cytokine drives human cachexia, but it lasted 12 weeks, did not test survival, and its pancreatic subgroup is not separately reported [[SUPP-014]]. The enzyme and supplement trials from the 1990s and 2000s are available to this atlas only as an abstract [[SUPP-L01]][[SUPP-L02]][[SUPP-L03]]. Whether reversing cachexia improves chemotherapy tolerance, or responding tumors simply stop driving it, is unresolved [[SUPP-023]].
research_notes.how_studied: Skeletal muscle is quantified on the CT slice at the third lumbar vertebra and indexed to height, giving a skeletal muscle index that can be compared at diagnosis and at progression [[SUPP-003]][[SUPP-015]]. Pre-diagnostic trajectories come from population cohorts with stored glucose, lipid and weight records linked to later cancer diagnoses and read backwards in time [[ANAT-031]]. Mouse models separate the gut and systemic arms by implanting tumors in the pancreas versus under the skin and by measuring fecal fat and protein [[ANAT-027]]. Drug trials randomize against placebo and weigh patients at 12 weeks, with appetite questionnaires and wrist-worn activity monitors as secondary measures [[SUPP-014]].

mechanism_notes.text: Reversing cachexia may improve delivered chemotherapy dose intensity and physical reserve, which would explain why anamorelin responders had twice the disease control of non-responders (75.0% versus 37.5%); the competing explanation is reverse causation, in which responding tumors stop secreting GDF-15 and interleukin-6 so appetite recovers on its own [[INF-SUPP-03]][[SUPP-023]][[SUPP-014]]. The phase 3 ponsegromab trial can test this through relative dose intensity and treatment discontinuation [[SEC-SUPP-15]].

Weight-based monitoring misses the problem because a systemic catabolic drive uncouples muscle from weight: muscle fell in 40-60% of patients while body-mass index held in most, and six months of resistance loading did not change CT muscle area [[SUPP-003]][[SUPP-015]]. This is why muscle-directed treatment is being tested on the cytokine axis rather than on exercise alone.

glossary.definition: A wasting state of ongoing muscle loss driven by the cancer's metabolic signals, not fully reversed by eating more.
Low skeletal muscle mass, usually measured on a CT scan.
Growth differentiation factor 15, a stress signal released by tumors that suppresses appetite and activity through a brainstem receptor.
Muscle area on a CT slice at the third lumbar vertebra divided by height squared.
Too little pancreatic enzyme reaching the intestine to digest food.
A drug that mimics the hunger hormone ghrelin, approved in Japan but not in the US.

related.statement: Enzyme insufficiency is the gut-side cause of weight loss in pancreatic cancer and responds to enzyme replacement.
Cachexia in pancreatic cancer is treated with counseling, appetite medicines and investigational GDF-15 blockade.
The phase 3 ponsegromab trial tests whether blocking GDF-15 reverses cachexia in pancreatic cancer.
Weight loss in pancreatic cancer is addressed first through dietitian-led nutrition and protein intake.
Muscle loss in cachexia limits physical function even though strength can improve with training.
GDF-15, the cytokine driving cachexia, also promotes pain through Schwann cells in pancreatic cancer.

faq.q: If I eat more, will the weight loss stop?
faq.a: Eating and enzymes address the gut side and slow loss, but the systemic drive continues: in a trial of an enriched supplement, both groups stopped losing weight only while intake was maintained [[SUPP-L02]], and blocking GDF-15 restored weight in a way that calories alone did not [[SUPP-014]]. Weight loss is not a sign of insufficient effort.

faq.q: Why does my doctor care about muscle when my weight is stable?
faq.a: Because muscle fell in 61% of men and 41% of women during chemotherapy while body-mass index fell in only 37%, and muscle loss predicted shorter survival even when weight held [[SUPP-003]].

topics.title: Digestion and pancreatic enzyme insufficiency
topics.orientation: The pancreas makes the enzymes that break down fat, protein and starch. When a tumor blocks the pancreatic duct or surgery removes the gland, food passes through undigested; replacement enzymes taken with meals restore much of that work.

section1.label: What this experience involves
section1.preview: Exocrine pancreatic insufficiency means the small intestine no longer receives enough pancreatic enzymes. The signs are pale, greasy or oily stools that float and are hard to flush, bloating and gas within an hour of eating, cramping, and weight loss despite a reasonable intake. It is present in about two-thirds of people with pancreatic cancer at diagnosis and rises above 90% within months when the tumor sits in the head [[ANAT-021]][[ANAT-041]].
section1.full: A healthy pancreas secretes about 2.5 liters a day of juice: acinar cells release lipase, proteases and amylase when the hormone cholecystokinin signals a meal, and duct cells add bicarbonate through CFTR channels (the same channel that is faulty in cystic fibrosis) to neutralize stomach acid, which lipase needs in order to work [[ANAT-009]]. A head tumor interrupts this in three ways: it blocks the duct so enzymes cannot leave, it replaces enzyme-making tissue, and after a Whipple operation the rebuilt anatomy delivers food and enzymes out of step. In 32 unresected head-region tumors, insufficiency was present in 66% at diagnosis and 92% after a median of two months [[ANAT-041]]. In advanced disease assessed by dietitians, 64-66% had insufficiency, with weight loss in 84%, flatus (gas) in 84% and steatorrhea in 48%; vitamin D was low in 44% and vitamin A in 18%, and insufficiency was associated with shorter survival (hazard ratio 2.28) [[ANAT-021]]. Despite this, US insurance data from 2001-2013 showed that only 1.9% of people with pancreatic cancer were ever tested, 21.9% ever filled an enzyme prescription, and 5.5% received an adequately dosed one [[SUPP-001]]. Diagnosis rests on symptoms plus a stool test, fecal elastase-1, with values below 200 micrograms per gram abnormal; the test loses accuracy after a Whipple, when the clinical picture decides [[SEC-SUPP-09]]. A person whose stools have started floating and who is losing weight while eating normally has a textbook presentation.

section2.label: Connection to pancreatic cancer
section2.preview: Pancreatic enzyme replacement therapy (PERT) supplies lipase, protease and amylase of porcine (pig-derived) origin in enteric-coated capsules taken with every meal and snack, so the enzymes release in the small intestine alongside the food. In a placebo-controlled trial after pancreatic surgery it raised fat absorption by about 26 percentage points [[SUPP-002]]; in metastatic disease it eased diarrhea within a week and pain and bloating within three [[SUPP-021]]. Pancrelipase is approved in the US for exocrine insufficiency from any cause [[SEC-SUPP-10]].
section2.full: Dose and timing decide whether it works. The US label starts adults after pancreatectomy at 500-1,000 lipase units per kilogram per meal and caps dosing at 2,500 units per kilogram per meal or 10,000 units per kilogram per day without further investigation [[SEC-SUPP-10]]; European guidance starts at 40,000-50,000 units with each main meal and half that with snacks, titrates upward on symptoms and weight, and adds an acid-suppressing drug when the response is incomplete, because acid inactivates lipase [[SEC-SUPP-09]]. Capsules are swallowed with the first mouthfuls and spread through a long meal rather than taken afterwards [[SEC-SUPP-18]]. The limits matter as much as the benefit. In the surgical trial, the coefficient of fat absorption rose 25.6 points more than on placebo, yet among people whose operations altered gut motility (total pancreatectomy, Whipple or similar) only 7 of 26 (27%) reached near-normal absorption, because enzymes and food leave the stomach out of step [[SUPP-002]]. Flatulence was the main side effect (12.5% versus 7.7%) [[SUPP-002]]. In 160 unresectable patients, enzyme use was associated with longer survival (the authors report an adjusted hazard ratio of 1.81 in favor of survival, roughly an 80% higher chance of being alive at any given time), but treated patients also received chemotherapy far more often (71.6% versus 46.5%), so the survival link is confounded [[SUPP-020]]. The one placebo-controlled trial in unresectable cancer showed weight +1.2% versus -3.7% and higher energy intake over eight weeks [[SUPP-L01]].

research_notes.what_findings_mean: The fat-absorption trial [[SUPP-002]] was one week double-blind in 58 post-surgical patients with mixed benign and malignant disease, so its 25.6-point gain is a physiological proof rather than a cancer-specific outcome. Prevalence figures come from dietitian assessment or monthly stool elastase in small cohorts [[ANAT-021]][[ANAT-041]]. The prescribing gap [[SUPP-001]] reflects commercially insured US patients from 2001-2013 and may have narrowed since. The survival association [[SUPP-020]] is non-randomized and inseparable from access to chemotherapy; symptom relief [[SUPP-021]] was measured without a placebo arm.
research_notes.how_studied: Fat absorption is measured as the coefficient of fat absorption: patients eat a fixed-fat diet for several days while stool is collected and its fat content weighed, so the percentage absorbed can be compared on enzymes and on placebo [[SUPP-002]]. Fecal elastase-1 is a stool immunoassay that reflects pancreatic output and is unaffected by taking enzymes, which is why it can be repeated monthly [[ANAT-041]][[SEC-SUPP-09]]. Prescribing patterns come from insurance claims linked to diagnosis codes [[SUPP-001]]. Symptom change is scored with the EORTC pancreatic cancer questionnaire, a standard patient-reported instrument, at baseline, one and three weeks [[SUPP-021]].

mechanism_notes.text: After a Whipple, enteric-coated enzyme microspheres and food leave the stomach at different times and enter a jejunal limb (the loop of small intestine joined to the stomach) without the duodenum's bicarbonate, so enzyme release is mistimed and lipase is partly inactivated by acid; this would explain why only 27% of such patients normalize fat absorption even at high doses [[INF-SUPP-01]][[SUPP-002]]. A competing explanation is residual insufficiency of the remnant plus bile-acid malabsorption; a crossover trial of opened or uncoated enzymes mixed with food plus acid suppression would discriminate between them.

glossary.definition: Too little pancreatic enzyme reaching the small intestine to digest fat, protein and starch.
Pale, greasy, floating stools caused by undigested fat.
A stool test that measures a pancreatic enzyme as a marker of how much the gland is producing.
The pancreatic enzyme that breaks dietary fat into absorbable pieces.
The percentage of eaten fat that is absorbed rather than passed in stool.
A capsule coating that resists stomach acid and dissolves in the small intestine.

related.statement: Enzyme insufficiency follows loss or obstruction of the acinar cells that make pancreatic digestive enzymes.
A tumor blocking the main pancreatic duct prevents enzymes from reaching the intestine and causes insufficiency.
Exocrine insufficiency is treated with pancreatic enzyme replacement capsules taken with every meal.
After a Whipple, enzyme insufficiency persists in most people because the rebuilt anatomy mistimes enzyme and food delivery.
Undigested fat and protein from enzyme insufficiency is one of the two engines of weight loss in pancreatic cancer.
Enzyme replacement is the precondition for nutrition advice to work when fat is passing through undigested.

faq.q: How do I know if I need enzymes?
faq.a: Floating, greasy stools, gas soon after meals and weight loss despite eating are the clinical signs, and a stool elastase below 200 micrograms per gram confirms it; European guidance recommends enzymes for pancreatic cancer with duct obstruction or after resection [[SEC-SUPP-09]]. In the US fewer than 2% of patients were ever tested, so asking is reasonable [[SUPP-001]].

faq.q: I take enzymes but still have symptoms. Why?
faq.a: The dose may be too low or taken at the wrong time, stomach acid may be inactivating the enzyme, or, after a Whipple, enzymes and food may be leaving the stomach out of step; only 27% of such patients normalized fat absorption in a trial [[SUPP-002]]. Guidance is to titrate the dose, spread capsules through the meal and add acid suppression [[SEC-SUPP-09]].

topics.title: Blood sugar and diabetes
topics.orientation: Diabetes and pancreatic cancer are linked in both directions, but the common pattern is the cancer causing the diabetes. Knowing which kind of diabetes a person has, cancer-driven, surgery-driven or steroid-driven, changes how it is managed.

section1.label: What this experience involves
section1.preview: Nearly half of people with pancreatic cancer have diabetes at diagnosis, and about three-quarters of those cases began within the previous two years [[ANAT-015]]. Blood sugar starts drifting upward around 30-36 months before diagnosis and crosses the diabetes threshold in the final 6-12 months [[ANAT-016]]. New diabetes together with unexplained weight loss, especially in someone who was not overweight, is a recognized warning pattern rather than a coincidence [[ANAT-028]].
section1.full: In 512 newly diagnosed patients at one US center, 47.4% met criteria for diabetes versus 7.2% of matched controls, and only 14% had a normal fasting glucose [[ANAT-015]]. The rise is slow and then steep: fasting glucose separated from controls 36-30 months before diagnosis and crossed 126 mg/dL (the diabetes threshold) about six months before, and in resected tumors a glucose signal was detectable when the tumor measured only 1-2 cubic centimeters, several doublings before the usual size at diagnosis [[ANAT-016]]. The reverse question, how often new diabetes signals cancer, has a sobering but small answer: among 2,122 people who developed diabetes after age 50, 0.85% were diagnosed with pancreatic cancer within three years, about eight times the expected rate, and over half of those within six months [[ORIG-009]]. Weight loss sharpens the signal: recent-onset diabetes with more than 8 lb of weight loss carried an incidence of 164 per 100,000 person-years against 16 with neither, and higher still in people of previously normal weight [[ANAT-028]]. US guidance does not endorse screening average-risk adults, so new diabetes is treated as a risk marker that justifies attention to other symptoms, not as a screening test. A third kind of high sugar appears during chemotherapy, when dexamethasone, a steroid given to prevent nausea, pushes glucose up for a day or two; in a lymphoma cohort those affected declared themselves in the first cycle [[SUPP-028]].

section2.label: Connection to pancreatic cancer
section2.preview: Cancer-associated diabetes is a paraneoplastic effect: the tumor secretes factors that impair insulin release and action throughout the body, rather than simply destroying insulin-making islets. The evidence is that it appears when tumors are only 1-2 cubic centimeters, is no more common with tumors in the islet-rich tail than in the head, and resolved in 17 of 30 people after removal of a head tumor even though surgery takes away more gland [[ANAT-015]][[ANAT-016]]. Surgery itself causes a different diabetes, through loss of islet mass.
section2.full: Candidate mediators include adrenomedullin, a peptide carried to islets inside tumor-derived vesicles that suppressed insulin secretion in human islets [[ANAT-014]][[ANAT-025]], and TGF-beta, a growth-regulating signal that selectively depleted beta cells in mice [[ANAT-026]], although the human picture is one of high insulin and insulin resistance, so no single mediator yet accounts for it. Surgical diabetes follows islet loss and host demand together. Healthy donors who gave half a pancreas developed impaired glucose handling or diabetes in 40-55% within a decade [[ANAT-006]]. After distal pancreatectomy, 290 of 1,034 patients (28%) developed diabetes at a median of 354 days, twice as often with obesity [[SUPP-004]]; after a Whipple, 30.2% had new diabetes by six months, predicted by body-mass index rather than by the volume of pancreas left behind [[SUPP-033]], and a fatty remnant plus an HbA1c (the three-month average of blood sugar) above 5.7% multiplied the two-year risk about fivefold [[SUPP-035]]. After total pancreatectomy, insulin-requiring diabetes is immediate and universal; at 12 months the median HbA1c was 8.0% on injections or a pump, with only 0.2% of time below 70 mg/dL (the low-blood-sugar threshold) on continuous monitoring [[SUPP-036]]. What helps: endocrinology input early, home or continuous glucose monitoring, insulin when needed, and checking glucose during steroid-containing chemotherapy cycles.

research_notes.what_findings_mean: The pre-diagnostic glucose work reads stored laboratory values backwards from diagnosis in population cohorts, which shows timing but cannot say which individual's diabetes is cancer-related; about 10% of cancers never raise glucose [[ANAT-016]]. The 'resolution after resection' finding rests on 30 patients at a median of 48 days, with similar weight loss in both groups [[ANAT-015]]. Post-surgical diabetes rates vary with follow-up length, indication and how diabetes was recorded, and remnant volume predicted it in one 66-patient cohort but not in a 159-patient one [[SUPP-033]][[SUPP-035]][[SUPP-004]]. Steroid hyperglycemia data come from lymphoma, not pancreatic cancer [[SUPP-028]].
research_notes.how_studied: Case-control registries compare fasting glucose, HbA1c and diabetes diagnoses in people later found to have pancreatic cancer against matched controls at fixed intervals before diagnosis [[ANAT-001]][[ANAT-016]]. Mechanistic studies expose cultured islets or mice to tumor-conditioned medium, isolated vesicles or specific peptides and measure glucose-stimulated insulin release [[ANAT-014]][[ANAT-025]]. Post-operative diabetes is tracked through national diabetes registers or clinic visits, and the remnant pancreas is measured by CT volumetry with tissue density as a proxy for fat content [[SUPP-004]][[SUPP-035]]. After total pancreatectomy, continuous glucose monitors report time in and below range [[SUPP-036]].

mechanism_notes.text: Tumor-derived mediators impose a functional suppression of insulin secretion and action on a numerically preserved beta-cell mass, so removing the tumor withdraws the mediator and function recovers, whereas surgery removes beta-cell mass irreversibly [[INF-ANAT-01]][[ANAT-015]][[ANAT-025]]. The competing explanation is structural beta-cell loss; serial measurements of C-peptide, a marker of the body's own insulin output, before and after resection would discriminate.

Diabetes after partial pancreatectomy appears when functional beta-cell capacity (remnant volume multiplied by islet quality, reduced by fat and atrophy) falls below the insulin demand set by body fat. Surgery removes a roughly fixed fraction of capacity, so variation in demand and remnant quality explains why body-mass index and HbA1c predict diabetes more consistently than volume [[INF-SUPP-02]][[SUPP-033]][[SUPP-035]][[SUPP-036]].

glossary.definition: Caused by substances a tumor releases into the body rather than by its direct growth.
Diabetes caused by disease or removal of the pancreas, as distinct from type 1 or type 2.
A blood test reflecting average blood sugar over about three months.
Clusters of hormone-producing cells scattered through the pancreas, including the beta cells that make insulin.
The islet cell that makes and releases insulin.
A wearable sensor that records blood sugar every few minutes.

related.statement: Cancer-associated diabetes arises from suppressed islet function, while surgical diabetes arises from loss of islet mass.
Diabetes after pancreatic surgery is managed with monitoring and insulin as described under managing blood sugar after surgery.
Total pancreatectomy causes immediate insulin-requiring diabetes in every patient.
New-onset diabetes with weight loss is a risk marker for pancreatic cancer rather than a screening test.
Rising blood sugar precedes the fat and muscle loss of pancreatic cancer by about a year.
Dexamethasone given to prevent chemotherapy nausea raises blood sugar for a day or two each cycle.

faq.q: I was just diagnosed with diabetes. Should I be scanned for pancreatic cancer?
faq.a: For most people, no: about 1% of those developing diabetes after 50 are found to have pancreatic cancer within three years [[ORIG-009]], and US guidance does not recommend screening average-risk adults. The combination with unexplained weight loss, especially from a normal starting weight, raises the risk enough to warrant a conversation [[ANAT-028]].

faq.q: Will my diabetes go away after surgery?
faq.a: Sometimes. Diabetes that began within two years of diagnosis resolved in 17 of 30 people after removal of a head tumor, while long-standing diabetes did not [[ANAT-015]]. Surgery can also cause new diabetes, in about 28-30% after partial resection [[SUPP-004]][[SUPP-033]].

topics.title: Fatigue and energy
topics.orientation: Fatigue in pancreatic cancer is a whole-body tiredness that rest does not fix. It usually has several causes stacked together, and some of them are treatable.

section1.label: What this experience involves
section1.preview: Cancer fatigue is different from ordinary tiredness: it is out of proportion to activity, is not relieved by sleep, and dulls thinking as well as muscles. It is common early and late. Fatigue was reported by 51% of people in the months before a pancreatic cancer diagnosis versus 26% of those without cancer [[ANAT-004]], and among people with pain or appetite distress at palliative-care referral, 77% also reported fatigue distress [[SUPP-032]].
section1.full: The evidence supports several contributors, and most people have more than one. First, the tumor's chemical signals: GDF-15, the cytokine that drives cachexia (cancer-related wasting), also lowers activity, and blocking it with an antibody in a phase 2 trial increased non-sedentary time by 12 minutes a day while it fell by 38 minutes on placebo [[SUPP-014]]; before diagnosis, weight-losing patients ran a measurably higher body temperature as fat tissue switched to burning calories [[ANAT-031]]. Second, treatment: severe fatigue (grade 3 or higher) occurred in 17% of people on the two-drug chemotherapy gemcitabine plus nab-paclitaxel versus 7% on gemcitabine alone [[TX-001]], and anemia from chemotherapy's effect on bone marrow reduces oxygen delivery, a standard cause that is checked with a blood count. Third, deconditioning: muscle fell in 61% of men and 41% of women during first-line chemotherapy [[SUPP-003]], and more sedentary time was associated with lower quality of life while light activity went with higher [[SUPP-017]]. Fourth, the fixable companions: undigested food from enzyme insufficiency, unstable blood sugar, pain and the opioids used for it, depression, and broken sleep. Long after a Whipple, fatigue scores remained modest (21-28 on a 100-point scale) in five-year survivors [[SUPP-031]]. Because the list is long, the useful first step is to work out which items apply.

section2.label: Connection to pancreatic cancer
section2.preview: Fatigue is not a sign that treatment is failing, nor a personal failing. It reflects the metabolic cost of a tumor that recruits the body's inflammatory machinery, the cumulative effect of chemotherapy on blood counts and muscle, and the ordinary consequences of eating and sleeping badly. Treating the treatable parts, anemia, enzyme insufficiency, blood sugar, pain and mood, and keeping up light regular activity are what the evidence supports.
section2.full: What helps has modest but real support. In 50 people exercising at home during preoperative chemotherapy, six-minute walk distance rose from 462.5 to 488.2 meters, a clinically meaningful gain, and self-reported physical function improved [[SUPP-017]]; supervised resistance training improved strength in some muscle groups in a randomized trial, though it did not change body weight [[SUPP-L12]]. Early palliative care lowered overall symptom burden in people with metastatic disease (a 7.4-point fall on the Edmonton symptom scale, a standard patient-rated symptom questionnaire) in a small prospective study [[SUPP-030]]. After surgery, an extra 18 g of protein a day improved walking speed and quality of life in elderly patients [[SUPP-016]]. Enzyme replacement relieved diarrhea and bloating within weeks in metastatic disease, removing one drain on energy [[SUPP-021]]. None of these is a cure for fatigue, and the studies cited here include no pancreatic-specific trial of a fatigue drug, so the practical approach is to name the contributors with the care team and address them one by one, pacing activity rather than pushing through it. A blood count, a glucose check and a stool question cover three of the commonest causes in one visit.

research_notes.what_findings_mean: Fatigue is rarely a primary endpoint; the numbers here come from symptom-prevalence surveys [[ANAT-004]][[SUPP-032]], adverse-event tables in chemotherapy trials [[TX-001]] and secondary outcomes of exercise and palliative-care studies [[SUPP-017]][[SUPP-030]]. The cytokine link is inferred from the activity measures in the ponsegromab trial, which was designed for weight, not fatigue [[SUPP-014]]. Anemia as a cause is established physiology rather than a pancreatic-specific finding among the studies cited here, which is why no number is attached to it.
research_notes.how_studied: Symptom prevalence comes from questionnaires and clinical records before diagnosis and at palliative-care admission [[ANAT-004]][[SUPP-032]]. Chemotherapy trials grade fatigue with standard toxicity criteria, where grade 3 means it limits self-care [[TX-001]]. Exercise studies measure walking distance in six minutes, sit-to-stand time and gait speed, and relate accelerometer-recorded activity to quality-of-life scores [[SUPP-017]]. The cachexia trial used wrist-worn monitors to record sedentary and non-sedentary minutes [[SUPP-014]].

mechanism_notes.text: Part of pancreatic cancer fatigue may be the same GDF-15 signaling that drives anorexia and inactivity in cachexia, since blocking GDF-15 raised measured activity in humans [[SUPP-014]] and pre-diagnostic patients showed a raised metabolic rate with fat browning [[ANAT-031]]. Fatigue was not an endpoint in those studies, so this remains an inference.

glossary.definition: Persistent exhaustion out of proportion to activity and not relieved by rest, caused by the cancer or its treatment.
Too few red blood cells or too little hemoglobin to carry oxygen efficiently.
Loss of fitness and muscle from inactivity, which makes ordinary tasks more tiring.
A signaling protein released by tumor or immune cells that acts on distant organs, including the brain.
A functional test measuring how far a person can walk in six minutes.

related.statement: The cytokine signaling that drives cachexia also lowers activity and contributes to fatigue in pancreatic cancer.
Fatigue is partly countered by light regular activity, which improved walking capacity during treatment.
Depression and poor sleep are common contributors to fatigue in pancreatic cancer and are treatable.
Gemcitabine plus nab-paclitaxel caused severe fatigue in 17% of patients, more than gemcitabine alone.
Undigested food from enzyme insufficiency drains energy and is a treatable contributor to fatigue.
Palliative-care teams address the symptom cluster of fatigue, pain, sleep and appetite together.

faq.q: Should I rest more or move more?
faq.a: Both, in proportion. More sedentary time was associated with lower quality of life and light activity with higher during preoperative treatment, and walking capacity improved with a home program [[SUPP-017]]. Pacing short daily activity around chemotherapy days works better than long rests followed by overexertion.

topics.title: Nausea, diarrhea and bowel changes during chemotherapy
topics.orientation: Nausea, diarrhea and constipation during chemotherapy are predictable from the drugs used, and each has a specific prevention or treatment. The disease itself adds bowel changes that can be mistaken for drug effects.

section1.label: What this experience involves
section1.preview: Nausea tends to peak in the first days after each infusion and then fade; with modern prevention most people have little vomiting, but low-grade nausea and food aversion are common. Bowel effects depend on the regimen: irinotecan-containing combinations such as FOLFIRINOX (fluorouracil, leucovorin, irinotecan and oxaliplatin) and NALIRIFOX (a combination built on a liposomal form of irinotecan) cause diarrhea, which was more frequent with NALIRIFOX than with gemcitabine plus nab-paclitaxel in a head-to-head trial [[TX-002]], while anti-nausea drugs and opioids push the other way, toward constipation.
section1.full: Oxaliplatin and irinotecan are classed as moderately emetogenic, so standard prevention is a 5-HT3 antagonist (a serotonin-receptor blocker such as ondansetron) plus dexamethasone (a steroid), with an NK1 antagonist (a second class of anti-nausea drug) optional; gemcitabine is low-risk [[SEC-SUPP-06]]. Olanzapine, an antipsychotic used at low dose for its anti-nausea effect, raised the proportion with no nausea over five days from 22% to 37% when added to standard drugs for highly emetogenic chemotherapy, at the cost of sedation on day two in 5% [[SUPP-027]]; that trial used cisplatin-level regimens, so the benefit for pancreatic regimens is extrapolated by class, and olanzapine is off-label for this use in the US. Irinotecan causes two distinct diarrheas: an early cholinergic form within a day of infusion, with cramping, sweating and watery stools, which atropine treats, and a late form days later, for which the liposomal irinotecan label directs loperamide for diarrhea of any severity and withholding treatment at grade 2 or worse [[SEC-SUPP-11]]. People who inherit low-activity variants of UGT1A1, the gene for the enzyme that clears irinotecan's active metabolite, carry more of it; reducing their starting dose by 30% brought severe toxicity down to the level of normal metabolizers with no measurable loss of survival in 779 patients [[GENE-018]]. In a neoadjuvant trial, grade 3-4 diarrhea occurred in 23% on FOLFIRINOX versus 1% on gemcitabine-based chemoradiation [[TX-L13]]. A practical example: watery stools on day five of a FOLFIRINOX cycle call for loperamide at the first loose stool and extra fluids, not waiting to see.

section2.label: Connection to pancreatic cancer
section2.preview: Not every bowel change is the chemotherapy. Pale, greasy, floating stools are undigested fat from enzyme insufficiency, which is present in about two-thirds of people and responds to enzyme capsules, not loperamide [[ANAT-021]]. Vomiting of undigested food hours after eating points to a narrowed duodenum rather than drug nausea. Sorting out which mechanism is at work comes first, because the treatments are different and sometimes opposite.
section2.full: Enzyme replacement lowered diarrhea scores from 26 to 8 within one week and bloating from 46 to 26 by three weeks in 29 people with metastatic disease, which is the pattern of maldigestion rather than drug toxicity [[SUPP-021]]. Bile-duct obstruction removes bile salts from the gut and adds to fat malabsorption; relieving it with a stent helps digestion as well as jaundice. A tumor pressing on the duodenum causes early fullness, then vomiting of food eaten hours earlier; it is uncommon at first presentation but developed in about 1 in 5 people with unresectable head tumors over the following months [[ANAT-032]]. Constipation has its own causes here: 5-HT3 anti-nausea drugs, opioids for pain, reduced intake and inactivity, and, less often, bowel obstruction from disease on the peritoneum, which must be excluded before stimulant laxatives or further chemotherapy, since the liposomal irinotecan label prohibits giving the drug with bowel obstruction [[SEC-SUPP-11]]. Dehydration from diarrhea or vomiting matters more than usual in pancreatic cancer because it concentrates the blood in a condition already prone to clots and can tip kidney function during chemotherapy. Steroid premedication also raises blood sugar for a day or two, so people with diabetes may need an adjusted plan on infusion days [[SUPP-028]]. Keeping a simple diary of stools, fluids and tablets taken makes the next clinic conversation far more useful.

action_note.heading: When to call the care team now
action_note.text: Diarrhea that persists despite loperamide, diarrhea of grade 2 or worse (four or more stools a day above your usual), or any diarrhea with a fever of 100.4 °F (38 °C) or higher, dizziness on standing or inability to keep fluids down needs same-day contact; the liposomal irinotecan label calls for withholding treatment at that level [[SEC-SUPP-11]][[SEC-SUPP-03]]. Repeated vomiting, vomiting of food eaten hours earlier, or a swollen abdomen with no stool or gas can mean a blockage rather than drug nausea and should not wait for the next visit [[SEC-SUPP-11]].

research_notes.what_findings_mean: The olanzapine trial [[SUPP-027]] enrolled people on cisplatin-level regimens, so its 15-point gain is a ceiling, not an estimate, for the moderately emetogenic drugs used here [[SEC-SUPP-06]]. Diarrhea rates come from adverse-event tables of trials designed for survival, graded by clinicians rather than reported by patients [[TX-002]][[TX-L13]]. The UGT1A1 study [[GENE-018]] is retrospective and mixes colorectal and pancreatic cancers, and no trial of irinotecan-diarrhea treatment is cited here; the loperamide and atropine instructions come from the product label [[SEC-SUPP-11]]. Symptom relief from enzymes was measured without a placebo [[SUPP-021]].
research_notes.how_studied: Antiemetic trials randomize people to standard prevention with or without the test drug and record nausea on daily diaries over 120 hours, reporting 'no nausea' and 'complete response', meaning no vomiting and no rescue medication [[SUPP-027]].
