A cyst is pure fluid: very bright on T2-weighted images (the MRI sequence that highlights water), without enhancement after contrast, and with high diffusion values because water moves freely inside it. A hemangioma is also very bright on T2 and fills in with contrast from the edge inward over successive phases, slowly, because its vessels are wide and the flow through them is sluggish. A metastasis is only moderately bright on T2, restricts diffusion because it is packed with cells, enhances at its rim early and washes out, and, when a liver-specific contrast agent is used, fails to take up the agent in the late hepatobiliary phase because it contains no functioning liver cells. When the spot is too small for those properties to be read reliably, time becomes the test: a cyst or hemangioma is stable across months, whereas a metastasis grows, and a repeat scan after an interval is how most indeterminate spots are classified. In 1,004 patients taken to staging laparoscopy, an indeterminate extrapancreatic lesion on imaging raised the odds of finding hidden spread nearly seven-fold, so the ambiguous spot is informative even before it is resolved [[DIAG-002]].

section2.label: Why it matters here
section2.preview: The liver is where pancreatic cancer most often spreads, and a confirmed metastasis moves the disease into the metastatic category and away from a pancreatectomy, so a small spot carries weight out of proportion to its size. Care teams resolve it before surgery rather than after, which is why a preoperative MRI is ordered when CT leaves a spot unsettled.
section2.full: In a cohort of 343 resected patients, the liver was the first site of recurrence in 49%, and liver recurrence carried a median survival of 13 months against 30 for lung recurrence [[SURG-015]]. Pancreatic cancer prepares the liver before cells arrive: in mouse models, tumor-derived vesicles and signals that make liver cells produce inflammatory proteins build a fibrotic niche, rich in macrophages (immune scavenger cells), that receives and sustains metastases [[SURG-010]][[SURG-022]], and single dormant cancer cells have been found in patients' livers, below the resolution of any scan [[SURG-012]]. The scan therefore under-counts, which is why laparoscopy still finds liver or peritoneal deposits in 18% of patients whose imaging showed localized disease [[DIAG-002]]. Preoperative MRI shifts the balance measurably: among 4,579 pancreatectomies in Ontario, patients who had an MRI first had a median survival of 33.1 months against 21.1, an adjusted hazard ratio (relative death rate) of 0.83, and a companion analysis found fewer futile operations, 6.4% against 9.7% [[DIAG-021]][[SEC-DIAG-07]]. The MRI did not change the cancer; it most likely identified metastases in patients who would otherwise have had an operation that could not help them, and the MRI group was also younger and more often given chemotherapy first [[DIAG-021]]. The usual sequence is that CT finds a spot, MRI characterizes it or does not, and an unresolved spot is biopsied if reachable or re-imaged after a course of chemotherapy, which answers the question while treatment is under way. Most spots prove benign; the ones that do not are best found before a Whipple rather than after.

research_notes.what_findings_mean: The MRI survival association is observational and confounded by indication, meaning the patients chosen for MRI differed from those who were not; the administrative data do not say what the MRI found or confirm that patients spared surgery had metastases [[DIAG-021]][[SEC-DIAG-07]]. The seven-fold odds for an indeterminate lesion come from one center's laparoscopy series and apply to lesions anywhere outside the pancreas, not only the liver [[DIAG-002]]. The liver-niche work is in mice, with observational human correlates [[SURG-010]][[SURG-022]], and the dormant-cell findings are descriptive in humans [[SURG-012]]. The imaging signatures described above are established radiology practice and are stated here without diagnostic-accuracy figures, because none of the sources used here measured the accuracy of MRI for sub-centimeter liver lesions in pancreatic cancer specifically.
research_notes.how_studied: The effect of preoperative MRI is studied in population data by comparing survival and futile-surgery rates between patients with and without MRI after adjustment or propensity weighting [[DIAG-021]][[SEC-DIAG-07]]. The predictive value of an indeterminate lesion is measured by multivariable regression against the laparoscopic finding [[DIAG-002]]. Site-specific recurrence outcomes are measured by classifying the first recurrence site on surveillance imaging and comparing survival [[SURG-015]]. Niche formation is studied by injecting tumor-derived vesicles or blocking individual signals in mice and counting liver metastases [[SURG-010]][[SURG-022]], and dormant cells by immunostaining patient livers for cells that have lost epithelial and immune-recognition markers [[SURG-012]].

mechanism_notes.text: Some cancer cells that reach the liver persist as single dormant cells under immune surveillance and awaken later, which would explain a liver metastasis appearing years after a clean preoperative MRI and a margin-negative operation [[INF-SURG-01]][[SURG-012]]. The competing explanation is slow continuous growth below imaging thresholds, and serial blood sampling paired with profiling of relapsing lesions is the test.

Liver recurrence may be so much more lethal than lung recurrence because the liver, uniquely, has been prepared by pancreatic-cancer-specific niche programs that accelerate outgrowth and exclude killer T cells, whereas the lung lacks an equivalent niche [[INF-SURG-02]][[SURG-015]][[SURG-022]]. Lead-time bias, lung nodules being found earlier and smaller on surveillance scans, is the competing explanation.

glossary.definition: A spot on a scan whose nature the radiologist cannot decide from that scan alone.
A common benign tangle of blood vessels in the liver that fills slowly with contrast from the edge inward.
A late set of MRI images with a liver-specific contrast agent in which normal liver cells take up the agent and metastases do not.
Hindered movement of water molecules on MRI, typical of tissue packed with cells such as a metastasis.
A deposit of cancer growing at a site distant from the organ where the cancer began.

related.statement: Small liver spots are findings within the liver, the organ to which pancreatic cancer most often spreads.
MRI characterizes small liver spots by their T2 brightness, diffusion and contrast behavior, which CT cannot read at that size.
The liver is prepared for metastasis by tumor-derived signals before any liver spot is visible on a scan.
An indeterminate lesion on imaging is the strongest predictor that staging laparoscopy will find hidden spread.
The liver is the first site of recurrence in about half of patients after resection, and liver recurrence carries the shortest survival.
Pancreas-protocol CT finds small liver spots but often cannot say what they are.
A liver spot confirmed as metastasis moves the disease into the metastatic category regardless of the pancreatic tumor's anatomy.

faq.q: My CT report mentions a 5 mm spot in the liver that is 'too small to characterize'. Is it cancer?
faq.a: Usually not; tiny cysts and hemangiomas are common in healthy adults and are the usual cause. Because the liver is where pancreatic cancer most often spreads, the spot will be checked rather than ignored, typically with MRI and, if still unresolved, a repeat scan after an interval, since benign spots stay the same and metastases grow. An unresolved lesion does raise the chance that hidden spread will be found at laparoscopy, which is why it is settled before any operation [[DIAG-002]].

topics.title: Treatment sequencing: before, after or instead of surgery
topics.orientation: Pancreatic cancer treatment is rarely one thing; it is an order of things. This topic explains the words doctors use for that order, why the order exists at all, and why the same drug can carry very different numbers depending on where in the sequence it was tested.

section1.label: What it does
section1.preview: Doctors name a treatment by its position in a sequence rather than by the drug. Neoadjuvant therapy is given before an operation, adjuvant therapy after it, and perioperative therapy on both sides. When no operation is planned, the main treatment is called definitive. For cancer that has spread, regimens are ordered as first line, second line and so on, and a gentler drug continued after a response is called maintenance.
section1.full: The reason sequencing exists is that a tumor visible on a scan is usually accompanied by cells too small to see, so an operation that removes everything visible can leave microscopic disease behind, and a drug that circulates through the whole body is needed to reach it [[SURG-002]][[SURG-009]]. Adjuvant therapy aims at that invisible residue; its success is measured as time without recurrence, and the gain accumulates over years [[TX-L07]][[TX-L08]]. Neoadjuvant therapy puts the systemic treatment first with three intentions: to treat the same microscopic disease earlier, to shrink the tumor away from blood vessels so the surgeon is more likely to clear the margins, and to let a fast-growing cancer declare itself before a major operation that would not have helped, as happens in about one in five upfront resections [[TX-004]][[SURG-008]]. In metastatic disease, a line is defined by the evidence behind it: a first-line regimen was tested in people with no prior treatment and a second-line regimen in people whose first treatment had failed, so a trial result belongs to its line [[TX-002]][[TX-014]]. Maintenance keeps a less toxic drug running after months of combination chemotherapy, as the tablet olaparib does for people with an inherited BRCA mutation [[TX-005]]. A reader who sees 53.5 months for adjuvant mFOLFIRINOX (a modified form of the four-drug FOLFIRINOX regimen) and 11.1 months for FOLFIRINOX in metastatic disease is looking at two populations and two starting clocks, not one drug working five times better in one setting [[TX-003]][[TX-L02]].

section2.label: Why it matters here
section2.preview: In pancreatic cancer the order is set by resectability and fitness. A tumor that can be removed cleanly is usually operated on first and followed by six months of chemotherapy, because that order has the strongest evidence. A borderline resectable tumor, one touching major vessels, usually receives chemotherapy first. A locally advanced tumor is treated with chemotherapy as the main therapy, with surgery considered only if it responds. Metastatic disease is treated in lines.
section2.full: After an operation, six months of modified FOLFIRINOX lengthened median survival to 53.5 months versus 35.5 months with gemcitabine in 493 fit patients under 80 whose postoperative CA 19-9 was below 180 U/mL, with 43.2% versus 31.4% alive at five years [[TX-003]]. For borderline resectable tumors, chemotherapy first is supported by randomized trials: in the PREOPANC trial, preoperative gemcitabine-based chemoradiation (chemotherapy combined with radiation) raised the clear-margin rate among those resected from 40% to 72% and, with five years of follow-up, improved survival for everyone randomized (hazard ratio 0.73; five-year survival 20.5% versus 6.5%) [[TX-004]][[TX-L10]], and eight cycles of mFOLFIRINOX before surgery gave 70 borderline patients a median survival of 29.8 months, with 49% reaching an operation [[TX-012]]. For tumors that look clearly resectable, chemotherapy first has not improved survival in randomized trials: in the NORPACT-1 trial, 18-month survival was 60% with neoadjuvant FOLFIRINOX versus 73% with upfront surgery, and the phase 3 trials that will settle the question, A021806 and PREOPANC-3, had posted no results as of 8 Oct 2026 [[TX-L11]][[TX-013]][[SEC-TX-12]][[SEC-TX-13]]. In locally advanced disease, chemotherapy is the main treatment; in a single-arm study of gemcitabine plus nab-paclitaxel, 17 of 107 patients (16%) went on to surgery [[TX-023]]. One caution applies to every neoadjuvant figure: survival among people who reached surgery (two-year survival 72% in one trial) describes a selected group, and the figure for everyone who started (56%) is the one that applies at the beginning [[TX-011]].

research_notes.what_findings_mean: Across trials, putting chemotherapy first has helped when the baseline risk of leaving tumor at the margin is high (borderline tumors) and has not helped when it is low (resectable tumors), even though it improves the pathology report in both settings [[TX-004]][[TX-L11]][[TX-L12]]. The gap between resected-cohort survival and intention-to-treat survival in the same trial is mostly selection: people whose cancer progressed during chemotherapy never reached the operation and are missing from the resected group [[TX-011]][[TX-012]][[TX-L25]]. Adjuvant trials show the gain scaling with regimen intensity, from observation to gemcitabine to gemcitabine-capecitabine to mFOLFIRINOX, but each step was tested in progressively fitter and more selected patients, so the absolute medians are not comparable across trials [[TX-L08]][[TX-L06]][[TX-003]].
research_notes.how_studied: Sequencing questions are answered by randomized trials in which the random assignment is the order of treatments rather than the drug, and the primary measure is survival or disease-free survival counted from randomization for everyone assigned (intention to treat), which keeps the comparison fair when some patients never reach surgery [[TX-004]][[TX-013]]. Several landmark reports, including the primary PRODIGE 24 paper, NORPACT-1, ESPAC-5 and the PREOPANC long-term update, were available to this atlas only as abstracts and are cited as such [[TX-L01]][[TX-L11]][[TX-L12]][[TX-L10]]. Single-arm and registry series show what is achievable in expert hands but cannot separate the effect of a treatment from the selection of who received it [[TX-011]][[SURG-019]].

mechanism_notes.text: The survival benefit of neoadjuvant therapy may be the sum of two parts: conversion of a likely positive margin into a clear one, whose value is high in borderline tumors and low in resectable ones, and earlier systemic treatment with selection away from futile surgery, whose value depends on how many patients would otherwise never receive effective adjuvant therapy. In clearly resectable disease both parts are small and may be offset by attrition and delay before the operation, which would explain the neutral or negative results so far [[INF-TX-01]][[TX-004]][[TX-L11]][[TX-L12]]. The pending phase 3 trials, analyzed by degree of vessel contact and by adjuvant completion, could test this [[SEC-TX-12]][[SEC-TX-13]].

topics.clinical_status: A concept rather than a product. In the US as of 8 Oct 2026, adjuvant chemotherapy after resection and chemotherapy before surgery for borderline resectable disease are guideline-recommended practice; chemotherapy before surgery for clearly resectable tumors is under phase 3 testing (A021806, PREOPANC-3) with no results posted; maintenance olaparib is FDA-approved only for germline BRCA-mutated metastatic disease after at least 16 weeks of platinum chemotherapy without progression (27 Dec 2019).

glossary.definition: Treatment given before an operation, with the aim of treating hidden spread early and making the operation more likely to succeed.
Treatment given after an operation to attack microscopic cancer that may remain.
Treatment given both before and after an operation.
The main treatment of a cancer when an operation is not planned.
The position of a regimen in the order of treatments for advanced cancer, so that first line is the initial regimen and second line is the one given after it stops working.
A gentler treatment continued after a response to hold the cancer in check.
A tumor that touches or partly wraps major blood vessels so that an operation might not clear it; the word borderline describes the anatomy, not the malignancy, which is fully cancerous.
A way of analyzing a trial that counts every person as assigned, whether or not they completed the treatment.
An operation in which the pathologist finds no cancer cells at the cut edges of the removed tissue; it does not by itself mean the cancer is cured.

related.statement: The resectability category assigned at diagnosis largely decides whether treatment sequencing starts with an operation or with chemotherapy.
Treatment sequencing explains the vocabulary, and the why-chemo-first topic explains the reasoning behind neoadjuvant therapy in more detail.
Treatment sequencing places modified FOLFIRINOX after surgery as the adjuvant standard for fit patients and before surgery for borderline resectable tumors.
In the adjuvant sequence, six months of chemotherapy follows recovery from the Whipple operation.
Treatment sequencing after neoadjuvant chemotherapy depends on restaging scans that decide whether an operation goes ahead.
The presence of microscopic disease beyond what scans show is the reason treatment sequencing includes systemic chemotherapy around every operation.
Treatment sequencing in metastatic disease continues into second-line and later chemotherapy once a first regimen stops working.
Maintenance olaparib is a step in treatment sequencing for people with germline BRCA mutations whose cancer has not progressed on platinum chemotherapy.
Treatment sequencing is why survival statistics must be read with their setting and starting clock, since adjuvant and metastatic medians describe different people.

faq.q: Does getting chemotherapy before surgery mean my cancer is worse?
faq.a: Not necessarily. Chemotherapy first is the usual approach for tumors that touch major vessels, where it raised clear-margin rates from 40% to 72% among those resected and improved long-term survival in a randomized trial [[TX-004]][[TX-L10]]. For clearly resectable tumors, surgery first remains standard because trials of chemotherapy first have not shown a survival gain [[TX-L11]].

faq.q: What does 'second line' mean?
faq.a: It means the regimen given after the first one has stopped controlling the cancer. Second-line trials enroll people at that later point, so their survival figures start from a later clock and are smaller than first-line figures; in the NAPOLI-1 trial the median survival was 6.1 months with the better arm [[TX-014]].

faq.q: Why do survival numbers for the same drug differ so much between topics?
faq.a: Because they come from different settings. Adjuvant mFOLFIRINOX gave a median of 53.5 months in selected patients who had recovered from surgery, while FOLFIRINOX in metastatic disease gave 11.1 months; the drug is similar, the people and the starting point are not [[TX-003]][[TX-L02]].

topics.title: FOLFIRINOX and modified FOLFIRINOX
topics.orientation: FOLFIRINOX is a four-drug chemotherapy combination named from its parts: FOLinic acid (leucovorin), Fluorouracil, IRINotecan and OXaliplatin. It exists in an original version, tested in metastatic disease, and a modified version, tested after surgery, and the results of the two should not be swapped.

section1.label: What it does
section1.preview: The regimen pairs two drugs that damage DNA in different ways with a fluorouracil infusion that starves dividing cells of a DNA building block. Oxaliplatin forms cross-links within DNA; irinotecan traps an enzyme on DNA so strands break when the cell copies them; fluorouracil, held onto its target by leucovorin, blocks the synthesis of thymidylate. Given every two weeks, the combination shrinks tumors more often than any single drug and causes more side effects.
section1.full: Each component has a defined action. Irinotecan is converted in the body to SN-38, which binds topoisomerase I while that enzyme is cutting DNA to relieve twisting, freezes it on the cut strand and turns a reversible nick into a lethal break when the copying machinery arrives [[TX-L21]]. Oxaliplatin is a platinum compound that binds neighboring guanine bases and distorts the double helix; its signature side effect is cumulative injury to sensory nerves, beginning as cold-triggered tingling with the first cycle [[TX-022]]. Fluorouracil's active metabolite inhibits thymidylate synthase only when a folate cofactor completes a stable three-part complex, which is why leucovorin is infused alongside it [[TX-L22]]. In the original regimen, oxaliplatin 85 mg/m², irinotecan 180 mg/m² and leucovorin 400 mg/m² are given on day 1, followed by a fluorouracil bolus of 400 mg/m² and then 2,400 mg/m² infused over 46 hours through a portable pump, every 14 days [[TX-L02]]. Modified FOLFIRINOX, used in the adjuvant PRODIGE 24 trial, omits the bolus, and irinotecan was cut from 180 to 150 mg/m² after a safety analysis [[TX-003]]. The effect on a tumor is read on scans after several cycles rather than felt at once; in the metastatic trial 31.6% of tumors shrank versus 9.4% with gemcitabine [[TX-L02]]. Because the three cytotoxic drugs share bone marrow and gut lining as targets, the main acute risks are neutropenia (a shortage of infection-fighting white cells), febrile neutropenia, diarrhea and nausea, so the regimen is reserved for people with good performance status [[TX-L02]][[SUPP-006]][[SEC-SUPP-06]].

section2.label: Why it matters here
section2.preview: FOLFIRINOX produced the largest survival gain seen in a pancreatic cancer chemotherapy trial. In 342 fit patients with metastatic disease, median survival was 11.1 months versus 6.8 months with gemcitabine, with slower decline in quality of life despite more side effects. After surgery, six months of the modified regimen lengthened median survival from 35.5 to 53.5 months versus gemcitabine. These are two regimens in two settings, and each number belongs only to its own.
section2.full: The metastatic trial (PRODIGE 4/ACCORD 11, available only as an abstract) enrolled patients aged 75 or younger with ECOG performance status 0-1 (fully active, or limited only in strenuous activity) and used the original regimen with the bolus; the hazard ratio for death was 0.57, progression-free survival 6.4 versus 3.3 months, and 5.4% had febrile neutropenia [[TX-L02]]. The adjuvant trial, PRODIGE 24, randomized 493 patients aged 18 to 79 who had recovered from a macroscopically complete resection, with postoperative CA 19-9 below 180 U/mL and good performance status, to 12 cycles of modified FOLFIRINOX over 24 weeks or six cycles of gemcitabine; at a median follow-up of 69.7 months, disease-free survival was 21.4 versus 12.8 months (hazard ratio 0.66) and overall survival 53.5 versus 35.5 months (hazard ratio 0.68), with 43.2% versus 31.4% alive at five years [[TX-003]][[TX-L01]]. Only 67.2% of the mFOLFIRINOX group completed all cycles, a third received at least 80% of the planned dose and 55% stopped oxaliplatin early, yet completing the course predicted survival; grade 3-4 (severe or life-threatening) adverse events occurred in 75.9% versus 52.9% [[TX-003]][[TX-L01]]. Before surgery, eight cycles of modified FOLFIRINOX gave 70 patients with borderline resectable tumors a median survival of 29.8 months, with 49% reaching pancreatectomy [[TX-012]]. A genomic analysis of PRODIGE 24 found the adjuvant benefit confined to KRAS-mutated tumors, a finding its authors call hypothesis-generating [[GENE-024]]. No US label names FOLFIRINOX: fluorouracil is labeled for pancreatic adenocarcinoma, but oxaliplatin and irinotecan carry colorectal indications only [[SEC-TX-09]].

action_note.heading: When to call the care team now
action_note.text: A temperature of 38.0 °C (100.4 °F) or higher during FOLFIRINOX can be the only sign of infection with dangerously low white cells and needs same-day evaluation, with antibiotics within an hour of arrival [[SEC-SUPP-03]][[SEC-SUPP-01]]. Diarrhea from irinotecan should be reported at the first loose stools rather than waited out; the label for liposomal irinotecan, which shares the same active metabolite, directs loperamide for late-onset diarrhea of any severity and withholding the drug for moderate or worse diarrhea [[SEC-SUPP-11]]. Severe mouth sores, diarrhea or weakness within days of the first cycle can signal an inherited inability to clear fluorouracil and warrant an immediate call [[SEC-GENE-02]].

research_notes.what_findings_mean: The two FOLFIRINOX trials answer different questions, one about extending life in metastatic disease and one about preventing recurrence after surgery, so their numbers cannot be combined or compared [[TX-L02]][[TX-003]]. The adjuvant result came from selected patients (recovered from surgery, CA 19-9 below 180, under 80 years), so the 53.5-month median overstates what unselected registries show, while the reduced dose intensity most patients actually received suggests the benefit does not depend on full doses [[TX-003]]. Febrile neutropenia affected one in five in a Korean cohort, mostly in the first four cycles, with carriers of a slow-metabolizing UGT1A1 gene variant, which impairs clearance of irinotecan's active form, at about four times the risk [[SUPP-006]]. The NAPOLI-3 trial compared NALIRIFOX, not FOLFIRINOX, with gemcitabine/nab-paclitaxel, so no phase 3 trial has set FOLFIRINOX against that doublet head to head [[TX-002]].
research_notes.how_studied: Both pivotal trials were open-label randomized phase 3 studies with overall survival (metastatic) or disease-free survival (adjuvant) as the primary endpoint, analyzed by intention to treat [[TX-003]][[TX-L02]]. The primary PRODIGE 4 and PRODIGE 24 papers were accessible to this atlas only as abstracts; the five-year PRODIGE 24 report, available in full, supplies the figures used here [[TX-L02]][[TX-L01]][[TX-003]]. The genomic substudy sequenced 317 of 350 tumors and tested formal treatment-by-biomarker interactions, which guards against reading chance subgroup differences as real, although its panel could not detect gene deletions [[GENE-024]]. The pharmacology of each component rests on older colorectal trials and biochemistry available only as abstracts [[TX-L18]][[TX-L19]][[TX-L20]][[TX-L21]].

mechanism_notes.text: The absence of adjuvant mFOLFIRINOX benefit in KRAS wild-type (unmutated) tumors may reflect a different biology, since such tumors are often driven by gene fusions or other alterations rather than the KRAS pathway. The interaction was statistically significant, but the subgroup was small and the authors present it as a hypothesis, not a reason to change treatment [[GENE-024]].

Because only a third of PRODIGE 24 patients received at least 80% of the planned dose and 55% stopped oxaliplatin early, yet the hazard ratio for death was still 0.68, a tolerated, reduced-intensity course appears to retain most of the regimen's benefit, and completing the planned months seems to matter more than delivering every milligram [[TX-003]]. Oxaliplatin's cumulative neuropathy is the usual reason for the reductions [[TX-022]].

topics.clinical_status: Not FDA-labeled as a regimen in the US as of 8 Oct 2026: fluorouracil is labeled for pancreatic adenocarcinoma, while oxaliplatin and irinotecan labels list colorectal indications only, so their use here is guideline-based and off-label. Guideline-recommended first-line option for fit patients with metastatic disease (original regimen), the standard adjuvant regimen for fit patients after resection (modified regimen), and a listed option before surgery for borderline resectable disease.

glossary.definition: A four-drug chemotherapy combination of folinic acid (leucovorin), fluorouracil, irinotecan and oxaliplatin given every two weeks.
A version of FOLFIRINOX that drops the fluorouracil bolus and often lowers the irinotecan dose to make it easier to tolerate.
A dose of drug injected over a few minutes rather than infused over hours.
A small portable device that delivers fluorouracil slowly over 46 hours through a central line while the person is at home.
A low count of neutrophils, the white blood cells that fight bacterial infection.
Fever occurring while neutrophils are low, treated as an emergency because infection can spread quickly.
An enzyme that cuts and reseals one DNA strand to relieve twisting during copying; irinotecan traps it mid-cut.
A trial statistic comparing the rate of an event, such as death, between two groups over time, where 0.68 means roughly a third lower rate.
A simple scale of how much a person can do day to day, used to judge fitness for intensive treatment.
The share of the planned drug dose over the planned time that a person actually received.

related.statement: FOLFIRINOX contains a 46-hour fluorouracil infusion with leucovorin as its backbone.
FOLFIRINOX contains oxaliplatin, whose cumulative nerve injury is the usual reason the drug is stopped early.
FOLFIRINOX contains irinotecan, the component responsible for much of its diarrhea and neutropenia.
FOLFIRINOX was tested against gemcitabine in both its metastatic and adjuvant trials.
NALIRIFOX replaces FOLFIRINOX's irinotecan with a liposomal form and uses a lower oxaliplatin dose, so it is a relative rather than the same regimen.
FOLFIRINOX appears at three points in treatment sequencing: first line for metastatic disease, before surgery for borderline tumors, and after surgery as modified FOLFIRINOX.
Inherited UGT1A1 and DPYD variants modulate how safely a person can receive FOLFIRINOX's irinotecan and fluorouracil.
FOLFIRINOX's oxaliplatin causes the numbness and tingling described in the neuropathy topic.
FOLFIRINOX is classed as a high-risk regimen for febrile neutropenia, the subject of the fever and infection topic.
Growth-factor support and dose adjustments are the tools used to keep people on FOLFIRINOX through neutropenia.
In the PRODIGE 24 genomic analysis, adjuvant mFOLFIRINOX benefit was present in KRAS-mutated tumors and absent in KRAS wild-type tumors.

faq.q: Is modified FOLFIRINOX a weaker version?
faq.a: It drops the fluorouracil bolus and sometimes lowers the irinotecan dose to reduce side effects. In the adjuvant trial the modified regimen still cut the risk of death by about a third compared with gemcitabine, even though most patients received reduced doses, so tolerability rather than maximum dose is what the modification trades [[TX-003]].

faq.q: Why do I go home with a pump?
faq.a: Fluorouracil works best when it is in the body continuously while cells divide, so it is infused over 46 hours through a portable pump instead of injected once. In the colorectal trial that established the schedule, infusion doubled response and halved severe toxicity compared with bolus dosing [[TX-L19]].

faq.q: Can older people have FOLFIRINOX?
faq.a: The metastatic trial enrolled people up to age 75 and the adjuvant trial up to 79, all with good performance status, so the results apply to fit people in those ranges [[TX-L02]][[TX-003]]. Fitness, organ function and recovery from surgery matter more than age alone, which is a conversation for the care team.

topics.title: Gemcitabine plus nab-paclitaxel
topics.orientation: Gemcitabine plus nab-paclitaxel, often written GnP or gem/Abraxane, is a two-drug chemotherapy given on a weekly schedule. It is one of the standard first-line treatments for metastatic pancreatic cancer and is often chosen when FOLFIRINOX would be too demanding.

section1.label: What it does
section1.preview: Nab-paclitaxel is paclitaxel bound to albumin, the main blood protein, which lets the drug be given without the solvent that made older paclitaxel hard to tolerate. Paclitaxel locks microtubules, the scaffolding a cell uses to pull its chromosomes apart, so dividing cells stall and die. Gemcitabine is a counterfeit DNA building block. Given together on days 1, 8 and 15 of a 28-day cycle, they shrink tumors more often than gemcitabine alone.
section1.full: The combination emerged from a phase 1/2 study in which the highest tolerated dose of nab-paclitaxel with gemcitabine was 125 mg/m², the dose used ever since [[TX-L23]]. The first explanation for why it worked, that albumin-bound paclitaxel was drawn into the tumor's fibrous stroma by the protein SPARC, stripped the stroma and let more gemcitabine in, came from human tumors grown in mice, where tumor gemcitabine rose 2.8-fold [[TX-L23]]. Later work in mice with intact, native tumors did not reproduce it: nab-paclitaxel killed the tumor's own cancer cells and raised the active form of gemcitabine by lowering cytidine deaminase, the enzyme that inactivates gemcitabine, without changing stromal content, collagen or blood vessels [[TX-008]]. SPARC made no difference to drug delivery at therapeutic doses in SPARC-deficient mice [[TX-009]], and SPARC levels in trial patients' tumors did not predict who benefited [[TX-L17]]. The mechanism in people remains unmeasured. What the albumin formulation clearly does is pharmaceutical: it allowed a fourfold higher dose than solvent-based paclitaxel in mice, with comparable tumor drug levels at equal doses [[TX-009]]. The side effects follow from the two drugs' actions on dividing cells and on nerves: grade 3 or worse (severe) neutropenia, a shortage of infection-fighting white cells, in 38%, fatigue in 17% and peripheral neuropathy in 17% of trial patients, versus 27%, 7% and 1% with gemcitabine alone; severe neuropathy improved to mild in a median of 29 days once the drug was paused [[TX-001]]. Hair loss is expected with paclitaxel.

section2.label: Why it matters here
section2.preview: In 861 previously untreated patients with metastatic pancreatic cancer, adding nab-paclitaxel to gemcitabine raised median survival from 6.7 to 8.5 months and the chance of being alive at one year from 22% to 35%. The FDA approved the combination for first-line metastatic disease on 6 September 2013. A trial of it after surgery did not meet its primary goal, and in locally advanced disease it is used off-label on guideline support.
section2.full: The MPACT trial randomized patients with a Karnofsky performance status of 70 or higher (a fitness scale on which 70 means able to care for oneself but not to work); the hazard ratio for death was 0.72, progression-free survival 5.5 versus 3.7 months, and 23% versus 7% of tumors responded [[TX-001]]. A fall in CA 19-9 of 90% or more occurred in 31% versus 14% of patients and marked a group with a median survival of 13.5 months [[TX-001]]. In the adjuvant APACT trial of 866 resected patients, the primary endpoint, disease-free survival judged by blinded radiologists, was 19.4 versus 18.8 months with gemcitabine alone (hazard ratio 0.88, not significant), even though investigators' assessments and a later survival analysis (41.8 versus 37.7 months) favored the combination; the label has no adjuvant indication [[TX-006]]. In a single-arm study of 107 patients with unresectable locally advanced disease, median survival was 18.8 months and 17 (16%) went on to surgery, seven with clear margins [[TX-023]]. In the NAPOLI-3 trial it was the comparator and was beaten by NALIRIFOX on median survival, 9.2 versus 11.1 months, with a different toxicity profile: more grade 3-4 neutropenia (25% versus 14%) and neuropathy (6% versus 3%) but far less diarrhea (5% versus 20%) [[TX-002]]. In 2026, adding Tumor Treating Fields, a wearable device that delivers alternating electric fields, to the combination in locally advanced disease was approved on a two-month gain in median survival [[TX-010]][[SEC-TX-11]]. Its practical appeal is weekly dosing without a home pump and a lower fitness bar than FOLFIRINOX, at the price of neuropathy.

action_note.heading: When to call the care team now
action_note.text: A temperature of 38.0 °C (100.4 °F) or higher during this regimen can be the only sign of infection while neutrophils are low and needs same-day evaluation, with antibiotics within an hour of arrival [[SEC-SUPP-03]][[SEC-SUPP-01]]. New numbness that affects buttoning clothes, walking or feeling the floor should be reported before the next dose: no drug prevents chemotherapy neuropathy, dose adjustment or a pause is the main tool, and in the pivotal trial severe neuropathy eased to mild within a median of 29 days once nab-paclitaxel was held [[SEC-SUPP-07]][[TX-001]].

research_notes.what_findings_mean: The survival gain is real but modest, about 1.8 months in the median and 13 percentage points at one year, and it was measured in people fit enough to meet a performance-status floor, so it describes the trial population rather than everyone with metastatic disease [[TX-001]]. The adjuvant trial is a lesson in how endpoints are counted: blinded radiologists censored about half of patients at the start of new therapy, investigators used CA 19-9 and clinical information, and the two readings disagreed enough to flip the result from negative to positive, which is why the primary analysis stands and the survival difference is treated as descriptive [[TX-006]]. The stroma-stripping story that accompanied the drug's launch is not supported by the mouse models with native tumors or by the trial's own biomarker analysis [[TX-008]][[TX-009]][[TX-L17]].
research_notes.how_studied: MPACT was an open-label randomized phase 3 trial with overall survival by intention to treat as the primary endpoint and tumor response judged by independent review, which limits the bias of an unblinded design [[TX-001]]. The mechanism studies used genetically engineered mice whose tumors develop their own stroma, measured drug metabolites inside tumors by mass spectrometry, and deleted SPARC genetically to test whether it mattered [[TX-008]][[TX-009]]. The locally advanced study, LAPACT, was single-arm, so its 18.8-month median and 16% conversion to surgery show what happened to a selected group rather than what the drug added [[TX-023]]. The phase 1/2 origin study and the SPARC biomarker analysis were available only as abstracts [[TX-L23]][[TX-L17]].

mechanism_notes.text: In mice, nab-paclitaxel lowers cytidine deaminase in tumor cells, so less gemcitabine is destroyed and more of its active triphosphate accumulates, which would explain why the combination kills tumor cells where either drug alone does not. The pharmacology is coherent and was shown directly in tumor tissue, but it has not been measured in patients, so it remains the best-supported rather than a proven explanation of the clinical benefit [[TX-008]][[TX-001]].

The failure of the adjuvant trial's primary endpoint alongside a positive survival signal may reflect the difficulty of detecting recurrence on scans after pancreatic surgery, where scar and reconstruction obscure small lesions; investigators who also used CA 19-9 called recurrence earlier. If so, the regimen may have a real but unproven adjuvant effect, which does not change its label [[TX-006]].

topics.clinical_status: Approved in the US as of 8 Oct 2026 for first-line treatment of metastatic adenocarcinoma of the pancreas in combination with gemcitabine (Abraxane, 6 Sep 2013). No adjuvant or locally advanced indication; use in those settings is guideline-based and off-label. Tumor Treating Fields added to this regimen for locally advanced disease received FDA device approval announced 12 Feb 2026.

glossary.definition: Paclitaxel bound to nanoparticles of the blood protein albumin, which replaces the castor-oil solvent of older paclitaxel.
Protein filaments that form a cell's internal scaffolding and pull chromosomes apart during division; paclitaxel freezes them.
A protein in tumor stroma once thought to pull albumin-bound drugs into the tumor, a role that later studies did not confirm.
The enzyme that inactivates gemcitabine; lower levels mean more active drug inside a cell.
A 0 to 100 scale of day-to-day function, where 70 means able to care for oneself but unable to work.
The time after surgery during which no recurrence is detected and the person is alive.
Nerve damage felt as numbness, tingling or pain, usually starting in the fingers and toes.

related.statement: Gemcitabine plus nab-paclitaxel contains gemcitabine, whose active form rises inside tumor cells when nab-paclitaxel lowers the enzyme that destroys it.
Gemcitabine plus nab-paclitaxel was the comparator that NALIRIFOX beat by 1.9 months in median survival in NAPOLI-3.
Gemcitabine plus nab-paclitaxel and FOLFIRINOX are the two main first-line choices for metastatic disease, and no phase 3 trial has compared them directly.
Tumor Treating Fields were approved in 2026 as an addition to gemcitabine plus nab-paclitaxel in locally advanced disease.
The stroma-stripping explanation for gemcitabine plus nab-paclitaxel is one of the lessons from stroma-directed treatments, because mouse and trial data did not support it.
Gemcitabine plus nab-paclitaxel caused grade 3 or worse neuropathy in 17% of trial patients, the subject of the neuropathy topic.
Response to gemcitabine plus nab-paclitaxel is tracked by CA 19-9, where a 90% fall marked a group with longer survival.
Gemcitabine plus nab-paclitaxel is a first-line regimen in treatment sequencing for metastatic disease and a guideline option for locally advanced disease.

faq.q: Is this regimen easier than FOLFIRINOX?
faq.a: It avoids the home infusion pump and the irinotecan diarrhea, and the trial allowed a lower fitness level, but it causes more neuropathy and neutropenia than NALIRIFOX did in a direct comparison [[TX-002]]. Which is easier depends on which side effects a person can better live with.

faq.q: Does nab-paclitaxel break down the tumor's scar tissue?
faq.a: That was the original idea, but mice with native tumors showed no change in stroma, and SPARC levels in trial patients did not predict benefit [[TX-008]][[TX-L17]]. The better-supported explanation is that nab-paclitaxel raises the active form of gemcitabine inside tumor cells [[TX-008]].

faq.q: Why was it not approved after surgery?
faq.a: The adjuvant trial's primary endpoint, recurrence judged by blinded radiologists, did not differ (19.4 versus 18.8 months), so the later survival difference is treated as descriptive and the label covers metastatic disease only [[TX-006]].

topics.title: NALIRIFOX
topics.orientation: NALIRIFOX is a four-drug regimen that replaces the irinotecan of FOLFIRINOX with a liposome-wrapped form (Onivyde) and uses a lower dose of oxaliplatin. It is the most recently approved first-line chemotherapy for metastatic pancreatic cancer.

section1.label: What it does
section1.preview: Liposomal irinotecan packages the drug inside microscopic fat-bubble carriers that circulate longer than free irinotecan and release its active metabolite, SN-38, gradually. SN-38 traps the enzyme topoisomerase I on DNA so strands break when cells divide. NALIRIFOX combines it with oxaliplatin, which cross-links DNA, and a 46-hour fluorouracil infusion with leucovorin, given on days 1 and 15 of a 28-day cycle.
section1.full: The regimen in the pivotal trial was liposomal irinotecan 50 mg/m², oxaliplatin 60 mg/m², leucovorin 400 mg/m² and fluorouracil 2,400 mg/m² over 46 hours, every two weeks [[TX-002]]. Three differences from classic FOLFIRINOX matter: the irinotecan is liposomal, oxaliplatin is 60 rather than 85 mg/m², and there is no fluorouracil bolus, so the trial was not a test of FOLFIRINOX under another name [[TX-002]]. Irinotecan acts as all drugs in its camptothecin family do: the drug does not bind DNA directly but stabilizes the complex in which topoisomerase I is attached to the cut strand, blocking the rejoining step [[TX-L21]]. The lower oxaliplatin dose is a deliberate trade against nerve damage, which rises with the total dose received [[TX-022]]. Irinotecan's dose-limiting toxicities are diarrhea and neutropenia (a shortage of infection-fighting white cells), both shaped by how fast a person clears SN-38 through the enzyme UGT1A1; the US label sets reduced starting doses for people who inherit two copies of the slow UGT1A1*28 variant [[GENE-018]][[SEC-TX-02]]. In the trial, grade 3-4 (severe) diarrhea occurred in 20% of patients versus 5% with gemcitabine/nab-paclitaxel, hypokalemia (low potassium, usually from diarrhea) in 15% versus 4% and nausea in 12% versus 3%, while neutropenia (14% versus 25%), anemia (11% versus 17%) and peripheral neuropathy (3% versus 6%) were less frequent; treatment-related deaths were 2% in each arm [[TX-002]]. The label carries a boxed warning for severe neutropenia and severe diarrhea and specifies loperamide for late-onset diarrhea and atropine for the early cholinergic form, with cramping and sweating, that can occur during the infusion [[SEC-SUPP-11]].

section2.label: Why it matters here
section2.preview: In the NAPOLI-3 trial, 770 previously untreated patients with metastatic pancreatic cancer were randomized to NALIRIFOX or gemcitabine plus nab-paclitaxel. Median survival was 11.1 versus 9.2 months (hazard ratio 0.83), and 45.6% versus 39.5% were alive at one year. The FDA approved the regimen for first-line metastatic disease on 13 February 2024. The trial had no upper age limit but required good performance status.
section2.full: Enrollment ran from February 2020 to August 2021 at 187 community and academic sites in 18 countries; patients had ECOG performance status 0-1 (fully active, or limited only in strenuous activity), and the primary endpoint was overall survival by intention to treat after 543 deaths [[TX-002]]. Progression-free survival was 7.4 versus 5.6 months (hazard ratio 0.69); 42% (160 of 383) of tumors responded versus 36% (140 of 387), a difference that was not statistically significant, and responses lasted a median of 7.3 versus 5.0 months [[TX-002]]. The upper confidence limit of the survival hazard ratio was 0.99, so the benefit, while real, is modest, about 1.9 months in the median, and the choice between the regimens turns largely on which side-effect profile a person can better tolerate: gastrointestinal with NALIRIFOX, hematologic and neurological with gemcitabine/nab-paclitaxel [[TX-002]]. The published report gave no quality-of-life results, and about half of each arm (51% versus 54%) went on to further treatment [[TX-002]]. Because its components are the same drug classes as FOLFIRINOX, the medians of the two pivotal trials look alike (11.1 months in both), but the trials had different comparators, eras and age limits, and the FOLFIRINOX figure comes from a trial report available only as an abstract, so the two have never been compared and are not interchangeable [[TX-L02]][[TX-002]]. Liposomal irinotecan was first approved in October 2015 for use after gemcitabine-based treatment, and the 2024 approval extended it to first line; it is not indicated on its own [[SEC-TX-02]].

action_note.heading: When to call the care team now
action_note.text: Diarrhea on NALIRIFOX is a label-level warning, not a nuisance: the Onivyde label directs loperamide at the first episode of late-onset diarrhea and withholding the drug for moderate or worse diarrhea, and it warns against use with a bowel obstruction [[SEC-SUPP-11]]. A temperature of 38.0 °C (100.4 °F) or higher needs same-day evaluation because neutropenia can be silent until infection takes hold [[SEC-SUPP-03]][[SEC-SUPP-01]]. Cramping, sweating or watery stools during or just after the infusion are the early cholinergic form and should be reported to the infusion nurse at once [[SEC-SUPP-11]].

research_notes.what_findings_mean: The NAPOLI-3 trial established NALIRIFOX as a first-line option by beating the regimen that is easiest to deliver, not by beating FOLFIRINOX, so it does not settle which triplet is better [[TX-002]]. The survival gain is near the lower edge of what the trial was designed to detect (it was powered for a hazard ratio of 0.75 and found 0.83), the response rates did not differ significantly, and the toxicity trade is not obviously favorable, which is why the regimens are presented as alternatives rather than a ranking [[TX-002]]. The trial's lack of an upper age limit is relevant to older fit patients, who were excluded from the original FOLFIRINOX trial [[TX-002]][[TX-L02]].
research_notes.how_studied: NAPOLI-3 was an open-label randomized phase 3 trial stratified by region, performance status and liver metastases, with overall survival by intention to treat as the primary endpoint and 90% power for a hazard ratio of 0.75; progression-free survival was investigator-assessed, which an open-label design can bias [[TX-002]]. Toxicity was recorded in the 749 patients who received treatment, so the adverse-event percentages have a slightly different denominator from the efficacy figures [[TX-002]]. The mechanism of the irinotecan component rests on biochemistry available only as an abstract [[TX-L21]], and the UGT1A1 safety evidence comes from a retrospective Dutch cohort of 779 patients, about half with pancreatic cancer [[GENE-018]].

mechanism_notes.text: The lower neuropathy rate with NALIRIFOX (3% versus 6% grade 3-4) is most plausibly a dose effect: the regimen uses oxaliplatin at 60 mg/m² rather than the 85 mg/m² of FOLFIRINOX, and oxaliplatin's chronic sensory neuropathy scales with cumulative dose in colorectal patients. That gain in nerve safety is paid for in diarrhea, which comes from the irinotecan component [[TX-002]][[TX-022]][[TX-L21]].

topics.clinical_status: Approved in the US as of 8 Oct 2026: Onivyde (irinotecan liposome) with oxaliplatin, fluorouracil and leucovorin for first-line treatment of metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma (13 Feb 2024). Onivyde with fluorouracil and leucovorin has been approved after gemcitabine-based therapy since 22 Oct 2015. It is not indicated as a single agent, and there is no adjuvant, neoadjuvant or locally advanced indication.

glossary.definition: A microscopic bubble of fat molecules used to carry a drug through the bloodstream and release it slowly.
The active form of irinotecan, made in the body, that traps topoisomerase I on DNA.
An enzyme that cuts and reseals one DNA strand to relieve twisting during copying; irinotecan traps it mid-cut.
A low blood potassium level, which on this regimen usually follows diarrhea and can affect heart rhythm.
Cramping, sweating and loose stools during or just after an irinotecan infusion, treated with atropine.
The most prominent safety warning the FDA places on a drug label.
The enzyme that clears SN-38; people who inherit slow versions reach higher drug levels at a standard dose.

related.statement: NALIRIFOX contains irinotecan in its liposomal form, which circulates longer than the free drug used in FOLFIRINOX.
NALIRIFOX contains oxaliplatin at 60 mg/m², a lower dose than FOLFIRINOX's 85 mg/m², which likely explains its lower neuropathy rate.
NALIRIFOX contains a 46-hour fluorouracil infusion with leucovorin and no bolus.
NALIRIFOX beat gemcitabine plus nab-paclitaxel by 1.9 months in median survival in NAPOLI-3, with a different side-effect profile.
NALIRIFOX differs from FOLFIRINOX in its irinotecan form, oxaliplatin dose and absence of a bolus, and the two have never been compared head to head.
The liposomal irinotecan in NALIRIFOX was first approved in 2015 for second-line use with fluorouracil and leucovorin after gemcitabine-based therapy.
Inherited UGT1A1 variants modulate the neutropenia and diarrhea risk of NALIRIFOX's irinotecan component.
NALIRIFOX caused grade 3-4 diarrhea in 20% of trial patients, the kind of bowel change described in the nausea and bowel topic.

faq.q: Is NALIRIFOX better than FOLFIRINOX?
faq.a: No trial has compared them. NALIRIFOX was tested against gemcitabine plus nab-paclitaxel, and FOLFIRINOX against gemcitabine alone, in different years and populations, so their similar 11.1-month medians cannot be read as equivalence or superiority [[TX-002]][[TX-L02]].

faq.q: Why is the oxaliplatin dose lower?
faq.a: The regimen uses 60 mg/m² rather than FOLFIRINOX's 85 mg/m², and oxaliplatin nerve damage rises with the total dose, which fits the lower severe neuropathy rate seen in the trial (3% versus 6% with the comparator) [[TX-002]][[TX-022]].

faq.q: Is Onivyde the same as regular irinotecan?
faq.a: It is the same drug wrapped in liposomes, which keeps it circulating longer and releases the active metabolite gradually. Its labeled uses are specific: with oxaliplatin, fluorouracil and leucovorin first line, or with fluorouracil and leucovorin after gemcitabine, and never alone [[SEC-TX-02]].

topics.title: Second-line and later chemotherapy
topics.orientation: When a first chemotherapy stops controlling the cancer, the next treatment is called second line. What is available depends on what was given first, on how well a person is at that point, and, since August 2026, on a RAS-targeted tablet that was tested in exactly this setting.

section1.label: What it does
section1.preview: Second-line therapy uses the drugs the cancer has not yet met. After a gemcitabine-based first line, the proven chemotherapy option is liposomal irinotecan with fluorouracil and leucovorin; oxaliplatin-based regimens have conflicting results. After FOLFIRINOX or NALIRIFOX, a gemcitabine-based regimen is the usual next step, though that order rests on drug logic rather than on a randomized trial of its own. Daraxonrasib, a RAS inhibitor, was approved in 2026 for previously treated metastatic disease.
section1.full: The logic rests on cross-resistance: a cancer that has grown through one class of drug is less likely to respond to it again, so the second line switches class. In the NAPOLI-1 trial, 417 patients whose metastatic disease had progressed after gemcitabine-based treatment were randomized; liposomal irinotecan 80 mg/m² with fluorouracil 2,400 mg/m² over 46 hours and leucovorin every two weeks gave a median survival of 6.1 months versus 4.2 months with fluorouracil and leucovorin alone (hazard ratio 0.67), progression-free survival of 3.1 versus 1.5 months and tumor shrinkage in 7.7% versus 0.8%; liposomal irinotecan alone (4.9 months) did no better than fluorouracil/leucovorin, so the label requires the combination [[TX-014]][[SEC-TX-02]]. Oxaliplatin after gemcitabine has two randomized trials pointing opposite ways: the CONKO-003 trial found that OFF (oxaliplatin, folinic acid, fluorouracil) lengthened median survival from 3.3 to 5.9 months in 168 patients, while the PANCREOX trial found that mFOLFOX6 (oxaliplatin with infusional fluorouracil and leucovorin) gave no progression-free benefit and shorter survival than infusional fluorouracil/leucovorin (6.1 versus 9.9 months) in 108 patients, with 20% withdrawing for toxicity versus 2% [[TX-L04]][[TX-L05]]. In a 61-patient Korean trial, irinotecan- and oxaliplatin-based doublets after gemcitabine gave similar results, about four months median survival [[TX-015]]. Daraxonrasib, an oral inhibitor of RAS proteins, roughly doubled median survival against chemotherapy in 500 previously treated patients (13.2 versus 6.7 months, hazard ratio 0.40) and was approved on 26 August 2026 for metastatic disease after at least one prior systemic therapy [[RAS-033]][[SEC-RAS-01]].

section2.label: Why it matters here
section2.preview: Second-line results are measured from a later starting point, in people who have already been through months of treatment, so chemotherapy medians of four to six months cannot be set beside first-line figures. What a person received first determines what remains, fitness at the time of progression matters more than the regimen name, and a handful of molecular findings open doors that chemotherapy does not.
section2.full: US approvals are keyed to the prior treatment: liposomal irinotecan's 2015 indication is specifically after gemcitabine-based therapy, and daraxonrasib's 2026 indication is after at least one prior systemic therapy, whichever it was [[SEC-TX-02]][[SEC-RAS-02]]. The PANCREOX trial is the caution that a more intensive regimen can shorten life when toxicity drives people off treatment and leaves no room for a third line, in a trial that admitted people with ECOG performance status 2, who are up and about but unable to work [[TX-L05]]. Molecular results become decisive here: pembrolizumab for the roughly 1-2% of pancreatic cancers with mismatch-repair deficiency (a DNA-repair defect that makes tumors visible to the immune system) produced responses in 4 of 22 patients in the label's trial data [[TX-016]][[SEC-TX-04]]; zenocutuzumab for NRG1 gene fusions in 15 of 36 previously treated patients [[TX-020]]; selpercatinib for RET fusions in 6 of 11 [[TX-019]]; and for people with an inherited BRCA mutation whose cancer has not progressed after 16 weeks of platinum chemotherapy, olaparib maintenance delays the next line rather than being one [[TX-005]]. Denominators matter: the NAPOLI-1 combination arm had 117 patients and its 1.9-month gain was measured in a population with median survival under six months, so it shows that active treatment helps fit people at this stage, not what any one person should expect [[TX-014]]. The daraxonrasib trial defined its main endpoints in the 92% of patients with RAS G12 mutations, yet the indication carries no mutation requirement, a gap worth asking about [[RAS-033]][[SEC-RAS-01]]. The questions at progression are fitness for another regimen, whether molecular testing has been done, and whether a trial is open.

action_note.heading: When to call the care team now
action_note.text: Every second-line chemotherapy here lowers white cells, so a temperature of 38.0 °C (100.4 °F) or higher needs same-day evaluation, with antibiotics within an hour of arrival [[SEC-SUPP-03]][[SEC-SUPP-01]]. On liposomal irinotecan, the label directs loperamide at the first episode of late-onset diarrhea and withholding the drug for moderate or worse diarrhea, and it must not be given with a bowel obstruction [[SEC-SUPP-11]]. Oxaliplatin-containing second-line regimens bring cold-triggered tingling that the label says to manage by avoiding cold exposure and reporting persistent numbness [[SEC-SUPP-12]].

research_notes.what_findings_mean: The randomized evidence covers one direction only, treatment after gemcitabine-based therapy; the reverse sequence, a gemcitabine regimen after a fluorouracil-based triplet, is practiced on pharmacological logic and the trials' reports of subsequent therapy rather than on a trial of its own [[TX-014]][[TX-002]][[TX-003]]. The oxaliplatin contradiction is best read as a warning about populations and schedules: CONKO-003 enrolled people after gemcitabine monotherapy, while PANCREOX included less fit patients and lost a fifth of the oxaliplatin arm to toxicity, so the same drug class produced opposite results [[TX-L04]][[TX-L05]]. Daraxonrasib's hazard ratio of 0.40 is far larger than any chemotherapy effect in this setting, but the trial was open-label and its full report is available only as an abstract [[RAS-033]].
research_notes.how_studied: Second-line trials randomize people at the moment of progression and count survival from that point, which is why their medians are short and why comparisons with first-line trials are invalid [[TX-014]][[TX-L04]]. NAPOLI-1 is available only as an abstract and registry results, and its combination arm was added by amendment part-way through, a design feature that can introduce timing differences between arms [[TX-014]]. CONKO-003 and PANCREOX are available only as abstracts, as is the daraxonrasib phase 3 report, supplemented by the FDA approval page [[TX-L04]][[TX-L05]][[RAS-033]][[SEC-RAS-01]]. The small Korean trial used a selection design that picks a regimen for further study rather than proving one superior [[TX-015]].

mechanism_notes.text: The opposite results of CONKO-003 and PANCREOX are most plausibly explained by who was enrolled and what followed rather than by oxaliplatin itself: PANCREOX admitted performance status 2, lost 20% of its oxaliplatin arm to toxicity against 2% of controls, and only 7% versus 25% received any later treatment, so the control arm's unusually long 9.9-month survival partly reflects access to a third line that the oxaliplatin arm lost [[TX-L04]][[TX-L05]][[TX-022]].

topics.clinical_status: In the US as of 8 Oct 2026: liposomal irinotecan (Onivyde) with fluorouracil and leucovorin is approved for metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma after gemcitabine-based therapy (22 Oct 2015); daraxonrasib (Rasonque) is approved for metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma after at least one prior systemic therapy or for people who cannot take multi-drug therapy (26 Aug 2026); pembrolizumab, zenocutuzumab, selpercatinib and larotrectinib hold approvals tied to specific molecular findings after prior therapy. Oxaliplatin-based (OFF, mFOLFOX) and gemcitabine-based second-line regimens are guideline-listed, off-label uses.

glossary.definition: The treatment given after the first regimen has stopped controlling the cancer.
Growth of the cancer or appearance of new spots on scans, or clear clinical worsening, that marks the end of a regimen's usefulness.
The tendency of a cancer that has resisted one drug to resist others that work the same way.
A second-line regimen of oxaliplatin, folinic acid (leucovorin) and fluorouracil tested in the CONKO-003 trial.
A two-weekly regimen of oxaliplatin with infusional fluorouracil and leucovorin, borrowed from colorectal cancer.
Irinotecan wrapped in microscopic fat bubbles that keep it circulating longer, sold as Onivyde.
A drug that blocks the RAS proteins whose mutant form drives most pancreatic cancers.
A gentler treatment continued after a response to hold the cancer in check, rather than a new line started after progression.

related.statement: The liposomal irinotecan used in second-line therapy after gemcitabine is the same drug that forms part of first-line NALIRIFOX.
After a fluorouracil-based first line, gemcitabine plus nab-paclitaxel is a usual second-line choice, though without a randomized trial of that sequence.
Second-line regimens after gemcitabine all contain fluorouracil with leucovorin, either alone, with oxaliplatin, or with liposomal irinotecan.
Oxaliplatin-containing second-line regimens (OFF, mFOLFOX) have one positive and one negative randomized trial.
Second-line and later metastatic disease is the setting in which daraxonrasib was tested and approved in August 2026.
Second-line chemotherapy is the step in treatment sequencing that follows progression on a first-line regimen.
Second-line options beyond chemotherapy depend on molecular testing for mismatch-repair deficiency, gene fusions and BRCA mutations.
Pembrolizumab is a second-line option for the 1-2% of pancreatic cancers with mismatch-repair deficiency.
Drugs for gene fusions are second-line options for the rare pancreatic cancers that carry NRG1, RET or NTRK fusions.
Second-line progression is the point at which a clinical trial is most often the best available option.

faq.q: What comes after FOLFIRINOX stops working?
faq.a: Usually a gemcitabine-based regimen, because the cancer has not yet met that drug class, but that order rests on drug logic rather than on a randomized trial of its own; the trials of second-line treatment all enrolled people after gemcitabine [[TX-014]][[TX-L04]]. Since August 2026, daraxonrasib is approved for metastatic disease after any prior systemic therapy [[SEC-RAS-01]].

faq.q: Why are second-line survival numbers so much lower?
faq.a: They start counting at progression, after months of treatment and in people who are less well, so a median of 6.1 months in NAPOLI-1 is not comparable with the 11.1 months of first-line trials [[TX-014]]. The right comparison is with the trial's own control arm, which gave 4.2 months.

faq.q: Should I have molecular testing before deciding?
faq.a: Yes if it has not been done, because a mismatch-repair-deficient tumor, an NRG1 or RET fusion, or an inherited BRCA mutation each opens a treatment with its own approval, found in only a few percent of patients but decisive for them [[TX-016]][[TX-020]][[TX-005]].

topics.title: Fluorouracil and leucovorin
topics.orientation: Fluorouracil (5-FU) is the oldest drug still central to pancreatic cancer chemotherapy, and leucovorin is the helper that makes it work. Together they form the backbone of FOLFIRINOX, NALIRIFOX, OFF and the second-line liposomal irinotecan regimen; capecitabine is a tablet that becomes fluorouracil inside the body.

section1.label: What it does
section1.preview: Fluorouracil is a counterfeit version of uracil, a building block of RNA, with a fluorine atom where a hydrogen should be. Inside cells it is converted to an active form, FdUMP, which jams thymidylate synthase, the enzyme that makes the DNA base thymine. The jam holds only when a folate cofactor is present to complete a three-part complex, and leucovorin supplies that cofactor. Without thymidylate, dividing cells cannot copy their DNA and die.
section1.full: The biochemistry was worked out in cell culture: inhibition of thymidylate synthase by FdUMP requires 5,10-methylenetetrahydrofolate, and the drug-enzyme-folate complex falls away when cellular folates are depleted, taking the drug's killing power with it [[TX-L22]]. Leucovorin (folinic acid) is a reduced folate that cells convert into that cofactor; in the first large randomized test, in colorectal cancer, response was 30.3% with high-dose leucovorin versus 12.1% with fluorouracil alone [[TX-L18]]. How the drug is given matters as much as the dose. Fluorouracil disappears from the blood within minutes and acts only on cells copying DNA at the time, so a two-day infusion keeps the enzyme blocked through more cell divisions than a brief injection (a bolus); in the colorectal trial that established the schedule, infusion doubled response (32.6% versus 14.4%) and halved severe toxicity (11.1% versus 23.9%) [[TX-L19]]. Pancreatic regimens therefore deliver 2,400 mg/m² over 46 hours through a portable pump on a central line, with or without a 400 mg/m² bolus first [[TX-L02]][[TX-003]]. Capecitabine is an oral prodrug converted to fluorouracil in three enzymatic steps, the last more active in tumor tissue, and it adds red, sore palms and soles. Fluorouracil's side effects fall on fast-dividing tissues: mouth ulcers, diarrhea and low blood counts, with rare chest pain from spasm of the heart's arteries. People who inherit a weak version of the enzyme DPD, which breaks down most of a dose, can have severe or fatal toxicity in the first cycles [[GENE-019]][[SEC-GENE-02]].

section2.label: Why it matters here
section2.preview: Fluorouracil was the drug gemcitabine beat in 1997, and it has since returned as the base of every multi-drug regimen that beat gemcitabine. On its own it is a weak treatment: as the control arm of second-line trials it gave median survivals of 3.3 to 4.2 months. Its value is as the component other drugs are built on, and its tablet form capecitabine adds a small, measurable benefit to adjuvant gemcitabine.
section2.full: In the 1997 trial that established gemcitabine, the comparator was fluorouracil 600 mg/m² as a weekly bolus, a schedule later shown to be inferior to infusion, and gemcitabine's survival advantage was 5.65 versus 4.41 months [[TX-L03]]. As the control arm of the NAPOLI-1 trial, on a bolus-style schedule, fluorouracil/leucovorin gave a median survival of 4.2 months after gemcitabine failure; in the CONKO-003 trial, fluorouracil with folinic acid gave 3.3 months; but in the PANCREOX trial, infusional fluorouracil/leucovorin gave 9.9 months and outperformed the oxaliplatin combination, so schedule and the fitness of those enrolled moved the result as much as any added drug [[TX-014]][[TX-L04]][[TX-L05]]. In the adjuvant ESPAC-4 trial, 730 patients received gemcitabine with or without capecitabine 1,660 mg/m² per day for 21 of every 28 days; median survival was 28.0 versus 25.5 months (hazard ratio 0.82), and the combination reduced local recurrence [[TX-L06]][[SURG-014]]. Adjuvant effects take years to read: the PRODIGE 24 trial, whose modified FOLFIRINOX arm rests on this backbone, needed a median follow-up of 69.7 months to report five-year survival [[TX-003]]. In the US, fluorouracil is labeled for pancreatic adenocarcinoma with the bolus-plus-46-hour infusional schedule; capecitabine is not labeled for pancreatic cancer, so its use here is guideline-based and off-label [[SEC-TX-09]][[TX-L06]]. The capecitabine label now directs testing of the DPYD gene, which encodes the DPD enzyme, before treatment unless treatment is urgent while stating that no FDA-authorized DPYD test exists; in a mixed-cancer cohort, genotype-guided dosing cut clinically relevant toxicity from 43.3% to 16.0% [[SEC-GENE-02]][[GENE-019]].

action_note.heading: When to call the care team now
action_note.text: Severe mouth sores, heavy diarrhea, confusion or marked weakness within the first days of a fluorouracil infusion or capecitabine course can signal an inherited inability to clear the drug and warrant an immediate call rather than waiting for the next visit [[SEC-GENE-02]]. A temperature of 38.0 °C (100.4 °F) or higher during treatment needs same-day evaluation [[SEC-SUPP-03]][[SEC-SUPP-01]]. Chest pain or pressure during or soon after a fluorouracil infusion needs emergency assessment, because the drug can cause spasm of the heart's arteries.

research_notes.what_findings_mean: Fluorouracil's pancreatic evidence is mostly indirect: its mechanism and the leucovorin and infusion principles come from biochemistry and colorectal trials, and its pancreatic role is defined by the combinations built on it and by the control arms it supplied [[TX-L22]][[TX-L18]][[TX-L19]][[TX-014]]. The spread of control-arm survivals (3.3 to 9.9 months) across second-line trials shows that schedule, dose and patient selection can move a result by months, which cautions against reading any single-drug figure as the drug's worth [[TX-L04]][[TX-L05]][[TX-014]]. The capecitabine benefit in ESPAC-4 was small (hazard ratio 0.82) but came with a reduction in local recurrence, and it remains the adjuvant option for people who cannot take mFOLFIRINOX [[TX-L06]][[SURG-014]].
research_notes.how_studied: The ternary-complex mechanism was shown by depleting folate in cultured cells and measuring how much drug-enzyme complex formed, a direct biochemical test [[TX-L22]]. The leucovorin and infusion schedules were settled by randomized colorectal trials in the 1980s and 1990s that compared response rates and toxicity, and they are available only as abstracts [[TX-L18]][[TX-L19]]. Pancreatic numbers come from the control arms of randomized trials in which fluorouracil/leucovorin was the comparator, so they describe the comparator population of each trial rather than a trial designed to measure fluorouracil [[TX-014]][[TX-L04]][[TX-L05]]. DPYD evidence is a retrospective comparison of patients genotyped before versus after treatment [[GENE-019]].

mechanism_notes.text: The 9.9-month survival of the infusional fluorouracil/leucovorin arm in PANCREOX, against 4.2 months for the bolus-style arm in NAPOLI-1 and 3.3 months in CONKO-003, is consistent with the colorectal finding that continuous infusion keeps thymidylate synthase blocked through more cell cycles while sparing marrow and gut, but the three trials differed in era, fitness and later treatment, so the schedule explains only part of the gap [[TX-L19]][[TX-L05]][[TX-014]][[TX-L04]].

topics.clinical_status: In the US as of 8 Oct 2026, fluorouracil injection is FDA-labeled for pancreatic adenocarcinoma, and the label lists the 400 mg/m² bolus plus 2,400-3,000 mg/m² 46-hour infusion schedule with leucovorin; leucovorin is labeled for use with fluorouracil in colorectal cancer. Capecitabine is labeled for colorectal, breast and gastric cancers, not pancreatic cancer, where its adjuvant use with gemcitabine is guideline-based and off-label; its label directs DPYD testing before treatment.

glossary.definition: A chemotherapy drug that mimics the RNA base uracil and blocks the enzyme that makes the DNA base thymine.
A form of folate, also called folinic acid, given with fluorouracil to lock the drug onto its target enzyme.
The enzyme that makes thymidylate, the thymine building block of DNA, and the target of fluorouracil.
The stable three-part grouping of drug, enzyme and folate that keeps thymidylate synthase blocked.
A dose of drug injected over a few minutes rather than infused over hours.
A small portable device that delivers fluorouracil slowly over 46 hours through a central line while the person is at home.
A tablet that the body converts into fluorouracil in three steps, the last of which is more active in tumors.
Redness, soreness and peeling of the palms and soles caused by capecitabine and some infusional fluorouracil schedules.
An inherited shortage of the enzyme that breaks down fluorouracil, which can make a standard dose dangerous.

related.statement: Fluorouracil and leucovorin form the backbone of FOLFIRINOX, infused over 46 hours with or without a bolus.
Fluorouracil and leucovorin are the infusional backbone of NALIRIFOX.
Fluorouracil and leucovorin are the base of every second-line regimen tested after gemcitabine, including the liposomal irinotecan combination.
Fluorouracil was the weekly bolus comparator that gemcitabine beat in 1997, and capecitabine later added a small benefit to adjuvant gemcitabine.
Inherited DPYD variants modulate how safely a person can receive fluorouracil or capecitabine, and the capecitabine label directs testing before treatment.
Fluorouracil and leucovorin are required partners for irinotecan in second line, where liposomal irinotecan alone gave no benefit.
Fluorouracil and leucovorin are the base to which oxaliplatin is added in FOLFOX and OFF.
Fluorouracil's diarrhea and mouth soreness are the kind of bowel and mouth changes described in the nausea and bowel topic.

faq.q: Why is leucovorin given if it is not a chemotherapy drug?
faq.a: Leucovorin is a folate, a vitamin-like molecule, that cells convert into the cofactor fluorouracil needs to lock onto thymidylate synthase. In cells starved of folate the drug-enzyme complex falls apart, and in the first randomized test adding leucovorin raised response from 12% to 30% [[TX-L22]][[TX-L18]].

faq.q: Can I take tablets instead of the pump?
faq.a: Capecitabine is the tablet form and becomes fluorouracil in the body; it is used with gemcitabine after surgery, where it added about 2.5 months to median survival [[TX-L06]]. In the multi-drug regimens, the 46-hour infusion is what the trials tested, and the capecitabine label now directs DPYD testing before starting [[SEC-GENE-02]].

faq.q: What is DPD deficiency?
faq.a: An inherited shortage of the enzyme that breaks down most of a fluorouracil dose, which can cause severe or fatal toxicity in the first cycles. Testing before treatment and adjusting the dose cut serious toxicity from 43% to 16% in one cohort, though the US label notes no FDA-authorized test yet exists [[GENE-019]][[SEC-GENE-02]].

topics.title: Oxaliplatin
topics.orientation: Oxaliplatin is a platinum chemotherapy drug and one of the four components of FOLFIRINOX and of NALIRIFOX, the combination regimens used for fit people with pancreatic cancer. Its signature side effect is nerve damage, which starts as a cold-triggered tingling and can become a lasting numbness.

section1.label: What it does
section1.preview: Oxaliplatin is a platinum compound. Inside a cell it binds DNA and forms crosslinks between neighboring bases, mostly on the same strand, which bend the double helix, stall copying and reading of the DNA, and push a dividing cell into programmed death. Cancer cells divide more often than most normal tissue and tolerate such damage poorly, the basis of its selectivity. The same platinum-DNA attachments, called adducts, build up in sensory nerve cell bodies, which is why nerves pay the price.
section1.full: In the trial that added oxaliplatin to infusional fluorouracil and leucovorin for colorectal cancer, the response rate rose from 22.3% to 50.7% and progression-free survival from 6.2 to 9.0 months, at the cost of grade 3 (severe) neuropathy in 18.2% versus none and grade 3 to 4 neutropenia (a shortage of infection-fighting white cells) in 41.7% versus 5.3% [[TX-L20]]. That add-on design is the cleanest measure of what the drug itself contributes, and it became the template for FOLFIRINOX, which places oxaliplatin alongside irinotecan, fluorouracil and leucovorin [[TX-L02]]. Because the bulky lesions it leaves on DNA are repaired partly by the homologous recombination system, a DNA-repair pathway that uses the matching chromosome as a template, platinum drugs tend to work better when that system is broken: among 262 people with advanced pancreatic cancer, those with homologous-recombination gene defects had longer progression-free survival on first-line platinum chemotherapy (hazard ratio 0.44) but no such advantage on non-platinum regimens [[GENE-016]]. Oxaliplatin's own US label covers colorectal cancer only; its use in pancreatic cancer rests on the FOLFIRINOX trials and on the NALIRIFOX regimen, where it is paired with liposomal irinotecan at a lower dose than in FOLFIRINOX [[TX-002]][[SEC-TX-09]]. Allergic reactions during infusion, low blood counts and nausea are its other recognized harms; oxaliplatin and irinotecan are both classed as moderately nausea-provoking, so preventive anti-nausea drugs are standard with every cycle [[SEC-SUPP-06]].

section2.label: Why it matters here
section2.preview: Oxaliplatin's cost is nerve damage with two time courses. A cold-triggered form appears within days of each infusion: in a study of 346 people on FOLFOX, an oxaliplatin regimen for colorectal cancer, 89% felt it with the first cycle, as tingling on touching or swallowing anything cold, throat discomfort and muscle cramps, peaking around day three [[TX-022]]. A chronic form builds with cumulative dose, keeps worsening for about three months after the last dose, and left 19% with severe persistent symptoms at 18 months [[TX-022]].
section2.full: The chronic form is the one that shapes decisions. During treatment tingling outranks numbness and the hands are worse than the feet; by 18 months the pattern reverses and the feet dominate [[TX-022]]. How severe the acute symptoms were in the first cycle predicted later chronic damage, so early reports matter [[TX-022]]. Nothing reliably prevents it: the antioxidant calmangafodipir made moderate-to-severe neuropathy more frequent (54.3% versus 40.3% at nine months), so no preventive drug is recommended and the main tool is lowering, delaying or stopping oxaliplatin when symptoms persist between cycles [[SUPP-010]][[SEC-SUPP-07]][[SEC-SUPP-12]]. For established painful neuropathy, the antidepressant duloxetine lowered average pain by 0.73 points more than placebo on a 0 to 10 scale over five weeks, with 59% versus 38% reporting any improvement, the only drug with moderate-quality support [[SUPP-026]][[SEC-SUPP-07]]. In the adjuvant FOLFIRINOX trial, 55.0% of patients stopped oxaliplatin before the twelfth cycle and only 33.6% received at least 80% of the planned dose intensity, yet the survival advantage over gemcitabine held, with median overall survival of 53.5 versus 35.5 months [[TX-003]]. Dropping oxaliplatin to protect the nerves while the other drugs continue is therefore a planned maneuver, not a failure. In the NALIRIFOX trial, which uses a lower oxaliplatin dose, grade 3 to 4 neuropathy affected 3% versus 6% with gemcitabine and nab-paclitaxel [[TX-002]].

action_note.heading: What to watch for during oxaliplatin
