topics.orientation: For about twenty years no drug could bind mutated KRAS itself, so the pathway around it was attacked instead: the enzyme that anchors RAS to the cell membrane, the receptors feeding signal in above it, and the signaling enzymes (kinases) carrying signal away below it. Almost all of those attempts failed, and how they failed shaped the drugs now in use.

section1.label: What it does
section1.preview: Four strategies were tried in turn. Farnesyltransferase inhibitors aimed to stop RAS reaching the membrane, where it has to sit to work. EGFR inhibitors aimed to cut the growth-factor signal arriving above RAS. MEK inhibitors aimed to block the kinase immediately below it. Later, SOS1 and SHP2 inhibitors aimed at the proteins that help switch RAS on. None of them touched the mutant protein itself.
section1.full: RAS proteins must carry an added lipid tail to dock at the inner face of the cell membrane, and farnesyltransferase attaches it, so blocking that enzyme was expected to leave RAS floating uselessly inside the cell. It did not, because KRAS can accept an alternative lipid from a second enzyme, so tipifarnib never tested the hypothesis it was built on [[RAS-036]]. The kinases below RAS were a sounder target but a leaky one: removing one step leaves the cell free to refill the pathway from above. Within hours of blockade, cells make fresh KRAS protein that receptor and aurora-kinase signaling hold in the active, drug-insensitive state, and about a fifth resume dividing [[RAS-008]]. Blocking the input as well as the output was the obvious reply, which is why MEK inhibition was paired with EGFR, with AKT (a parallel growth-signaling enzyme), and later with SOS1 and SHP2 [[RAS-020]][[RAS-005]][[RAS-018]].

section2.label: Why it matters here
section2.preview: The pancreatic record for this pathway is a long run of negative trials, two of them large. Tipifarnib added to gemcitabine was tested in 688 patients and changed survival by about eleven days. Erlotinib, the only one of these drugs that ever reached a positive result, added about ten days to the median. One combination did measurably worse than chemotherapy alone. That record is what makes the 2026 result unusual.
section2.full: In the phase 3 tipifarnib trial median survival was 193 days with the drug and 182 without it, a difference well within chance (P=0.75), with ten drug-related deaths against seven; the trial is available only as a published abstract [[RAS-036]]. Erlotinib with gemcitabine did reach significance in 569 patients, with a hazard ratio of 0.82 and one-year survival of 23% against 17%, and was approved on that basis; it too is available only as an abstract [[RAS-037]]. Trametinib added to gemcitabine gave a hazard ratio of 0.98 in 160 patients, with no benefit in the KRAS-mutant subgroup, again available only as an abstract [[RAS-038]]. MEK plus EGFR produced no tumor responses at all in 46 patients [[RAS-020]], and MEK plus AKT was halted at an interim futility analysis with median survival of 3.9 against 6.7 months on chemotherapy [[RAS-005]]. Daraxonrasib, approved in August 2026, was the first drug on this pathway to reach a hazard ratio of 0.40 [[RAS-033]][[SEC-RAS-01]].

research_notes.what_findings_mean: These trials share a feature that limits what can be read from them: several combinations reached their molecular target and still produced nothing. The SHP2-plus-ERK study measured a significant fall in a downstream signaling protein with zero tumor responses and never established a dose to take forward [[RAS-039]]; the SOS1 combination had to cap trametinib at 1 mg to be tolerable [[RAS-018]]; MEK and EGFR were each given below their single-drug doses [[RAS-020]]. The failures may mean the mechanism is wrong, or only that tolerable human exposures are too low to test it [[RAS-005]].
research_notes.how_studied: Three of these results, for tipifarnib, erlotinib and trametinib, are available only as published abstracts, so hazard ratios, confidence intervals and the authors' own stated limitations cannot be checked against full texts [[RAS-036]][[RAS-037]][[RAS-038]]. The two combination studies are available in full [[RAS-020]][[RAS-005]]. Design matters as much as access: the MEK-plus-EGFR study was single-arm against a historical survival threshold, which cannot separate a drug effect from the natural course, while the MEK-plus-AKT study randomized against chemotherapy and could therefore demonstrate harm.

mechanism_notes.text: The repeated failure of single-node blockade below RAS has a consistent mechanical explanation. Blocking MEK or ERK leaves the receptors above RAS free to reload the pathway, and laboratory work shows PI3K recruiting scaffolding to the membrane to reactivate signaling through normal, non-mutant RAS while mutant KRAS is held down [[INF-RAS-01]][[RAS-027]][[RAS-008]]. On that reading, a drug had to act on RAS itself rather than on one step beside it, which is the design logic of the multi-selective agents that followed [[RAS-033]]. The competing reading is that the earlier combinations were never given at exposures high enough to test their own hypothesis [[RAS-018]][[RAS-039]].

topics.clinical_status: As of 8 Oct 2026 in the US, none of the drugs described here is approved for pancreatic cancer except erlotinib with gemcitabine, which was approved on the trial described and is rarely used given a median survival gain of about ten days. Tipifarnib, selumetinib, trametinib, the SOS1 inhibitor and the SHP2-plus-ERK combination have no pancreatic indication, and the SOS1 and SHP2 programs did not continue past phase 1 in this disease.

glossary.definition: The enzyme that attaches a lipid tail to certain proteins, including RAS, so they can anchor to the inside of the cell membrane.
A kinase immediately downstream of RAS that passes the growth signal along to ERK.
The epidermal growth factor receptor, a protein on the cell surface that feeds growth signals into the RAS pathway.
A protein that helps load RAS with GTP, the step that switches RAS on.
An enzyme that relays signals from surface receptors toward RAS, acting just upstream of it.
A planned look at a trial's data partway through, which can stop the trial if the experimental treatment clearly will not prove better.

related.statement: Every strategy described here attacked a protein beside KRAS because KRAS itself could not be bound by a drug.
Daraxonrasib was the first drug aimed at this pathway to produce a large randomized survival benefit in pancreatic cancer, after the failures described here.
The adaptive reactivation that defeated MEK and EGFR inhibitors is the same process that now underlies resistance to RAS inhibitors.
The erlotinib trial shows why a significant hazard ratio and a ten-day median gain can describe the same result.
This run of negative pathway trials is the historical background against which any new pancreatic cancer result is judged.

faq.q: If these drugs failed, why were they ever approved or used?
faq.a: Only one was approved for pancreatic cancer. Erlotinib with gemcitabine met its survival endpoint in 569 patients, with a hazard ratio of 0.82 and one-year survival of 23% against 17%, and the median gain of about ten days explains why it is rarely used today [[RAS-037]]. The others, including tipifarnib and trametinib, were tested and never approved for this disease [[RAS-036]][[RAS-038]].

faq.q: Were the failures because the idea was wrong or the drugs were weak?
faq.a: Both remain possible and the trials cannot separate them. Several combinations demonstrably hit their molecular target yet produced no tumor shrinkage, and in each case dosing had to be reduced for tolerability, so the hypothesis was never tested at full strength [[RAS-039]][[RAS-018]][[RAS-020]].

topics.title: Personalized mRNA neoantigen vaccines
topics.orientation: A personalized mRNA neoantigen vaccine is built for one person from the mutations found in their own removed tumor, with the aim of teaching T cells to recognize cancer cells that surgery and chemotherapy left behind. One such vaccine, autogene cevumeran, has completed a small phase 1 study in resected pancreatic cancer, and the randomized trial that would show whether it helps has no results yet.

section1.label: What it does
section1.preview: A pancreatic tumor carries mutations found in no one else's cancer. After the operation the removed tumor is sequenced, up to twenty mutant protein fragments predicted to be visible to T cells are selected, and the instructions for making them are written into messenger RNA wrapped in fat particles. Given into a vein, that RNA turns the person's own antigen-presenting cells into a training display.
section1.full: The phase 1 trial staggered its components so each could be attributed separately: surgery, then one dose of the checkpoint antibody atezolizumab at week 6, then nine vaccine doses from week 9, then twelve cycles of chemotherapy [[IMM-001]]. Manufacturing kept that timetable, with a median of 9.4 weeks from surgery to the first vaccine dose, and one of nineteen patients had too few usable mutations for a vaccine to be built at all [[IMM-001]]. What the vaccine produced was both measurable and new. Eight of sixteen vaccinated patients developed T cells reacting to their own neoantigens, none detectable before vaccination, and in those eight a median of 7.5 T-cell clones grew from undetectable to a median 2.8 percent of all circulating T cells, with single-cell sequencing identifying them as cytotoxic (killer) CD8 T cells carrying the cell-killing proteins perforin and granzyme B [[IMM-001]]. The hit rate on the target list was low: 25 of 230 administered neoantigens, 11 percent, provoked a response, a median of two per responder [[IMM-001]]. Those cells then lasted. Most tracked clones persisted beyond two years, and a single booster dose at week 46 lengthened their estimated median lifespan from about 1.1 years to 7.7 years [[IMM-002]]. Side effects were mild: one severe (grade 3) event in sixteen, a fever with raised blood pressure [[IMM-001]].

section2.label: Why it matters here
section2.preview: Raising an immune response and lengthening someone's life are different achievements, and this is the clearest place in pancreatic cancer to see the gap between them. Among the sixteen vaccinated patients, those who mounted a response stayed free of recurrence far longer than those who did not. That comparison was drawn afterwards, inside a single treated group, with nobody untreated to compare against.
section2.full: The published hazard ratio for recurrence between responders and non-responders was 0.08 at 18 months and 0.14 at 3.2 years, with non-responders recurring at a median of 13.4 months and responders not reaching a median [[IMM-001]][[IMM-002]]. Three features make that an upper bound on any effect rather than an estimate of one. It compares subgroups of one treated arm, split by a test performed during treatment, so a patient who recurred early had less time to mount a detectable response. The responder threshold was a single cut-point taken from the same patients [[IMM-001]]. And a separation of almost the same size can be produced from blood drawn before any treatment at all: across two randomized vaccine trials, a baseline immune profile measured in the blood split median survival 271 days against 77 days, and did so in every arm including the chemotherapy arm [[IMM-022]]. Something measured before treatment cannot be an effect of treatment. The trial that can settle the question, IMCODE003, randomizes an estimated 260 patients with macroscopically complete resections to the vaccine plus atezolizumab plus chemotherapy or chemotherapy alone, with disease-free survival as its primary endpoint; it is listed as active and not recruiting, with primary completion expected in January 2031 and no results posted [[SEC-IMMUNE-01]].

research_notes.what_findings_mean: The phase 1 trial met its safety endpoint and showed the manufacturing can run on a post-surgical timetable; every outcome finding in it was labeled exploratory in advance, and no randomized neoantigen-vaccine result exists in this disease as of 8 Oct 2026 [[IMM-001]][[SEC-IMMUNE-08]]. The low per-neoantigen hit rate matters more here than in other cancers, because pancreatic tumors carry few mutations to start with, averaging around 35 predicted neoantigens against roughly 112 in non-small-cell lung cancer and 370 in melanoma, so an 11 percent response rate works on an already short list [[IMM-026]][[IMM-001]]. Durability is the firmest positive result: T cells from most tested responders still produced interferon-gamma and killed on neoantigen re-exposure up to 3.6 years after vaccination [[IMM-002]].
research_notes.how_studied: Immune response was read two ways. An interferon-gamma ELISpot test on blood cells counts the cells that secrete that signaling protein when re-exposed to the vaccine peptides; it detects only strong responses and does not separate helper (CD4) from killer (CD8) T cells [[IMM-001]]. Sequencing of T-cell receptor beta chains then tracks individual clones over time, which is what showed the expanded clones were absent before vaccination and did not overlap the clones expanded by the checkpoint antibody [[IMM-001]]. Clone lifespan was modeled rather than observed, by fitting exponential decay to serial clone frequencies, which is why those figures come as wide ranges [[IMM-002]]. Recurrence-free survival was also measured from the last priming dose, a landmark approach that removes part of the advantage a patient gains simply by living long enough to be tested [[IMM-001]].

mechanism_notes.text: The responder-versus-non-responder survival gap may run backwards from the direction it appears to run. Tumor left behind after surgery could both suppress T-cell priming, through systemic inflammation and the expansion of suppressive myeloid (bone-marrow-derived immune) cells, and cause early recurrence by itself, which would generate a large survival split with no contribution from the vaccine [[INF-IMMUNE-02]][[IMM-022]]. The competing account is that the vaccine works and only in people whose immune systems can answer it. The two can be told apart by adjusting the responder analysis for circulating tumor DNA at the time of the first dose, and by running the identical responder split inside a control arm [[INF-IMMUNE-02]][[IMM-001]].

topics.clinical_status: Investigational in the US as of 8 Oct 2026: autogene cevumeran is not FDA-approved for any indication, and every published clinical result in pancreatic cancer comes from one 19-patient phase 1 trial and its extended follow-up. The randomized phase 2 IMCODE003 (NCT05968326, estimated 260 participants, primary endpoint disease-free survival) is listed as active and not recruiting with primary completion expected January 2031 and no posted results. Access is through clinical trials only.

glossary.definition: A protein fragment that exists only because of a mutation in the cancer, so the immune system has never been taught to tolerate it.
A vaccine that delivers genetic instructions so the body's own cells briefly make the target protein and display it to the immune system.
A laboratory test that counts individual immune cells secreting a signaling protein after being shown a specific target.
The time from a starting point, usually surgery, until cancer is detected again or the person dies, whichever comes first.
A result a trial looks at without being designed to test it, so a difference found there raises a question rather than answering one.
A way of counting survival from a later fixed time point so that patients are not credited for simply having lived long enough to be measured.
An extra dose given months after the first course to re-stimulate immune cells that would otherwise fade.

related.statement: A personalized mRNA vaccine works by loading antigen-presenting cells with mutant protein fragments, the step pancreatic cancer otherwise performs poorly.
The mRNA vaccine's measurable product is new cytotoxic T-cell clones in the blood, which persisted for more than two years in most vaccinated patients.
Personalized mRNA vaccines are built from each patient's private mutations, whereas KRAS vaccines target a mutation shared across most pancreatic cancers.
Vaccines after surgery are aimed at microscopic disease that imaging cannot see, which is why the trials measure recurrence rather than tumor shrinkage.
Circulating tumor DNA at the time of vaccination is the measurement that would separate a true vaccine effect from a responder group that simply had less cancer left.
The responder-versus-non-responder comparison in the mRNA vaccine trial is a worked example of why a within-arm split is not a treatment effect.
Autogene cevumeran is available only inside a clinical trial, and its randomized test is closed to new enrollment with results expected around 2031.

faq.q: Can I get this vaccine?
faq.a: Not as prescribed treatment anywhere: it is investigational and not FDA-approved for any indication [[IMM-001]]. The randomized trial is listed as active but not recruiting, so new enrollment is closed, and other neoantigen-vaccine trials are the realistic route to ask your team about [[SEC-IMMUNE-01]].

faq.q: If half the patients responded, does that mean it worked in half?
faq.a: It means half developed detectable T cells against their own tumor mutations, which is a biological result, not a clinical one [[IMM-001]]. Whether those T cells prevented recurrence cannot be answered by a trial with no untreated comparison group, and a similar survival split can be produced by immune measurements taken before any treatment [[IMM-022]].

faq.q: Why does each person need a different vaccine?
faq.a: The mutations that make a cancer look foreign are mostly unique to that tumor, so the target list has to be read off the removed specimen. Pancreatic cancers also carry relatively few such mutations, around 35 on average, which is part of why only about one in nine targeted fragments provoked a response [[IMM-026]][[IMM-001]].

topics.title: Shared-antigen KRAS vaccines
topics.orientation: Instead of building a vaccine for one person, a shared-antigen vaccine aims at something many pancreatic cancers hold in common, most often a single changed amino acid in the KRAS protein, so one product can be manufactured in advance and given to anyone whose tumor carries the matching change. This entry covers the current KRAS peptide vaccines and the older whole-cell programs that went before them.

section1.label: What it does
section1.preview: Nearly every pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma carries a KRAS mutation, and a handful of variants account for most of them. That makes the mutant KRAS fragment an off-the-shelf target: a product made in advance, usable in anyone whose tumor carries the right change and whose tissue-type molecules can display it. The hard engineering problem turns out not to be the peptide but getting it to the lymph nodes.
section1.full: ELI-002, the current KRAS peptide vaccine, solves the delivery problem with chemistry. Each 18-amino-acid mutant KRAS peptide, and the CpG adjuvant (an immune-alerting additive) that accompanies it, carries a lipid tail that binds albumin, the most abundant protein in blood; albumin drains into the lymphatic vessels, so a subcutaneous injection concentrates in the draining lymph node where T cells are primed instead of dispersing through the circulation [[IMM-003]]. The reason that detail earns a sentence comes from mouse work in which the identical peptide and adjuvant in soluble form failed while the lymph-node-targeted version eradicated established tumors; the only difference between the working and failing arms was where the antigen went [[IMM-016]]. In the phase 1 AMPLIFY-201 trial, 25 patients, 20 of them with pancreatic cancer, who had no disease visible on imaging after surgery but still had detectable tumor DNA or raised tumor markers, received a two-peptide version covering KRAS G12D and G12R [[IMM-003]]. Mutant-KRAS-specific T cells appeared in 21 of 25, 84 percent, rising to every patient at the two highest adjuvant doses, with both helper (CD4) and killer (CD8) T-cell responses in 59 percent [[IMM-003]]. Related side effects occurred in 12 of 25 and were all mild or moderate (grade 1 or 2), most often fatigue and injection-site reactions, with no dose-limiting toxicity [[IMM-004]].

section2.label: Why it matters here
section2.preview: The outcome numbers from that trial have been reported two ways, and the difference between them is the lesson. Headline hazard ratios of 0.12 for recurrence and 0.23 for death came from splitting the same 25 patients at a threshold chosen by testing which cut-off best separated their own outcomes. The earlier report, using a landmark correction instead (counting outcomes only from a later fixed time point), found a recurrence hazard ratio whose confidence interval crossed 1.
section2.full: That corrected figure is a hazard ratio of 0.22, 95 percent confidence interval 0.038 to 1.27, P=0.076, and it is the defensible bound on the association [[IMM-004]]. A second number belongs beside it. Everyone entered this trial with no disease visible on scans, and the median recurrence-free survival was still 16.33 months overall and 15.31 months in the pancreatic patients [[IMM-003]]. The randomized successor, AMPLIFY-7P, has completed enrollment at 158 participants and compares the vaccine against observation for disease-free survival; it is listed as active and not recruiting, past its primary completion date, with no results posted [[SEC-IMMUNE-02]][[SEC-RAS-12]]. The older shared-antigen programs show what randomization does to an encouraging signal. GVAX, irradiated pancreatic cancer cells engineered to secrete the immune-stimulating factor GM-CSF, was paired with CRS-207, a weakened Listeria bacterium carrying mesothelin, a protein on most pancreatic cancer cells, and tested against single-agent chemotherapy in 213 previously treated patients: median survival 3.7 versus 4.6 months, hazard ratio 1.17, with the point estimate favoring chemotherapy [[IMM-005]]. The regimen was well tolerated; it simply did not help.

research_notes.what_findings_mean: A 2026 randomized trial added nivolumab and ipilimumab to the GVAX and CRS-207 backbone and makes the dissociation unmistakable. Its primary endpoint, tumor response, was missed in both arms, at 0 percent of 30 patients and 7 percent of 27, with median survival 4.3 and 3.9 months; the exploratory immunology in the same patients identified the specific T-cell clones (clonotypes) reactive to mutant KRAS and to mesothelin and found them expanded and inside the tumor, predominantly as CD8 memory cells [[IMM-012]]. Severe treatment-related events occurred in 68 percent, mostly from the Listeria component, including one confirmed CRS-207 bloodstream infection [[IMM-012]]. Mutant-KRAS peptide vaccination in resected pancreatic cancer dates back more than fifteen years, so the concept is not new; the lymph-node delivery is [[SEC-IMMUNE-04]][[IMM-016]].
research_notes.how_studied: T-cell responses here were measured directly from blood without first growing the cells, which sets a high bar and is why the 84 percent figure is meaningful [[IMM-003]]. Because these patients had no measurable tumor, the trial used circulating tumor DNA and serum markers as its disease readout rather than scans, with a tumor-informed DNA assay in 21 of 25 and a generic serum-based one in the rest, an inconsistency that matters when the same measurement defines who is eligible and who improved [[IMM-004]][[IMM-003]]. Two different thresholds were used to define a strong responder, a median split at 12.75-fold and a later receiver-operating-characteristic cut-off at 9.17-fold (chosen to best separate outcomes), both derived from the trial's own outcomes; the randomized trial avoids this by comparing allocated groups instead [[IMM-003]][[SEC-IMMUNE-02]].

mechanism_notes.text: The GVAX trials suggest the limiting step sits after priming and trafficking, not before them. Antigen-specific CD8 memory T cells were documented inside tumors that kept growing, which is consistent with too few effector cells arriving relative to tumor burden combined with active local switching-off once they land [[INF-IMMUNE-01]][[IMM-012]]. The competing account is that the clones detected inside the tumor are weakly binding (low-avidity) bystanders rather than too few fighters. The randomized vaccine trials now closed to enrollment can distinguish these by testing whether disease-free survival tracks the size of the immune response as a continuous measure [[INF-IMMUNE-01]][[SEC-IMMUNE-02]].

topics.clinical_status: No KRAS vaccine is approved anywhere as of 8 Oct 2026. ELI-002 is investigational: AMPLIFY-201 (phase 1, 25 patients) is complete, and the randomized AMPLIFY-7P (NCT05726864, 158 enrolled, phase 2 primary endpoint disease-free survival versus observation) is active and not recruiting with no posted results. GVAX and CRS-207 are not FDA-approved for any indication; the randomized phase 2b against chemotherapy missed its survival endpoint and the program was discontinued in that setting. Access to any of these is through clinical trials only.

glossary.definition: A target present in many different people's tumors, which allows one vaccine to be made in advance rather than built per patient.
A substance given with a vaccine that alerts the immune system and makes it respond more strongly to the target.
The lymph node that collects fluid from a region of the body and where T-cell responses to anything arriving there are started.
Cancer left after treatment in amounts too small to see on scans but large enough to show up as tumor DNA or markers in blood.
A comparison of how fast events happen in two groups, where 1 means no difference and below 1 favors the first group.
A natural signal that recruits and matures the cells which present antigens, used in whole-cell vaccines to draw the immune system to the injection site.
A protein found on the surface of most pancreatic cancer cells and little normal tissue, which made it an early immune target.

related.statement: KRAS vaccines target the mutant KRAS protein itself, which is why a mutation present in the great majority of pancreatic cancers can serve as one shared vaccine target.
A shared-antigen KRAS vaccine only fits patients whose tumor carries one of the covered variants, so KRAS-wild-type pancreatic cancers fall outside these trials.
ELI-002 is engineered to accumulate in the draining lymph nodes, because that is where T cells are primed against a new antigen.
The KRAS vaccine trials select and follow patients by circulating tumor DNA and serum markers, because by design the participants have no tumor visible on imaging.
Shared-antigen KRAS vaccines and personalized mRNA vaccines share the same unresolved question: an immune response has been shown, a survival benefit has not.
Both the KRAS peptide vaccine and the GVAX whole-cell vaccine act by supplying antigen-presenting cells with material, a step this cancer performs poorly on its own.
The two different hazard ratios reported from the same 25-patient KRAS vaccine trial illustrate how much a data-derived threshold can change an apparent result.

faq.q: Almost every pancreatic cancer has a KRAS mutation, so why isn't there a KRAS vaccine already?
faq.a: The shared target is real: blood sequencing in a randomized trial found KRAS mutations in 77 percent of 173 metastatic pancreatic cancers [[IMM-007]]. Raising KRAS-specific T cells has also been achieved repeatedly, in 84 percent of patients in the most recent phase 1 trial [[IMM-003]]. What has not been shown is that those T cells delay recurrence or extend life, and the randomized trial designed to test it has not reported [[IMM-004]][[SEC-IMMUNE-02]].

faq.q: If the vaccine made T cells that got into the tumor, why didn't the tumor shrink?
faq.a: That exact situation was documented in a randomized trial: mutant-KRAS- and mesothelin-reactive CD8 memory T cells were found expanded and inside the tumors, while the response rate was 0 percent in one arm and 7 percent in the other [[IMM-012]]. It places the obstacle after the T cells arrive, not before.

faq.q: Is GVAX still being studied?
faq.a: Not as a path to approval in previously treated metastatic disease: the randomized trial against chemotherapy gave a hazard ratio of 1.17, favoring chemotherapy, and the program was discontinued in that setting [[IMM-005]]. It has continued to appear in small combination studies used mainly to ask mechanistic questions [[IMM-012]].

topics.title: Engineered T cells: TCR-T and CAR-T
topics.orientation: Rather than training a patient's T cells with a vaccine, these approaches remove T cells from the blood, give them a new receptor by gene transfer, and return them. Two designs exist: a T-cell receptor that reads mutant fragments held up by tissue-type molecules, and a chimeric antigen receptor that grips a surface protein directly. In pancreatic cancer both remain investigational, and the results so far are a small number of very detailed cases.

section1.label: What it does
section1.preview: A T-cell receptor sees short protein fragments only when a tissue-type molecule called HLA holds one up, which lets it reach mutations buried inside the cell, including mutant KRAS. A chimeric antigen receptor skips that step: it is an antibody fragment bolted onto T-cell signaling machinery, so it binds a protein on the cell surface and needs no HLA. Each design buys a different constraint.
section1.full: The receptor route produced the most striking single result in this disease. A 71-year-old woman with lung-only metastases after a Whipple operation, whose tumor carried KRAS G12D and who happened to have the HLA-C*08:02 tissue type, received 16.2 billion of her own T cells carrying two transferred receptors against that exact mutation-and-HLA pair. Her metastases shrank 62 percent by one month and 72 percent by six months, and the transferred cells still made up 2.4 percent of her circulating T cells at that point [[IMM-006]]. Specificity was then proven in the laboratory: the receptors recognized other people's pancreatic cancer cell lines only when both KRAS G12D and HLA-C*08:02 were present [[IMM-006]]. That same dependence is the ceiling on the approach. HLA-C*08:02 is carried by roughly 8 to 13 percent of people of European ancestry, and the tumor must also carry G12D, so the eligible fraction is small [[IMM-006]]. It is also a single point of failure. In a colorectal case treated the same way, seven of seven lung metastases regressed, and the one lesion that later grew had kept the KRAS G12D mutation while deleting the chromosome copy that carried HLA-C*08:02 [[IMM-014]].

section2.label: Why it matters here
section2.preview: Designing around the display step does not rescue the approach, which is what makes this cancer unusual. Mesothelin CAR-T cells, which need no HLA at all, produced no measurable responses in six patients, with stable disease as the best result. And in the second pancreatic receptor case, the engineered cells persisted in large numbers, caused severe cytokine toxicity, and the tumor grew regardless.
section2.full: That second case is the sharpest observation in the field. The patient received 29.6 billion cells, developed severe (grade 3) cytokine release syndrome and moderate (grade 2) neurological toxicity, and died of progression six months later; sequencing of a growing lesion found the target mutation still expressed, no HLA loss, no defect in the antigen-processing machinery and no interferon-gamma pathway mutation [[IMM-006]]. Every escape route known at the time was excluded. The mesothelin CAR-T cells were not inert either: in one of the six patients the metabolically active tumor volume on PET fell 69.2 percent with complete loss of signal in all liver lesions, without ever meeting response criteria by size [[IMM-015]]. Which target is chosen separates success from failure sharply. In a 37-patient phase 1 trial of CAR-T cells aimed at claudin-18.2, a protein found on stomach-lining and some pancreatic cancer cells, the gastric cancer group had a 57.1 percent response rate while the pooled nine-patient group that contained all five pancreatic patients had 22.2 percent, and pancreatic results were never reported separately [[IMM-008]]. The costs are real: the preconditioning chemotherapy caused severe (grade 3 or 4) lymphopenia, a shortage of lymphocytes, in all 37 patients and neutropenia (low infection-fighting white cells) in 68 percent, and one patient had life-threatening (grade 4) bleeding from the gut as a tumor shrank rapidly [[IMM-008]].

research_notes.what_findings_mean: Claudin-18.2 CAR-T has become the first CAR-T cell product approved for any solid tumor, by China's regulator in June 2026, and the indication is advanced gastric or gastro-esophageal junction cancer after at least two prior lines; pancreatic cancer is not included and there is no FDA approval, so no one with pancreatic cancer can obtain it on label in any country [[SEC-IMMUNE-07]][[IMM-008]]. A pancreatic-specific pooled analysis of that product exists but is available only as an abstract, so no pancreatic efficacy figure is reported here [[SEC-IMMUNE-05]]. A cohort report of receptor-engineered cells against KRAS G12V in pancreatic cancer has also appeared but is available only as an abstract, and two further mesothelin CAR-T trials that included pancreatic patients are likewise not available in full; these are the main gaps in the evidence summarized here [[SEC-IMMUNE-06]][[SEC-IMMUNE-09]].
research_notes.how_studied: These are deliberately small studies read in unusual depth. Specificity is established in the laboratory by showing that engineered cells respond to cancer lines only when both the mutation and the matching HLA tissue type are present, which rules out off-target recognition [[IMM-006]]. Persistence is measured by sequencing the transferred receptor in serial blood samples, which is how it became clear that cells can be abundant while the tumor progresses [[IMM-006]][[IMM-014]]. Escape is investigated by sequencing a growing lesion and comparing it with a responding one, the method that identified loss of the HLA-C*08:02 copy [[IMM-014]]. Lesion-level FDG-PET (a scan of radioactive-sugar uptake) adds a readout that standard size criteria miss, which is how activity confined to liver deposits was detected [[IMM-015]].

mechanism_notes.text: The pattern across these cases suggests the binding constraint lies after the T cell has arrived and recognized its target. Clone frequencies of a few percent of blood T cells, of which only a fraction reaches the tumor, may deliver too small an effector dose against a large tumor burden, while local signals switch off the cells that do land [[INF-IMMUNE-01]][[IMM-006]][[IMM-015]]. If that is right, repeatedly re-stimulating the transferred cells should help, and in mice a lymph-node-targeted vaccine boost did exactly that, eradicating established tumors without chemotherapy preconditioning or high-dose cytokines [[IMM-016]]. The competing explanation is that the cells found inside tumors are the wrong ones, weakly binding (low avidity) or poorly matched, which measuring effector-to-tumor ratios and on-site function in paired biopsies would separate [[INF-IMMUNE-01]].

topics.clinical_status: No engineered T-cell product is FDA-approved for pancreatic cancer, or for any indication in the case of mesothelin CAR-T, as of 8 Oct 2026. KRAS G12D-directed receptor gene therapy was given under single-patient investigational applications and requires both the KRAS G12D mutation and the HLA-C*08:02 tissue type. Claudin-18.2 CAR-T (satricabtagene autoleucel) was approved by China's national regulator in June 2026 for claudin-18.2-positive, HER2-negative advanced gastric or gastro-esophageal junction cancer after at least two prior lines; that approval does not cover pancreatic cancer and there is no US approval. Access is through clinical trials only.

glossary.definition: The natural receptor a T cell uses to read short protein fragments displayed by a tissue-type molecule on another cell's surface.
An artificial receptor that joins an antibody-like gripping part to T-cell signaling parts, so the cell can attack a surface protein without needing a tissue-type molecule.
The tissue-type molecules that hold up protein fragments from inside a cell so T cells can inspect them; people carry different versions.
The loss of one of the two inherited copies of a stretch of chromosome, which can delete the exact tissue-type molecule a therapy depends on.
A systemic inflammatory reaction, with fever and low blood pressure, caused by large numbers of immune cells activating at once.
Chemotherapy given before an infusion of engineered cells to clear space for them, which predictably lowers blood counts.
The amount of tumor taking up radioactive sugar on a PET scan, which can fall before any change in size is visible.

related.statement: Engineered T-cell therapy replaces the T cell's own target recognition with a transferred receptor, bypassing the need for the patient's immune system to find the tumor by itself.
A transferred T-cell receptor still depends on the tumor displaying its target through HLA, whereas a chimeric antigen receptor does not, which is why the two designs fail in different ways.
Mutant KRAS is the target of the receptor-engineered cells that produced the one dramatic pancreatic response, which required the patient to carry the HLA-C*08:02 tissue type as well.
Eligibility for KRAS-directed cell therapy depends on testing both the tumor's KRAS variant and the patient's HLA type, since the therapy only works when both match.
Lymph-node-targeted vaccination, the delivery idea behind the KRAS peptide vaccines, eradicated established mouse tumors when used to re-stimulate transferred receptor-engineered T cells.
No engineered T-cell product is approved for pancreatic cancer, so the published pancreatic experience comes from phase 1 trials and single-patient authorizations.

faq.q: CAR-T cured people with leukemia. Why not pancreatic cancer?
faq.a: In pancreatic cancer the mesothelin CAR-T experience gave no objective responses in six patients, and the first solid-tumor CAR-T approval anywhere covers gastric cancer, not pancreatic [[IMM-015]][[SEC-IMMUNE-07]]. The obstacle appears to sit after recognition: cells have been present, persisting and inside the tumor while it grew [[IMM-006]].

faq.q: One patient had a 72 percent response. Could that work for me?
faq.a: Only if your tumor carries KRAS G12D and you carry the HLA-C*08:02 tissue type, a combination present in a small minority, and even then the published experience is two patients with opposite outcomes [[IMM-006]]. A molecular report and HLA typing are what would answer the first part of the question.

faq.q: What side effects do these treatments cause?
faq.a: Cytokine release syndrome and neurological toxicity occurred at grade 3 and grade 2 in the second receptor-therapy patient [[IMM-006]]. With CAR-T the preconditioning chemotherapy is the dominant harm: grade 3 or 4 lymphopenia in all 37 patients in one trial, neutropenia in 68 percent, and one case of grade 4 gut bleeding as a tumor shrank [[IMM-008]].

topics.title: Immune combinations: checkpoint, CD40, chemokine blockers
topics.orientation: If one immune drug does nothing in pancreatic cancer, the reasoning runs, the tumor must be holding T cells back by more than one route, so block several at once. This entry covers what has actually been tried in people, checkpoint antibodies with chemotherapy, CD40 agonists, chemokine and macrophage blockers and an oncolytic (cancer-infecting) virus, and what each attempt established.

section1.label: What it does
section1.preview: Each component removes a different brake. Checkpoint antibodies block PD-1, PD-L1 or CTLA-4, the switches that shut an activated T cell down. CXCR4 and CCR2 blockers interrupt the chemical trails that draw suppressive myeloid cells (immature bone-marrow-derived immune cells) into the tumor and hold them there. A CD40 agonist does the opposite of blocking: it pushes the licensing signal that antigen-presenting cells need before they can start a response.
section1.full: In patients, these drugs have done what their mechanisms predict. The CXCR4 antagonist motixafortide, assessed in paired biopsies, increased infiltration by CD8 (killer) effector T cells into the tumor and reduced myeloid-derived suppressor cells [[IMM-010]]. The CCR2 inhibitor PF-04136309 held inflammatory monocytes, the precursors of tumor macrophages, back in the bone marrow, shifting the bone-marrow-to-blood monocyte ratio against a concurrent chemotherapy-only group at P=0.0006 [[IMM-017]]. An antibody blocking CSF1R, a survival signal for macrophages, given with a vaccine and pembrolizumab met a prespecified immune endpoint: 5 of 8 patients had a more than 80 percent rise in CD8 T cells inside the tumor between the pretreatment biopsy and the resected specimen, four of them with a matching rise in granzyme B, the enzyme killer cells use [[IMM-018]]. The oncolytic virus pelareorep, given into a vein, was recovered replicating inside tumor tissue on an on-treatment biopsy [[IMM-019]]. The boundary observation comes from the same CSF1R study, which recorded a significant rise in suppressive regulatory T cells in those identical specimens [[IMM-018]]. Each of these is a demonstration that the drug reached its target and changed the tumor's immune makeup.

section2.label: Why it matters here
section2.preview: None of those changes has lengthened survival. Adding durvalumab and tremelimumab to gemcitabine and nab-paclitaxel in 180 patients gave median survival of 9.8 against 8.8 months, a hazard ratio of 0.94. The reason sits in the same trial's sequencing: 172 of 173 tumors were microsatellite stable (lacking the DNA-repair defect that checkpoint drugs need), and mutation load never came near the level that predicts checkpoint benefit in other cancers.
section2.full: Median blood tumor mutational burden was 3.7 mutations per megabase (million DNA letters) with a maximum of 11.2, and exactly one patient in 173 was microsatellite-instability-high [[IMM-007]]. That patient is the exception defining the rule. Pembrolizumab is approved in the US on a tissue-agnostic basis for mismatch-repair-deficient or MSI-high tumors that have progressed after prior treatment, and pancreatic cancer falls inside that indication, but the defect was present in 7 of 833 consecutive pancreatic cancers, 0.8 percent, all of them in people with Lynch syndrome [[IMM-020]][[SEC-TME-02]]. Where it is present the difference is large: in a real-world series of nine patients found by blood testing, seven responded and six of those seven were still responding at a median of 21 months [[IMM-021]]. For everyone else the combinations fail in a consistent pattern. The randomized PRINCE trial met its one-year survival target only in the chemotherapy-plus-nivolumab arm at 57.7 percent; adding the CD40 agonist sotigalimab gave 48.1 percent and the three-drug combination 41.3 percent, neither meeting the target, against the trial's own synthetic control estimate (a benchmark built from earlier data) of 45 percent for chemotherapy alone [[TME-024]]. Stripped of chemotherapy, CXCR4 blockade plus pembrolizumab produced 1 objective response in 37 patients [[IMM-010]].

research_notes.what_findings_mean: The repeated shape of these results is an early signal that shrinks as the data complete. The CXCR4-plus-pembrolizumab-plus-chemotherapy cohort was published with an interim response rate of 32 percent at 22 patients; the final posted registry result at 43 patients was 8 responses, 18.6 percent, with median survival 6.6 months, within the range chemotherapy alone produces [[IMM-010]][[SEC-IMMUNE-03]]. The CCR2 result has the same character: a 48.5 percent partial response rate against a prespecified 25 percent benchmark, but non-randomized, 33 evaluable patients, a single center, and a concurrent comparison group of only five, in a setting where FOLFIRINOX alone produces high response rates [[IMM-017]]. The oncolytic-virus trial showed one response lasting 17.4 months alongside a median survival of 3.1 months [[IMM-019]].
research_notes.how_studied: Two different kinds of endpoint are in play and they come apart here. Pharmacodynamic endpoints, measured in paired biopsies, bone marrow and blood, establish that a drug engaged its target: cell counts before and after, with a prespecified threshold in the CSF1R study [[IMM-018]][[IMM-017]][[IMM-010]]. Clinical endpoints need a comparison group. The PA.7 trial randomized 180 patients with survival as the primary endpoint and sequenced circulating tumor DNA in 173 of them, which is why its negative result comes with the quantitative explanation attached [[IMM-007]]. The PRINCE trial randomized across three experimental arms but used a historical benchmark rather than a concurrent chemotherapy arm, so it can exclude a large CD40 effect while leaving each arm's absolute benefit uncertain [[TME-024]].

mechanism_notes.text: The pattern across these trials points to a constraint that sits downstream of everything they fix. Antigen supply, priming and trafficking were each addressed, and T cells did arrive, yet tumors did not shrink, which is consistent with too few effector cells relative to tumor burden plus active local switching-off (de-licensing) after arrival [[INF-IMMUNE-01]][[IMM-018]][[IMM-012]]. The simultaneous rise in regulatory T cells alongside CD8 cells in the same specimens is the concrete version of that second mechanism [[IMM-018]]. An alternative is that the arriving cells are simply not tumor-reactive, which paired-biopsy measurements of on-site function would distinguish [[INF-IMMUNE-01]].

topics.clinical_status: As of 8 Oct 2026 no immune combination is FDA-approved for pancreatic cancer. Pembrolizumab alone carries a tissue-agnostic US approval for unresectable or metastatic mismatch-repair-deficient or MSI-high tumors that have progressed after prior treatment, determined by an FDA-authorized test, which covers roughly 1 in 125 people with pancreatic cancer; no checkpoint inhibitor is approved for pancreatic cancer unselected by that marker. Sotigalimab, motixafortide for this use, PF-04136309, IMC-CS4 and pelareorep are all investigational; motixafortide's only US approval is for stem-cell mobilization in multiple myeloma, a different indication. Access to the combinations is through clinical trials only.

glossary.definition: An antibody that blocks a switch-off signal such as PD-1 or CTLA-4 so that T cells already recognizing the tumor stay active.
An antibody that pushes rather than blocks, delivering the activating signal antigen-presenting cells need before they can license T cells.
A receptor such as CXCR4 or CCR2 that lets an immune cell follow a chemical trail to a particular tissue.
An immature immune cell recruited by tumors that actively blocks T-cell function rather than helping it.
A T cell whose job is to restrain other T cells, useful in normal tissue and unhelpful inside a tumor.
A virus chosen or engineered to replicate inside cancer cells, killing them and alerting the immune system in the process.
A measurement showing a drug did what it was designed to do in the body, which is a separate question from whether patients lived longer.
The number of mutations per million DNA letters in a tumor, a rough measure of how foreign it may look to T cells.

related.statement: CXCR4, CCR2 and CSF1R blockers were designed to strip suppressive macrophages and monocytes out of the pancreatic tumor, and in patients they measurably did so.
Immune combinations raise the number of CD8 T cells inside pancreatic tumors, and in the same specimens they raise regulatory T cells that restrain them.
Pembrolizumab in mismatch-repair-deficient tumors is the one approved immune route in pancreatic cancer, and it is the exception these unselected combination trials run into.
Mismatch repair deficiency, present in under 1 percent of pancreatic cancers, is the molecular feature that separates the patients checkpoint blockade helps from the great majority it does not.
Immune combinations and stroma-directed drugs repeat the same pattern: a target is measurably engaged in the tumor and survival does not change.
The CXCR4 combination's fall from a 32 percent interim response rate to 18.6 percent at full accrual is a worked example of why interim numbers are not conclusions.

faq.q: Why does immunotherapy work in melanoma and lung cancer but not here?
faq.a: Partly because of how few mutations these tumors carry. In 173 sequenced metastatic pancreatic cancers the median mutation load was 3.7 per megabase (million DNA letters) with a maximum of 11.2, and one patient was MSI-high [[IMM-007]]. Checkpoint drugs release a brake on T cells that already recognize the tumor, and in most pancreatic cancers there are too few such T cells to release.

faq.q: The scan report says my tumor has more T cells in it now. Is that good news?
faq.a: It means the treatment is doing something measurable, which is worth knowing, but in these trials rises in tumor CD8 T cells have come alongside rises in suppressive regulatory T cells and no tumor shrinkage [[IMM-018]]. Immune changes inside a tumor and benefit to a person have repeatedly come apart in this disease [[IMM-012]].

faq.q: Is there any immunotherapy I should ask about?
faq.a: Testing for mismatch-repair deficiency or microsatellite instability is the question worth raising, because that result opens an approved route [[SEC-TME-02]]. It is uncommon, roughly 1 to 2 percent of pancreatic cancers, but where it is found response rates have been high and durable [[SEC-IMMUNE-10]][[IMM-021]].

topics.title: Cachexia and supportive-care research
topics.orientation: Cachexia is the wasting syndrome that strips muscle from someone with cancer even when the number on the scale holds steady, and until recently nothing available altered its biology. This entry covers the research trying to: an antibody against one specific hormone, an appetite-receptor drug, and trials of protein and exercise.

section1.label: What it does
section1.preview: Growth differentiation factor 15, or GDF-15, is a circulating protein that acts on appetite circuitry in the brainstem, the same pathway that generates nausea. Tumors push its level up. Ponsegromab is an antibody that mops it up, an attempt to cut one specific signal rather than add calories. Anamorelin works at the other end, imitating ghrelin, the hormone that signals hunger.
section1.full: The ponsegromab trial is the strongest evidence here because it was a randomized interference with one molecule. 187 patients with cancer cachexia and a serum GDF-15 of at least 1,500 picograms per milliliter, 32 percent of them with pancreatic cancer, were assigned to placebo or one of three antibody doses every four weeks for twelve weeks [[SUPP-014]]. Weight rose with dose: 1.22 kg above placebo at 100 mg, 1.92 kg at 200 mg and 2.81 kg at 400 mg, with credible intervals (the statistical range of plausible effects) excluding zero at every dose [[SUPP-014]]. Appetite and cachexia symptoms improved on a standard questionnaire, and measured activity rose at the top dose, where non-sedentary time increased by 12.1 minutes a day while falling 37.7 minutes on placebo [[SUPP-014]]. Adverse events were less frequent on the antibody than on placebo, 70 against 80 percent [[SUPP-014]]. Anamorelin, taken by mouth, raised lean body mass by 1.89 kg over twelve weeks in 50 Japanese patients with gastrointestinal cancer cachexia, though only five of them had pancreatic cancer, and treatment-related raised blood sugar and new diabetes each appeared in about 6 percent [[SUPP-022]].

section2.label: Why it matters here
section2.preview: Weight is not the measurement that predicts how someone does, and no trial of these drugs has yet reported the one that does. Muscle, not weight, carries the prognostic signal during chemotherapy: among patients whose body-mass index held steady, losing skeletal muscle still carried a hazard ratio for death of 1.50, a 50 percent higher death rate. Whether reversing that changes anything is untested.
section2.full: In a 484-patient cohort, sarcopenia (low muscle mass) at diagnosis carried an adjusted hazard ratio for death of 1.72 and muscle loss during first-line chemotherapy 1.39, while a change in body-mass index added nothing once muscle was preserved [[SUPP-003]]. The ponsegromab trial reported weight rather than body composition over twelve weeks, so whether those 2.81 kg were muscle is unknown, and survival was not an endpoint [[SUPP-014]]. The phase 3 trial that could address this is recruiting in pancreatic cancer cachexia with a planned 982 participants and has no results [[SEC-SUPP-15]]. The simpler interventions divide along an informative line. Six months of supervised progressive resistance training in 65 patients changed no CT-measured muscle or fat compartment, with all effect sizes negligible, although only 28 had paired scans [[SUPP-015]]. A blinded trial of 18 grams of extra protein daily for six weeks after pancreatic resection raised protein intake from 56.7 to 77.3 grams and improved walking speed, nutritional status and quality of life against a carbohydrate placebo [[SUPP-016]]. Exercise during preoperative treatment improved six-minute walk distance by 25.7 meters in 50 patients [[SUPP-017]].

research_notes.what_findings_mean: The exercise work has produced a tumor-level finding worth separating from the functional one. Resected tumors from patients who had exercised during preoperative therapy contained about twice the vessel density of matched historical controls, with more open, elongated vessels and no difference in fibrosis, and a parallel study found more CD8 (killer) T cells inside those tumors [[SUPP-018]][[SUPP-019]]. Both human comparisons used historical controls, so exercise and tumor response cannot be separated; the causal part of each study is in mice. Real-world anamorelin use exposes a practical limit the trial did not: 28 of 74 patients stopped within three weeks, mostly for mild adverse effects, with three cases of bowel obstruction, and the US pancreatic trial closed after enrolling four patients [[SUPP-023]][[SEC-SUPP-16]].
research_notes.how_studied: Muscle is quantified from CT scans already taken for staging, by measuring cross-sectional muscle area at the third lumbar vertebra and dividing by height squared, which is why those cut-offs are research-derived rather than clinical standards [[SUPP-003]][[SUPP-015]]. The ponsegromab trial selected patients by a blood GDF-15 threshold, which concentrates the population in whom blocking that one signal could matter and limits what the result says about everyone else [[SUPP-014]]. Function was measured by walking tests and sit-to-stand timing rather than by questionnaire alone, and activity by wearable accelerometers, which detect changes in ordinary movement that patients may not report [[SUPP-014]][[SUPP-017]].

mechanism_notes.text: Reversing cachexia may improve tumor outcomes indirectly, by restoring the physical reserve and chemotherapy tolerance that wasting erodes, so that fewer doses are reduced or delayed [[INF-SUPP-03]]. The observation behind this is that anamorelin responders had disease control on chemotherapy in 75 percent of cases against 37.5 percent in non-responders [[SUPP-023]]. The published alternative runs the other way: a tumor that is responding produces less GDF-15 and less of the inflammatory signal interleukin-6, so appetite and weight recover and the drug merely marks the responders [[INF-SUPP-03]]. Delivered chemotherapy dose intensity in the randomized phase 3 would separate them [[SEC-SUPP-15]].

topics.clinical_status: Ponsegromab is investigational in the US as of 8 Oct 2026: the phase 2 is complete with posted results, and a phase 3 in pancreatic cancer cachexia (NCT06989437, planned 982 participants) is recruiting. Anamorelin has been approved in Japan since 2021 for cachexia in gastrointestinal and lung cancers but is not FDA-approved, is not recommended by the US cachexia guideline on that basis, and the US pancreatic trial closed after enrolling four patients. Dietary counseling, oral nutrition supplements and exercise are standard supportive care rather than regulated products; the US guideline advises against routine tube or intravenous feeding in advanced cancer and offers short-term progestins, corticosteroids or low-dose olanzapine for appetite.

glossary.definition: A wasting syndrome driven by the illness itself, in which muscle is broken down faster than eating can replace it.
Muscle mass below a defined threshold for a person's sex and height, measured here from a single CT slice at the lower back.
A protein released in large amounts by some tumors that acts on brainstem appetite circuits to suppress eating.
The hormone released by an empty stomach that signals hunger and promotes muscle building.
Everything in the body that is not fat, used as a stand-in for muscle in cachexia trials.
Building up strength and walking capacity during the treatment that precedes surgery, rather than waiting until afterwards to rehabilitate.
The Bayesian equivalent of a confidence interval: the range in which the true effect most plausibly lies given the data.

related.statement: Cachexia research targets the biology behind the weight and muscle loss that this symptom entry describes from the patient's side.
The investigational agents here sit alongside the appetite and nutrition measures currently available, none of which reverses muscle loss.
A blinded trial of 18 grams of daily protein after pancreatic resection improved walking speed and quality of life, which is why dietitian involvement is standard rather than optional.
Exercise during preoperative treatment improved walking distance in 50 patients, and in resected specimens was associated with denser tumor blood vessels and more CD8 T cells.
Exercise acts through an interleukin-15 pathway that mobilizes CD8 T cells into pancreatic tumors in mice, with more CD8 cells seen in tumors from patients who exercised.
Anamorelin raises blood sugar and caused new diabetes in about 6 percent of trial patients, which matters in a disease where diabetes is already common.

faq.q: Is there a drug for cachexia yet?
faq.a: Not an approved one in the US. The anti-GDF-15 antibody ponsegromab produced up to 2.81 kg of weight gain over twelve weeks in a randomized phase 2 and is now in a phase 3 specifically in pancreatic cancer cachexia, with no results [[SUPP-014]][[SEC-SUPP-15]]. Anamorelin is approved in Japan but not in the US [[SUPP-022]]. The current US guidance is dietary counseling for everyone, with short-term progestins, corticosteroids or low-dose olanzapine as appetite options and no routine tube or intravenous feeding in advanced cancer [[SEC-SUPP-05]].

faq.q: My weight is stable, so is the muscle loss still a problem?
faq.a: Yes, and that is the main finding of this work. Among patients whose body-mass index held steady, losing skeletal muscle still predicted shorter survival, with a hazard ratio of 1.50, whereas weight change carried no information once muscle was maintained [[SUPP-003]].

faq.q: Will lifting weights rebuild the muscle?
faq.a: Resistance training alone did not change CT-measured muscle over six months in a randomized trial, though it did improve strength and the paired-scan group was small [[SUPP-015]]. Adding protein worked better on function: 18 grams a day after surgery improved walking speed and quality of life against placebo [[SUPP-016]].

topics.title: Reprogramming rather than removing the stroma
topics.orientation: Pancreatic tumors sit inside dense fibrous tissue, and for roughly a decade the plan was to dissolve it. That approach failed in mice and in people, sometimes harmfully. The newer idea is to change what those cells are doing rather than remove them, or to remove only the subset that helps the cancer, and all of it is still preclinical.

section1.label: What it does
section1.preview: The fibroblasts in a pancreatic tumor, the connective-tissue cells that build its scar, are not one population. Some suppress T cells and support growth; others hold the cancer back. Reprogramming means pushing the harmful ones toward a resting state and leaving the rest alone, while subtype-selective depletion means killing only the harmful ones. Both depend on being able to tell them apart, which is a recent ability.
section1.full: Two markers made that distinction practical. CD105, a co-receptor for the fibroblast-activating signal TGF-beta, cleanly separated two stable fibroblast lineages in all 19 mouse tumors examined and in most normal and tumor tissues of both mouse and human, in roughly a 7-to-3 ratio [[TME-036]]. Transplanted at matched doses alongside cancer cells, CD105-negative fibroblasts strongly restricted tumor growth while CD105-positive fibroblasts permitted it; crucially, the restriction vanished entirely in mice lacking T and B cells and was blunted in mice lacking type 1 dendritic cells, so the protective fibroblasts work through the immune system rather than by walling the tumor in [[TME-036]]. LRRC15 marks the other side of the split. Selectively killing LRRC15-positive myofibroblasts in mice slowed tumor growth, relieved direct suppression of CD8 T cells and improved the response to the checkpoint antibody anti-PD-L1, while deleting the TGF-beta receptor in resident fibroblasts showed where those cells come from in the first place [[TME-037]]. Reprogramming has its own proof of principle: the vitamin D analog calcipotriol returned stellate cells (the pancreas's resting fibroblast-like cells) toward quiescence, raised both gemcitabine levels inside the tumor and vessel patency (the share of open blood vessels), and extended median survival in mice from 14 to 22 days, with no effect at all when given alone [[TME-038]].

section2.label: Why it matters here
section2.preview: This distinction matters because the opposite approach actively harmed animals, and what separates the two is which cells were hit. Deleting the hedgehog signal (a growth pathway that builds the stroma) or killing myofibroblasts wholesale shortened survival and increased spread. The conclusion is not that the tissue around the tumor is unimportant, but that it contains cells pulling in both directions, so a drug clearing both at once can make things worse.
section2.full: Deleting the hedgehog ligand shortened median survival from 6.17 to 3.61 months and raised metastasis from 15.3 to 43.4 percent, while chronic inhibition of Smoothened, the hedgehog pathway's receptor, shortened it from 156 to 121 days [[TME-002]]. Ablating about 80 percent of myofibroblasts shortened survival at two different disease stages, markedly increased hypoxia (oxygen shortage) and expanded regulatory T cells, and the survival deficit was reversed by the checkpoint antibody anti-CTLA-4, which points to an immune mechanism rather than a mechanical one [[TME-012]]. A fibroblast-targeting trial in patients was itself terminated for disease acceleration [[SEC-TME-07]]. Nothing in the reprogramming literature has yet reached people. The closest human data concern losartan, a blood-pressure drug thought to lower matrix content and tissue pressure: added to total neoadjuvant FOLFIRINOX and chemoradiotherapy in 49 patients with locally advanced disease, it accompanied a margin-negative resection rate reported as 61 to 69 percent and a median overall survival of 31.4 months [[TME-016]]. There was no control arm, three patients stopped losartan for intolerance, and no on-treatment measurement of stiffness, perfusion or matrix content was made, so the chemotherapy, the radiotherapy and selection at a high-volume center could account for all of it [[TME-016]].

research_notes.what_findings_mean: The direction-reversing results are not in conflict once the target is specified. Depleting fibroblasts that express the surface enzyme FAP, combined with anti-PD-L1, nearly eliminated malignant cells in mice, the opposite sign from bulk myofibroblast ablation [[TME-019]][[TME-012]]. The human relevance of the markers is weaker than the mouse biology: LRRC15 entered the field as a gene-expression signature associated with failure to respond to anti-PD-L1 in patients, and the causal test that followed was in mice [[SEC-TME-06]][[TME-037]]. The CD105 work is largely subcutaneous (tumors implanted under the skin) rather than orthotopic (in the pancreas), and the human component is marker presence rather than function [[TME-036]]. No stroma-directed therapy of any kind is approved for pancreatic cancer.
research_notes.how_studied: These are genetic experiments rather than drug trials, which is what gives them their precision. A diphtheria-toxin receptor knocked into the LRRC15 gene lets one cell type be killed on command, and a tamoxifen-switchable deletion of the TGF-beta receptor in resident fibroblasts shows which upstream signal creates them [[TME-037]]. The CD105 work uses the cleanest available design for direction of effect: two prospectively sorted lineages transplanted at identical doses into four host genotypes, so that losing the effect in immunodeficient mice identifies the mechanism as immune [[TME-036]]. Each design also carries its limits: implanted rather than spontaneous tumors, growth rather than survival endpoints, and LRRC15 depletion that also cut total fibroblast content by about 70 percent [[TME-037]].

mechanism_notes.text: The sign of any stromal intervention may be set by the resulting ratio of suppressive to restraining fibroblast states rather than by how much stroma is removed. Tools acting on the restraining population, hedgehog inhibition, myofibroblast ablation, collagen deletion, shift the balance toward suppression and shorten survival, while tools acting on the suppressive population or converting cells to a quiescent state shift it the other way [[INF-TME-01]][[TME-036]][[TME-037]][[TME-038]]. The competing account is timing rather than composition: the harmful experiments all perturbed the stroma from the precursor stage onward [[INF-TME-01]][[TME-002]][[TME-012]].

topics.clinical_status: No stroma-directed therapy is approved for pancreatic cancer in the US as of 8 Oct 2026. Subtype-selective fibroblast depletion and vitamin D analog reprogramming are preclinical: LRRC15-directed agents are investigational, and vitamin D analogs are not approved as pancreatic cancer therapy. Losartan is approved for high blood pressure and for no cancer indication; its only pancreatic evidence is one single-arm phase 2. Hedgehog inhibitors are approved for basal cell carcinoma only, and the pancreatic program was abandoned. Pegvorhyaluronidase alfa failed its confirmatory phase 3 survival endpoint.

glossary.definition: The non-cancer tissue woven through a tumor: fibroblasts, matrix proteins, blood vessels and immune cells.
A connective-tissue cell within a tumor that has changed state, producing matrix and signals that can either help or restrain the cancer.
The resting fibroblast-like cell of the pancreas that stores fat droplets and becomes activated into a matrix-producing cell by injury or cancer.
The resting, non-activated state a cell can be pushed back into instead of being killed.
A contractile, matrix-producing fibroblast state, identified in these studies by markers such as alpha-smooth-muscle actin or LRRC15.
The antigen-presenting cell that starts CD8 T-cell responses, and without which the protective fibroblast effect disappears.
A study in which everyone receives the treatment, so an encouraging result cannot be attributed to any one component of it.
An operation after which no cancer is seen at the cut edges of the specimen, which lowers but does not eliminate the chance of recurrence.

related.statement: Reprogramming strategies act on the fibroblast states this entry describes, pushing suppressive ones toward rest rather than clearing the whole population.
Reprogramming treats desmoplasia (the dense scar around the tumor) as a composition problem rather than as excess tissue to be dissolved, because clearing it wholesale shortened survival in mice.
The failures of hedgehog inhibition and bulk fibroblast depletion are the lessons that reprogramming and subtype-selective depletion were designed around.
Losartan was added to neoadjuvant chemotherapy on the premise that reducing matrix and tissue pressure improves drug delivery, a premise the trial did not measure.
LRRC15-positive myofibroblasts directly suppress CD8 T-cell function in mice, and removing them improved the response to checkpoint blockade.
Returning stellate cells toward quiescence raised vessel patency and intratumoral chemotherapy levels in mice, whereas depleting myofibroblasts markedly increased hypoxia.
Subtype-selective fibroblast depletion improved anti-PD-L1 response in mice, which is the preclinical rationale behind pairing stroma-directed and immune drugs.

faq.q: Can the scar tissue around the tumor be broken down so chemotherapy gets in?
faq.a: That was tried and it did not work out as expected. In mice, reducing hedgehog-driven stroma shortened survival and nearly tripled metastasis, and depleting myofibroblasts shortened survival and expanded suppressive T cells [[TME-002]][[TME-012]]. The tissue contains cells that restrain the cancer as well as cells that help it, and clearing both at once removed the restraint.

faq.q: Should I take vitamin D, or ask about losartan?
faq.a: Neither has shown benefit in pancreatic cancer. The vitamin D analog result is a mouse survival gain of 14 to 22 days that required chemotherapy alongside it, with no effect alone [[TME-038]]. Losartan's pancreatic evidence is one single-arm trial of 49 patients that could not separate the drug from the chemotherapy and selection [[TME-016]].

faq.q: Is any stroma-directed treatment available?
faq.a: No stroma-directed therapy is approved for pancreatic cancer. Hedgehog inhibitors are approved only for a skin cancer, the stroma-dissolving hyaluronidase enzyme failed its confirmatory phase 3 survival endpoint, and the subtype-selective approaches have not been tested in people [[TME-037]][[TME-036]].

topics.title: What would count as progress
topics.orientation: News about pancreatic cancer arrives as announcements: a trial has opened, a drug has received a designation, an early result looked encouraging. Deciding whether any of it is progress means asking a few specific questions about what has been measured, in whom, and against what.

section1.label: What this means
section1.preview: A trial's registry entry and a trial's result are two different objects. Registration records that a study exists, how it is designed and whether it is enrolling; results exist only once the registry posts them or a journal publishes them. A study can be recruiting for years, or finished, with nothing yet known about whether the treatment works. The first question is which of the two an announcement describes.
section1.full: Registry status words describe enrollment, not outcome, and the distance between the two can be long: the adjuvant trial of daraxonrasib lists primary completion in 2029 [[SEC-RAS-07]], and the randomized test of a personalized mRNA vaccine lists 2031 while already closed to new patients [[SEC-IMMUNE-01]]. The records can come apart the other way too. The trial behind a 2026 approval still showed no posted registry results [[SEC-RAS-05]], and several landmark pancreatic trials published in journals never posted results to the registry at all [[SEC-TX-14]]. The second question is what a result was compared against. A single-arm study compares its patients with expectation, so it cannot separate the drug from the kind of patient who enrolled; a randomized trial compares them with a control group assembled at the same time by the same rules.

section2.label: In pancreatic cancer
section2.preview: Pancreatic cancer has an unusual number of results that shrank when they finally met a control group, and the shrinkage has a repeated shape: an encouraging number from a small, interim or hand-picked dataset, then nothing once the comparison is made. A convincing result looks different. It moves tumor response, time without progression and survival in the same direction at once.
section2.full: A CXCR4 antagonist (an immune-cell trafficking blocker) with the checkpoint drug pembrolizumab reported a 32% response rate at interim and 8 of 43 (18.6%) at full accrual [[IMM-010]]. A vaccine program built on a subgroup from an earlier phase 2, a choice its authors later called a design error, gave median survival of 3.7 against 4.6 months with chemotherapy in 303 randomized patients, a hazard ratio of 1.17 pointing the wrong way [[IMM-005]]. Response rates can rise while survival does not: the stroma-dissolving enzyme hyaluronidase lifted response from 36% to 47% while the hazard ratio for death came out at 1.00, meaning no difference at all [[TME-004]], and hydroxychloroquine, a malaria drug tested against the tumor's recycling machinery, from 21.1% to 38.2% with 12-month survival of 41% against 49% [[TME-027]]. Time without progression can double on its own, as with maintenance olaparib [[TX-005]]. The contrast is daraxonrasib in 500 randomized patients: survival 13.2 against 6.7 months, progression-free survival 7.2 against 3.6, response 30% against 11% [[RAS-033]].

research_notes.what_findings_mean: An immune result is not a clinical result. In one randomized phase 2, antigen-specific memory T cells expanded and entered the tumor in the same patients whose response rate was 0% in one arm and 7% in the other [[IMM-012]]. A blood immune profile measured before any treatment predicted survival equally well in the control and vaccine arms of randomized trials, with median survival of 271 against 77 days, so being a 'responder' can mark how robust someone already was rather than what a treatment did to them [[IMM-022]][[IMM-005]].
research_notes.how_studied: Judging a claim means reading three records against each other: the publication, the registry entry with its status, enrollment and posted results, and, for a marketed drug, the approval document [[SEC-RAS-05]][[SEC-RAS-06]]. Interim and final analyses of the same cohort are compared wherever both exist, which is how a response rate falling at full accrual becomes visible [[IMM-010]]. Whether an analysis was planned in advance or chosen after the data arrived is checked in the protocol, because a cut-point drawn from the same patients it then divides will divide them [[IMM-001]].

mechanism_notes.text: The within-trial finding that immune responders outlive non-responders may be generated by the disease rather than by the treatment. Residual tumor left after surgery can both suppress the immune response and cause early recurrence, which would produce a large survival split with no contribution from the vaccine [[INF-IMMUNE-02]][[IMM-022]]. A responder threshold set after the fact, using the very outcomes it is meant to predict, widens the gap further [[IMM-001]]. The two accounts can be told apart by running the identical responder split inside a control arm, which is why the randomized trial matters more than the size of the correlation [[IMM-005]].

glossary.definition: The public record of a trial's design, eligibility and enrollment status, created before the trial starts and updated as it runs.
Outcome data entered into the trial registry itself, which many published trials never provide.
A study in which everyone receives the treatment, so outcomes can only be compared with expectation rather than with a control group.
A look at a trial's data before enrollment is complete, which can give a more favorable number than the final one.
An analysis decided after the data were seen, which can find differences that a planned analysis would not.
A US regulatory status that speeds up a drug's review; it describes the process, not evidence that the drug works.

related.statement: Judging whether a result counts as progress starts with reading its endpoints, which is what the topic on treatment results sets out.
A trial's phase and registry status describe where it stands, while this topic asks whether its result changes anything.
Daraxonrasib is the pancreatic cancer result in which response, progression-free survival and overall survival moved together in a randomized trial.
Immune combination trials supply most of the pancreatic examples of early results that shrank toward nothing under randomization.
The personalized mRNA vaccine is a phase 1 result whose randomized test has no posted outcomes, which is why it is not yet progress.
The stroma-directed trials are the clearest pancreatic examples of tumor response rising while survival does not.

faq.q: A drug just received a breakthrough therapy or orphan drug designation. Is that progress?
faq.a: A designation is a regulatory process status that speeds up review; it is not a finding about whether the drug works. Designations reported for daraxonrasib in pancreatic cancer appear in trade press without confirmation from an FDA source, even though the drug's approval itself is documented [[SEC-RAS-15]][[RAS-033]].

faq.q: A trial is listed as 'active, not recruiting'. Does that mean results are close?
faq.a: Not necessarily. The randomized trial of a personalized mRNA vaccine after surgery is closed to new patients and still lists primary completion in 2031 with no posted results [[SEC-IMMUNE-01]]. The status describes enrollment, and the completion date is the first point at which the main question could be answered.

faq.q: What would a result have to show before it changed anything?
faq.a: A randomized comparison against current treatment in which the endpoints agree. In the trial that led to the 2026 approval, 500 previously treated patients had median survival of 13.2 against 6.7 months, progression-free survival of 7.2 against 3.6 months, and response rates of 30% against 11%, all favoring the same arm [[RAS-033]].
